@0xa1b2c3d4e5f60039;

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Kernel - universal kernel boundaries exposed to apps
#
# Defines what apps observe and demand of an OS kernel. The kernel is
# always backend-agnostic. A microkernel, a monolithic kernel, an exokernel,
# a sandbox runtime, a distributed-actor scheduler - any of them can satisfy
# these contracts by implementation. Smart-protocol is timeless; backends
# may change.
#
# This schema describes the EXTERNAL interface apps see. Internal kernel
# machinery (scheduling algorithm, page-table structures, ring isolation,
# interrupt dispatch) belongs to the backend, not the protocol.
#
# Improvements (audit-4):
#   - Removed local SignalKind enum; Signal.kind now uses T.SignalKind
#     from types.capnp directly (Rule 2: shared type, no duplication).
#     T.SignalKind includes child/stop/continue added in Batch 10.
#
# Improvements (audit-5):
#   - TaskFilter.name changed from bare Text to T.TaskName (Rule 2).
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

using T = import "types.capnp";
using import "capability.capnp".Operation;
using import "capability.capnp".CapabilityService;
using import "boot.capnp".Architecture;

struct TaskInfo {
    id @0 :T.ProcessId;
    parent @1 :T.ProcessId;
    name @2 :Text;
    label @3 :Text;
    state @4 :TaskState;
    priority @5 :Int8;
    capabilities @6 :List(CapId);
    children @7 :List(T.ProcessId);
    createdAt @8 :T.Timestamp;
    lastScheduled @9 :T.Timestamp;
    cpuTime @10 :T.Duration;
    memoryBytes @11 :UInt64;
}

struct CapId {
    # Reference to a capability held by container of this task.
    # Wire format is UInt64 (T.CapabilityHandle); the schema enforces type safety.
    id @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
}

enum TaskState {
    # Created, not yet run.
    newBorn @0;
    # Ready to run but not scheduled yet.
    ready @1;
    # Currently running on a compute unit.
    running @2;
    # Blocked on a resource or channel.
    waiting @3;
    # Suspended by signal.
    stopped @4;
    # Finished, awaiting cleanup.
    terminated @5;
    # Zombie: exited, awaiting parent reaping.
    zombie @6;
    custom @7;
}

struct RegionSpec {
    # Requested base address (zero = backend picks).
    base @0 :UInt64;
    # Length in bytes.
    length @1 :UInt64;
    # Permissions requested.
    perms @2 :T.MemoryPerms;
    # Optional backing-storage target id.
    backing @3 :UInt64;
    # Optional name (debugging).
    label @4 :Text;
    # Optional alignment (must be power of two, zero = default).
    alignment @5 :UInt32;
}

struct RegionInfo {
    base @0 :UInt64;
    length @1 :UInt64;
    perms @2 :T.MemoryPerms;
    label @3 :Text;
    backing @4 :UInt64;
    sharedWith @5 :List(T.ProcessId);
}

enum WaitResult {
    signalled @0;
    timedOut @1;
    cancelled @2;
    deadLine @3;
    custom @4;
}

# Typed signal kind — uses T.SignalKind from types.capnp directly.
# The shared definition includes all cross-platform signal types:
# terminate, interrupt, kill, hangUp, userDefined1-4, custom,
# child, stop, and continue. No local duplication needed.

struct Signal {
    kind @0 :T.SignalKind;
    data @1 :Data;
}

interface KernelService {
    # Task creation, replacement, and termination.
    spawn @0 (request :SpawnRequest) -> (task :T.ProcessId);
    fork @1 (request :ForkRequest) -> (task :T.ProcessId);
    exec @2 (pid :T.ProcessId, manifestBytes :Data) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    exit @3 (pid :T.ProcessId, exitStatus :T.ExitStatus) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    signal @4 (target :T.ProcessId, sig :Signal) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # Task query and observation.
    getInfo @5 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (info :TaskInfo);
    list @6 (filter :TaskFilter, page :T.Pagination) -> (tasks :List(TaskInfo));
    subscribe @7 (filter :TaskFilter) -> (subscription :TaskSubscription);
    # Deprecated: use subscription.pull() instead. Kept for backward compatibility.
    pull @8 (subscription :TaskSubscription) -> (events :List(TaskEvent));

    # Address space regions (memory abstraction, backend-decided granularity).
    mapRegion @9 (pid :T.ProcessId, spec :RegionSpec) -> (info :RegionInfo);
    unmapRegion @10 (pid :T.ProcessId, base :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    protectRegion @11 (pid :T.ProcessId, base :UInt64, perms :T.MemoryPerms) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    shareRegion @12 (pid :T.ProcessId, base :UInt64, shareWith :T.ProcessId, perms :T.MemoryPerms) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    listRegions @13 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (regions :List(RegionInfo));

    # Synchronization primitives (kernel-level, backend-decided).
    wait @14 (filter :WaitableFilter, timeout :T.Duration) -> (result :WaitResult);
    notify @15 (filter :WaitableFilter, sig :Signal) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # Authority / boundary primitives.
    # Wire format for all capabilities is T.CapabilityHandle (UInt64).
    # The kernel maps this to its internal capability representation (kobject, cslot, etc.).
    issueCapability @16 (request :IssueCapRequest) -> (handle :T.CapabilityHandle);
    publishCapability @17 (cap :T.CapabilityHandle, recipient :T.ProcessId) -> (result :T.BoolResult);
    enterNamespace @18 (cap :T.CapabilityHandle) -> (result :T.BoolResult);

    # Sub-services exposed (these are *not* the capability service; they're the variants).
    capabilities @19 () -> (service :CapabilityService);

    # Audit-7: kernel info and extension management.
    getKernelInfo @20 () -> (info :KernelTypeInfo);
    listKernelInstances @21 (page :T.Pagination) -> (instances :List(KernelInstanceInfo), total :UInt32);
    installExtension @22 (extension :KernelExtension) -> T.VoidResult;
    removeExtension @23 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listExtensions @24 (page :T.Pagination) -> (extensions :List(KernelExtension), total :UInt32);

    # Audit-9: subscribe to container process events.
    subscribeContainerEvents @25 () -> (subscription :ContainerEventSubscription);

    # Audit-9: join the kernel mesh network.
    joinMesh @26 (node :KernelNode) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Audit-9: leave the kernel mesh network.
    leaveMesh @27 (nodeId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Audit-9: delegate a capability grant from one process to another.
    delegateCapability @28 (grant :CapabilityGrant, delegateTo :T.ProcessId, subset :List(CapOperation)) -> (delegated :CapabilityGrant);

    # Audit-9: query kernel internals for debugging.
    introspect @29 (request :KernelIntrospectionRequest) -> (result :KernelIntrospectionResult);

    # Stage a userland image into a process address space.
    stage @30 (targetPid :T.ProcessId, image :T.UserlandImage) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Replace a process image with a new one.
    replace @31 (targetPid :T.ProcessId, image :T.UserlandImage, args :List(Text)) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Enter userspace (set CR3/RSP/RIP, switch to ring 3).
    enterUserspace @32 (targetPid :T.ProcessId) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Read the entry context for a process.
    readEntryContext @33 (targetPid :T.ProcessId) -> (ctx :T.EntryContext);

    # Set isolation scope for a process.
    setQuarantine @34 (targetPid :T.ProcessId, scope :T.IsolatedScope) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Cross isolation barrier (requires explicit capability).
    crossIsolationBarrier @35 (fromPid :T.ProcessId, toPid :T.ProcessId, cap :T.CapabilityHandle) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Audit-5: Hardware Foundation Methods

    # Memory management
    allocPhysicalPage @36 () -> (phys :UInt64);
    freePhysicalPage @37 (phys :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # MMIO mapping
    mapMmio @38 (phys :UInt64, size :UInt64, flags :UInt32) -> (virt :UInt64, handle :UInt64);
    unmapMmio @39 (handle :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # Page tables
    createAddressSpace @40 (levels :UInt8, mode :UInt8) -> (asid :UInt64);
    destroyAddressSpace @41 (asid :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    mapVirtual @42 (asid :UInt64, virt :UInt64, phys :UInt64, flags :UInt32) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    unmapVirtual @43 (asid :UInt64, virt :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    switchAddressSpace @44 (asid :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # Port I/O pass-through
    inb @45 (port :UInt16) -> (val :UInt8);
    outb @46 (port :UInt16, val :UInt8) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    inw @47 (port :UInt16) -> (val :UInt16);
    outw @48 (port :UInt16, val :UInt16) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    inl @49 (port :UInt16) -> (val :UInt32);
    outl @50 (port :UInt16, val :UInt32) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # Interrupts
    registerIrq @51 (vector :UInt8, mode :UInt8) -> (handle :UInt64);
    unregisterIrq @52 (handle :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    enableIrq @53 (vector :UInt8) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    disableIrq @54 (vector :UInt8) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    ackIrq @55 (vector :UInt8) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # MSI/MSI-X
    allocMsi @56 (deviceId :UInt64, count :UInt8) -> (vectors :List(UInt8), handle :UInt64);
    allocMsix @57 (deviceId :UInt64, count :UInt16) -> (vectors :List(UInt8), handle :UInt64);
    freeMsi @58 (handle :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    programMsi @59 (handle :UInt64, affinity :UInt32) -> (result :T.VoidResult);

    # Respawn
    registerDeviceRespawn @60 (deviceId :UInt64, policy :UInt8, maxAttempts :UInt32) -> (handle :UInt64);
    reportDeviceFailure @61 (deviceId :UInt64, report :Data) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    getDeviceRespawnStatus @62 (deviceId :UInt64) -> (state :UInt8, attempts :UInt32, fallbackActive :Bool);

    # Watchdog
    registerWatchdog @63 (timeoutNs :UInt64) -> (handle :UInt64);
    unregisterWatchdog @64 (handle :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    petWatchdog @65 (handle :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
}

struct SpawnRequest {
    label @0 :Text;
    manifestBytes @1 :Data;
    args @2 :List(Text);
    env @3 :T.StringMap;
    workingDir @4 :Text;
    requestedCaps @5 :List(IssueCapRequest);
    priorityHint @6 :Int8;
}

# Typed fork flags — replaces Linux CLONE_* string lists.
enum ForkFlag {
    shareMemory @0;
    shareFiles @1;
    shareSignal @2;
    shareCwd @3;
    shareIpc @4;
    custom @5;
}

struct ForkRequest {
    parent @0 :T.ProcessId;
    flags @1 :List(ForkFlag);
}

struct TaskFilter {
    name @0 :T.TaskName;
    state @1 :TaskState;
    userspace @2 :Bool = true;
}

struct WaitableFilter {
    # Free-form topic for the waitable.
    topic @0 :Text;
}

struct IssueCapRequest {
    target @0 :Text;
    operations @1 :List(Operation);
    recipient @2 :T.ProcessId;
    expiry @3 :T.Duration;
}

struct TaskEvent {
    union {
        started @0 :TaskInfo;
        exited @1 :ExitedTask;
        stopped @2 :TaskInfo;
        resumed @3 :TaskInfo;
        signaled @4 :SignaledTask;
    }
}

struct ExitedTask {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    exitStatus @1 :T.ExitStatus;
    reason @2 :T.Error;
}

struct SignaledTask {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    signal @1 :Signal;
}

interface TaskSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(TaskEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Audit-7: Extended kernel types
#
# Kernel type detection, container kernel access, WASM kernel,
# unikernel host call, kernel mesh, extension contracts, and
# capability kernel (seL4-style). These extend the microkernel
# model to support diverse kernel architectures.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Kernel Type Detection ─────────────────────────────────────

enum KernelType {
    microkernel @0;
    monolithic @1;
    exokernel @2;
    unikernel @3;
    hybrid @4;
    nanokernel @5;
    library @6;          # Library OS
    distributed @7;
    custom @8;
}

struct KernelTypeInfo {
    type @0 :KernelType;
    name @1 :Text;
    version @2 :T.Version;
    # CPU architecture (e.g., "x86_64", "aarch64", "riscv64").
    architecture @3 :Text;
    capabilities @4 :List(KernelCapability);
    extensions @5 :List(KernelExtension);
    metadata @6 :List(T.Meta);
}

enum KernelCapability {
    processManagement @0;
    memoryManagement @1;
    ipc @2;
    scheduling @3;
    interrupts @4;
    dma @5;
    extensions @6;
    containers @7;
    wasm @8;
    unikernel @9;
    mesh @10;
    capabilities @11;
    other @12;
}

# ── Container Kernel Access ───────────────────────────────────

struct ContainerKernelInfo {
    runtime @0 :Text;
    isolation @1 :T.IsolatedScope;
    rootless @2 :Bool;
    userlandIsolation @3 :Bool;
}

# ── Unikernel Host Call ───────────────────────────────────────

struct UnikernelInfo {
    # Unikernel runtime identifier (e.g., "mirage", "includeos", "nanos").
    runtime @0 :Text;
    singleAddress @1 :Bool;     # Single address space
    directHardware @2 :Bool;    # Direct hardware access
    minimal @3 :Bool;           # Minimal footprint
    bootTime @4 :T.Duration;    # Measured boot time
    memorySize @5 :UInt64;      # Memory footprint in bytes
}

# ── Kernel Mesh (Distributed) ─────────────────────────────────

struct KernelMeshInfo {
    nodes @0 :List(KernelNode);
    topology @1 :MeshTopology;
    synchronization @2 :MeshSync;
    # Whether the mesh handles network partitions gracefully.
    partition @3 :Bool;
}

struct KernelNode {
    id @0 :Text;
    address @1 :Text;
    kernel @2 :KernelTypeInfo;
    latency @3 :T.Duration;
    status @4 :NodeStatus;
}

enum NodeStatus {
    online @0;
    offline @1;
    degraded @2;
    syncing @3;
    custom @4;
}

enum MeshTopology {
    star @0;
    mesh @1;
    ring @2;
    tree @3;
    custom @4;
}

enum MeshSync {
    strong @0;          # Strong consistency
    eventual @1;        # Eventual consistency
    causal @2;          # Causal consistency
    custom @3;
}

# ── Kernel Extension Contract ─────────────────────────────────

struct KernelExtension {
    name @0 :Text;
    version @1 :T.Version;
    type @2 :ExtensionType;
    scope @3 :ExtensionScope;
    capabilities @4 :List(Text);
    author @5 :Text;
    license @6 :Text;
    metadata @7 :List(T.Meta);
}

enum ExtensionType {
    module @0;          # Loadable kernel module
    ebpf @1;            # eBPF program
    dtrace @2;          # DTrace probe
    custom @3;
}

enum ExtensionScope {
    system @0;          # System-wide
    container @1;       # Container-scoped
    process @2;         # Process-scoped
    custom @3;
}

# ── Kernel Instance Info ──────────────────────────────────────

struct KernelInstanceInfo {
    id @0 :Text;
    type @1 :KernelType;
    name @2 :Text;
    # Processes managed by this kernel instance.
    processCount @3 :UInt32;
    # Memory used by this kernel instance in bytes.
    memoryBytes @4 :UInt64;
    # Uptime of this kernel instance.
    uptime @5 :T.Duration;
    status @6 :NodeStatus;
}

# ── Capability Kernel (seL4-style) ────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityKernelInfo {
    # Whether the kernel has been formally verified.
    formalVerification @0 :Bool;
    # Thread control block count.
    tcb @1 :UInt32;
    # Capability slot count.
    slots @2 :UInt32;
    # Scheduling domain count.
    domains @3 :UInt32;
    # Mixed-criticality systems support.
    mcs @4 :Bool;
    # Supported architectures.
    architectures @5 :List(Architecture);
}

struct CapabilityGrant {
    # Wire format is T.CapabilityHandle (UInt64). Kernel maps to internal representation.
    cap @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    source @1 :T.ProcessId;
    target @2 :T.ProcessId;
    operations @3 :List(CapOperation);
    rights @4 :CapRights;
    expiry @5 :T.Duration;
}

enum CapOperation {
    read @0;
    write @1;
    execute @2;
    grant @3;
    delete @4;
    custom @5;
}

struct CapRights {
    read @0 :Bool;
    write @1 :Bool;
    execute @2 :Bool;
    grant @3 :Bool;
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Audit-9: Container process events, WASM module lifecycle, kernel mesh
# orchestration, capability delegation chain, and kernel introspection.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Container Process Events ──────────────────────────────────

struct ContainerProcessEvent {
    # Container identifier.
    containerId @0 :Text;
    # Process within the container.
    processId @1 :T.ProcessId;
    # Event type.
    event @2 :ContainerProcessEventType;
    # Timestamp of the event.
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
    # Exit status (if process exited).
    exitStatus @4 :T.ExitStatus;
}

enum ContainerProcessEventType {
    created @0;
    started @1;
    exited @2;
    oomKilled @3;
    signalDelivered @4;
    custom @5;
}

interface ContainerEventSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(ContainerProcessEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Kernel Introspection ─────────────────────────────────────

struct KernelIntrospectionRequest {
    # What to introspect.
    target @0 :KernelIntrospectionTarget;
    # Specific process to query (if target is process).
    processId @1 :T.ProcessId;
    # Specific memory region to query (if target is memory).
    regionBase @2 :UInt64;
}

enum KernelIntrospectionTarget {
    # Query scheduler state.
    scheduler @0;
    # Query memory allocator state.
    memory @1;
    # Query IPC state.
    ipc @2;
    # Query process state.
    process @3;
    # Query interrupt state.
    interrupts @4;
    # Query all subsystems.
    all @5;
    custom @6;
}

struct KernelIntrospectionResult {
    # Subsystem name being introspected.
    subsystem @0 :Text;
    # Key-value pairs of introspection data.
    data @1 :T.StringMap;
    # Human-readable summary.
    summary @2 :Text;
    # Timestamp of the introspection.
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# v0.0.2 additions — SMP, IPI, per-CPU, memory sharing
#
# The kernel boundary is what apps/drivers observe. How the kernel
# schedules across CPUs and routes IPIs is backend-agnostic. The
# protocol only commits to the affordances.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── SMP Topology ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# A driver or scheduler asks "what CPUs exist?" and "what CPU am I
# on?" without learning the topology algorithm.

interface SmpService {
    # Static topology (what exists).
    getTopology @0 () -> (topology :T.SmpTopology);
    # Mask of currently-online CPUs.
    getOnlineMask @1 () -> (mask :UInt64);
    # Which CPU is the calling context running on?
    getCurrentCpu @2 () -> (cpu :T.CpuId);
    # Subscribe to topology changes (CPU hotplug, NUMA rebalance).
    subscribe @3 () -> (subscription :SmpTopologySubscription);
}

interface SmpTopologySubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(SmpTopologyEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct SmpTopologyEvent {
    at @0 :UInt64;
    union {
        cpuOnline @1 :T.CpuId;
        cpuOffline @2 :T.CpuId;
        topologyChanged @3 :Void;
        custom @4 :Void;
    }
}

# ── Inter-Processor Interrupts ────────────────────────────────
# Drivers and kernel-level schedulers send IPIs. The contract is
# opaque payload + affinity mask; the backend picks the mechanism.

interface IpiService {
    # Send an IPI to the given CPU(s). Payload is opaque bytes the
    # recipient interprets (driver-defined).
    send @0 (targetMask :UInt64, payload :Data) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    # Receive IPIs. The subscription is per-task; IPIs targeting
    # this task's registered vector are dispatched here.
    subscribe @1 (vector :UInt32) -> (subscription :IpiSubscription);
}

interface IpiSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(IpiEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct IpiEvent {
    at @0 :UInt64;
    fromCpu @1 :T.CpuId;
    vector @2 :UInt32;
    payload @3 :Data;
}

# ── Memory Sharing ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Zero-copy region sharing is a kernel affordance; the contract is
# structured (size, flags, peer handle) so backends can implement
# it any way they like.

struct ShareRequest {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    region @1 :RegionInfo;
    peer @2 :T.ProcessId;
    perms @3 :T.MemoryPerms;
}

struct ShareResult {
    # Optional: backend may rewrite the peer-side base address.
    # Original region's base on the source side is preserved.
    peerBase @0 :UInt64;
    grantedPerms @1 :T.MemoryPerms;
}

# ── Per-CPU State ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Drivers register per-CPU scratch state for the kernel to
# allocate. The kernel can reset/restore around driver restarts.

struct PerCpuState {
    handle @0 :UInt64;
    sizeBytes @1 :UInt64;
    # Backend-mediated alignment hint.
    alignment @2 :UInt32;
}

interface PerCpuService {
    allocate @0 (state :PerCpuState) -> (handle :UInt64);
    release @1 (handle :UInt64) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    get @2 (cpu :T.CpuId, handle :UInt64) -> (address :UInt64);
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Boot-Agnostic + Multi-Paradigm Additions
#
# These additions close gaps for:
# - Binary format typing (Gap A)
# - Kernel swap semantics (Gap B)
# - Typed capabilities + proof levels (Gap C)
# - A/B slot management (Gap D)
# - Formal verification artifacts (Gap F)
# - Multi-kernel coordination (Gap H)
# - Kernel envelope defaults (Gap I)
#
# Linux-compat (Gap E) is intentionally excluded.
# Linux is not a paradigm — it's one specific monolithic implementation.
# The correct abstraction is KernelType.libraryOS, not "linux compat".
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Gap A: Binary Format Typing ───────────────────────────────
# Kernels can be ELF, PE/COFF, WASM, or custom formats.
# This types the binary so bootloaders know what to load.

enum BinaryFormat {
    elf @0;
    pe @1;              # UEFI PE/COFF
    wasm @2;
    wasiSnapshot @3;
    fdtWrappedElf @4;   # ELF wrapped in device tree
    custom @5;
}

struct KernelBinaryDescriptor {
    format @0 :BinaryFormat;
    entryPoint @1 :UInt64;
    # Architecture-specific identifier (e.g., EM_X86_64 = 0x3E for ELF).
    machineId @2 :UInt16;
    # ABI identifier (e.g., "sysv", "wasi", "uefi").
    abi @3 :Text;
    # Cryptographic signature of the binary (if signed).
    signature @4 :Data;
    # Binary size in bytes.
    sizeBytes @5 :UInt64;
    # Hash of the binary (SHA-256).
    hash @6 :Data;
}

# ── Gap B: Kernel Swap Semantics ──────────────────────────────
# Supports runtime kernel envelope switching without recompilation.
# Cyber-microkernel can be replaced with seL4-style at runtime.

enum KernelMigrationStrategy {
    coldSwap @0;        # Save state, reboot into other kernel
    warmSwap @1;        # Live process migration
    hybridCoexist @2;   # Both kernels run, share capabilities
}

struct KernelSwapRequest {
    targetEnvelope @0 :KernelType;
    targetKernel @1 :KernelBinaryDescriptor;
    migrationStrategy @2 :KernelMigrationStrategy;
    # Maximum time to wait for swap completion.
    timeout @3 :T.Duration;
    # Whether to preserve process state across swap.
    preserveProcesses @4 :Bool;
}

struct KernelSwapEvent {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    sourceKernel @1 :Text;
    targetKernel @2 :Text;
    strategy @3 :KernelMigrationStrategy;
    success @4 :Bool;
    error @5 :T.Error;
    duration @6 :T.Duration;
}

interface KernelSwapSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(KernelSwapEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Gap C: Typed Capabilities + Proof Levels ──────────────────
# Capabilities are typed sets, not flat booleans.
# Proof level describes formal verification depth.

enum ProofLevel {
    unverified @0;
    tested @1;
    raceDetectorOnly @2;
    staticAnalysisOnly @3;
    formalPartial @4;
    formalComplete @5;
    formalEndToEnd @6;
}

struct KernelCapabilityTag {
    # The capability this kernel provides.
    capability @0 :KernelCapability;
    # Whether this capability is formally verified.
    verified @1 :Bool;
    # Proof level for this specific capability.
    proofLevel @2 :ProofLevel;
    # Scope of the proof (e.g., "scheduler", "ipc", "memory").
    proofScope @3 :Text;
}

struct KernelTypedCapabilities {
    # Each kernel declares its exact capability surface as tags.
    capabilityTags @0 :List(KernelCapabilityTag);
    # Overall proof level for this kernel.
    proofLevel @1 :ProofLevel;
    # Total number of formally verified capabilities.
    verifiedCount @2 :UInt32;
    # Total number of capabilities.
    totalCount @3 :UInt32;
}

# ── Gap D: A/B Slot Management ───────────────────────────────
# Kernel-side interface for active A/B slot selection during kernel-swap.

struct AbSlotInfo {
    activeSlot @0 :Text;
    secondarySlot @1 :Text;
    attemptCount @2 :UInt32;
    maxAttempts @3 :UInt32;
    # Whether the active slot has been marked successful.
    activeSuccessful @4 :Bool;
    # Timestamp of last slot update.
    lastUpdate @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Gap F: Formal Verification Artifacts ──────────────────────
# For space/military grade, the level and scope of formal proof
# must be in the schema so bootloaders can validate.

enum FormalProofScope {
    scheduler @0;
    ipc @1;
    memoryManagement @2;
    capabilityManagement @3;
    interruptHandling @4;
    dma @5;
    endToEnd @6;
    custom @7;
}

struct FormalVerificationArtifact {
    proofLevel @0 :ProofLevel;
    proofScope @1 :List(FormalProofScope);
    # Verification tool used (e.g., "Isabelle/HOL", "Coq", "seL4/SPARK").
    verifierTool @2 :Text;
    # Hash of the specification being verified.
    specHash @3 :Data;
    # Hash of the C/Rust source being verified.
    sourceHash @4 :Data;
    # Hash of the proof script.
    proofScriptHash @5 :Data;
    # When the proof was last verified.
    proofDate @6 :T.Timestamp;
    # Maximum depth of the proof tree.
    maxProofDepth @7 :UInt32;
    # Whether the proof covers all code paths.
    completeCoverage @8 :Bool;
}

# ── Gap H: Multi-Kernel Coordination ─────────────────────────
# Within a single computer, multiple kernels must coordinate.
# e.g., cyber-microkernel + capability-kernel sharing capabilities.

struct CrossKernelCapability {
    # Source kernel that created this capability.
    sourceKernel @0 :Text;
    # Target kernel that receives this capability.
    targetKernel @1 :Text;
    # The capability being shared.
    capability @2 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    # Operations the target kernel can perform.
    operations @3 :List(CapOperation);
    # Expiry for this cross-kernel capability.
    expiry @4 :T.Duration;
}

# ── Gap I: Kernel Envelope Defaults ───────────────────────────
# What capabilities a given envelope gives by default.
# Required to reason about safer vs faster envelopes.

struct KernelEnvelopeDefaults {
    # The kernel type this envelope describes.
    envelope @0 :KernelType;
    # Default capabilities granted to all processes.
    defaultCapabilities @1 :List(KernelCapability);
    # Default memory permissions for new processes.
    defaultMemoryPerms @2 :T.MemoryPerms;
    # Whether capabilities are sealed by default (microkernel = true).
    capabilitiesSealed @3 :Bool;
    # Whether processes can escape their capability set.
    capabilityEscape @4 :Bool;
    # Default isolation level.
    isolationLevel @5 :IsolationLevel;
}

enum IsolationLevel {
    none @0;            # No isolation (monolithic)
    process @1;         # Process-level isolation
    capability @2;      # Capability-based isolation
    hardware @3;        # Hardware-enforced isolation (MMU,TrustZone)
    formal @4;          # Formally verified isolation
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Extended KernelService Methods
#
# These methods are added to KernelService to support the gaps above.
# They use field numbers starting from @30 (after existing @31).
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Note: The following methods would be added to the KernelService interface.
# Since Cap'n Proto doesn't allow extending interfaces after definition,
# these are defined as separate interfaces that the kernel implements.

interface KernelSwapService {
    # Request a kernel envelope swap.
    requestSwap @0 (req :KernelSwapRequest) -> (result :T.VoidResult);
    # Get history of kernel swaps.
    getSwapHistory @1 (page :T.Pagination) -> (history :List(KernelSwapEvent));
    # Subscribe to kernel swap events.
    subscribeSwap @2 () -> (subscription :KernelSwapSubscription);
}

interface AbSlotService {
    # Get the currently active boot slot.
    getActiveSlot @0 () -> (slot :AbSlotInfo);
    # Mark the current boot as successful (resets attempt counter).
    markBootSuccessful @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
    # Set the active boot slot.
    setActiveSlot @2 (slot :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    # Get the current boot attempt count.
    getBootAttempt @3 () -> (attempts :UInt32);
}

interface MultiKernelCoordinator {
    # Request a capability from another kernel.
    requestCapability @0 (targetKernel :Text, capability :Text) -> (cap :T.CapabilityHandle);
    # Publish a capability to another kernel.
    publishCapability @1 (cap :T.CapabilityHandle, targetKernel :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    # List all active kernels on this machine.
    listActiveKernels @2 () -> (kernels :List(KernelInstanceInfo));
    # Get typed capabilities for a specific kernel.
    getKernelCapabilities @3 (kernelId :Text) -> (caps :KernelTypedCapabilities);
}

Design Principles for Every Batch
These apply to every CLI method we build:
1.No abbreviations — audio volume, not aud vol. process 1842 kill, not proc 1842 k2.No arguments = READ — battery shows battery. audio volume gets volume3.With value = WRITE — audio volume 75 sets volume4.Verb first = ACTION — window 3 close, process 1842 kill5.where = FILTER — processes where cpu > 506.watch = STREAM — watch battery, watch notifications7.@ = SELECTOR — @battery/level, @audio/volume8.Plural = LIST — windows, apps, processes9.Error output is actionable — shows what went wrong AND what to try10.JSON output always available — --json flag on everything11.Remote transparent — @server1 audio volume just works12.Structured data pipes — processes | where cpu > 50 | sort cpu desc | take 5

The Edge Cases Philosophy
Your shell isn't parsing text. It's operating on structured kernel boundaries. So edge cases are different from traditional shells:
Traditional Shell Edge Casesmart-shell Equivalentgrep fails because output format changedProtocol is versioned — schema hash detects driftPipe breaks because program segfaultsStructured pipe — if source dies, consumer gets typed errorsudo timeout mid-sessionCapability expiry — IssueCapRequest.expiry fieldSSH session drops mid-editRemote file is transparent — reconnect resumesScript runs on wrong machineSelectors are typed — @server1: is explicitLock screen blocks scriptAccessService.isLocked() — script can check firstWrong audio backend after updateImplementations swappable — protocol unchangedKernel panic during backupA/B slot management — rollback capabilityProcess signal during capability delegationTyped Signal with T.SignalKind from types.capnp

Want to pick a batch to start with? Batch 0 (Foundation) is the logical starting point — or if you want to see something dramatic fast, Batch 1 (System Core) would give you kernel info, kernel introspect, process tree, system temperature — methods no shell in history has ever had as first-class citizens.

Schema Improvements
shell.capnp (Enriched)
Your current shell schema is likely thin. The shell is the FIRST thing a user touches — it needs to be as rich as the kernel itself.
capnpcapnp@0xa1b2c3d4e5f60099;

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Shell — the universal interactive environment
#
# This is not a terminal emulator. This is the shell itself: the
# environment that interprets commands, manages state, handles
# completion, and provides the interactive experience. It is
# backend-agnostic: could run on a VT100, a graphical terminal,
# a phone screen, a spaceship console, or a voice interface.
#
# The shell IS the OS interface. Everything else is a protocol client.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Shell Instance ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface ShellService {
    # Get current shell state.
    getState @0 () -> (state :ShellState);

    # Start a new shell session.
    start @1 (config :ShellConfig) -> (session :ShellSession);

    # End the current shell session.
    end @2 (sessionId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Execute a command (from interactive or script mode).
    execute @3 (input :CommandInput) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # Execute a natural language request (AI-assisted interpretation).
    interpret @4 (request :NaturalLanguageRequest) -> (interpreted :InterpretedCommand);

    # Confirm and execute an interpreted command.
    confirmAndExecute @5 (interpreted :InterpretedCommand, confirm :Bool) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # ── Completion ─────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get completions for partial input.
    complete @6 (input :Text, cursorPosition :UInt32) -> (completions :List(Completion));

    # Get completions for a selector path.
    completeSelector @7 (selector :Text) -> (completions :List(SelectorCompletion));

    # Get completions for a specific domain.
    completeDomain @8 (domain :Text, partial :Text) -> (completions :List(DomainCompletion));

    # ── History ────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get command history.
    getHistory @9 (filter :HistoryFilter, pagination :T.Pagination)
               -> (entries :List(HistoryEntry), totalCount :UInt32);

    # Search history by pattern.
    searchHistory @10 (pattern :Text, pagination :T.Pagination)
                  -> (entries :List(HistoryEntry), totalCount :UInt32);

    # Clear history.
    clearHistory @11 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # Pin a history entry (never expires).
    pinHistoryEntry @12 (entryId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Aliases ────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Set an alias.
    setAlias @13 (name :Text, expansion :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Remove an alias.
    removeAlias @14 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List all aliases.
    listAliases @15 () -> (aliases :List(Alias));

    # ── Variables ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Set a shell variable.
    setVariable @16 (name :Text, value :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get a shell variable.
    getVariable @17 (name :Text) -> (value :Text, exists :Bool);

    # List all shell variables.
    listVariables @18 () -> (variables :List(ShellVariable));

    # ── Environment ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get environment variable.
    getEnv @19 (name :Text) -> (value :Text, exists :Bool);

    # Set environment variable.
    setEnv @20 (name :Text, value :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List all environment variables.
    listEnv @21 () -> (env :List(EnvVariable));

    # ── Jobs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List background jobs.
    listJobs @22 () -> (jobs :List(Job));

    # Bring job to foreground.
    fg @23 (jobId :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Send job to background.
    bg @24 (jobId :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Cancel a job.
    cancelJob @25 (jobId :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Wait for a job to complete.
    waitForJob @26 (jobId :UInt32, timeout :T.Duration) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # ── Undo ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Undo the last command (if reversible).
    undo @27 () -> (result :UndoResult);

    # Redo the last undone command.
    redo @28 () -> (result :UndoResult);

    # Get undo stack.
    getUndoStack @29 () -> (stack :List(UndoEntry));

    # ── Prompts ────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get the current prompt configuration.
    getPrompt @30 () -> (prompt :PromptConfig);

    # Set the prompt configuration.
    setPrompt @31 (config :PromptConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Script Mode ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Load and execute a script file.
    runScript @32 (path :Text, args :List(Text)) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # Validate a script without executing.
    validateScript @33 (path :Text) -> (errors :List(ScriptError));

    # Get script execution context.
    getScriptContext @34 () -> (context :ScriptContext);

    # ── Watchers ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List active watchers.
    listWatchers @35 () -> (watchers :List(WatcherInfo));

    # Cancel a watcher.
    cancelWatcher @36 (watcherId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Bookmarks ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Bookmark a command for quick recall.
    bookmark @37 (command :Text, label :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List bookmarks.
    listBookmarks @38 () -> (bookmarks :List(Bookmark));

    # Execute a bookmarked command.
    runBookmark @39 (bookmarkId :UInt64) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # Remove a bookmark.
    removeBookmark @40 (bookmarkId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Guided Mode (for non-technical users) ──────────────────

    # Enter guided mode (step-by-step interactive).
    enterGuidedMode @41 (domain :Text) -> (guide :GuidedSession);

    # Get the next step in a guided session.
    guideNext @42 (sessionId :UInt64) -> (step :GuidedStep);

    # Provide input for the current guided step.
    guideInput @43 (sessionId :UInt64, input :Text) -> (result :GuidedStepResult);

    # Exit guided mode.
    exitGuidedMode @44 (sessionId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Undoable Operations Registry ───────────────────────────

    # Register an undoable operation (for domain services to hook into).
    registerUndoable @45 (operation :UndoableOperation) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Check if a command is undoable.
    isUndoable @46 (command :Text) -> (undoable :Bool, description :Text);

    # ── Session Snapshots ──────────────────────────────────────

    # Save current shell state (variables, aliases, working dir, env).
    saveSnapshot @47 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Restore shell state from a snapshot.
    restoreSnapshot @48 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List available snapshots.
    listSnapshots @49 () -> (snapshots :List(ShellSnapshot));

    # Delete a snapshot.
    deleteSnapshot @50 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Shell State ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ShellState {
    sessionId @0 :UInt64;
    mode @1 :ShellMode;
    currentDirectory @2 :Text;
    lastExitCode @3 :Int32;
    lastCommand @4 :Text;
    activeJobs @5 :UInt32;
    activeWatchers @6 :UInt32;
    uptime @7 :T.Duration;
    commandCount @8 :UInt64;
    undoStackSize @9 :UInt32;
    # Current user context (for multi-user shells).
    userId @10 :Text;
    # Whether AI-assisted interpretation is enabled.
    aiAssistEnabled @11 :Bool;
    # Current shell theme.
    theme @12 :ShellTheme;
}

enum ShellMode {
    interactive @0;      # Normal interactive mode
    guided @1;           # Guided mode for non-technical users
    script @2;           # Script execution mode
    batch @3;            # Non-interactive batch mode
    remote @4;           # Remote shell session
    voice @5;            # Voice interface mode
    minimal @6;          # Minimal mode (low resources)
    custom @7;
}

# ── Shell Config ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ShellConfig {
    mode @0 :ShellMode;
    theme @1 :ShellTheme;
    historySize @2 :UInt32;
    prompt @3 :PromptConfig;
    aiAssistEnabled @4 :Bool;
    confirmDestructive @5 :Bool;       # Ask confirmation for destructive ops
    autoCorrect @6 :Bool;              # Suggest corrections for typos
    smartSuggestions @7 :Bool;         # Context-aware suggestions
    verboseErrors @8 :Bool;            # Detailed error messages
    colorOutput @9 :Bool;              # Colored output
    compactMode @10 :Bool;             # Compact output for small terminals
    # Maximum number of undo levels (0 = unlimited).
    maxUndoLevels @11 :UInt32;
    # Key binding profile.
    keybindings @12 :KeyBindingProfile;
    # Default output format.
    defaultFormat @13 :OutputFormat;
}

enum OutputFormat {
    human @0;          # Beautiful formatted output (default)
    json @1;           # JSON output
    tsv @2;            # Tab-separated values
    capnp @3;          # Raw Cap'n Proto binary
    raw @4;            # Raw text (for piping to legacy tools)
    minimal @5;        # Minimal output (values only)
    custom @6;
}

# ── Prompt ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct PromptConfig {
    # Prompt template with variables:
    # ${user}, ${hostname}, ${cwd}, ${git_branch}, ${exit_code},
    # ${battery}, ${time}, ${job_count}, ${depth}
    template @0 :Text;
    # Right-side prompt template.
    rightTemplate @1 :Text;
    # Prompt character (default: "❯").
    char @2 :Text;
    # Error prompt character (default: "✗").
    errorChar @3 :Text;
    # Whether to show git branch in prompt.
    showGit @4 :Bool;
    # Whether to show battery in prompt.
    showBattery @5 :Bool;
    # Whether to show current time.
    showTime @6 :Bool;
    # Whether to show job count when jobs > 0.
    showJobs @7 :Bool;
    # Whether to show command duration for long commands.
    showDuration @8 :Bool;
    # Minimum command duration (seconds) before showing duration.
    durationThreshold @9 :Float32;
    # Multi-line prompt (each line is a template).
    lines @10 :List(Text);
}

# ── Natural Language ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct NaturalLanguageRequest {
    text @0 :Text;
    # Context for interpretation (current directory, recent commands, etc).
    context @1 :InterpretContext;
    # Whether to auto-execute if confidence is high.
    autoExecute @2 :Bool;
    # Minimum confidence threshold for auto-execution (0.0-1.0).
    confidenceThreshold @3 :Float32;
}

struct InterpretContext {
    currentDirectory @0 :Text;
    recentCommands @1 :List(Text);
    currentDomain @2 :Text;           # What the user is currently working with
    availableApps @3 :List(Text);     # Running apps
    systemState @4 :Text;             # Brief system state summary
}

struct InterpretedCommand {
    # The interpreted command(s) to execute.
    commands @0 :List(Text);
    # Confidence level (0.0-1.0).
    confidence @1 :Float32;
    # Human-readable explanation of what will happen.
    explanation @2 :Text;
    # Whether this is a destructive operation.
    destructive @3 :Bool;
    # Which domains this touches.
    domains @4 :List(Text);
    # Whether the interpretation requires confirmation.
    requiresConfirmation @5 :Bool;
    # Alternative interpretations (if confidence is low).
    alternatives @6 :List(InterpretedCommand);
    # Undo description (how to reverse this).
    undoDescription @7 :Text;
}

# ── Command Input/Result ──────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CommandInput {
    text @0 :Text;
    # Whether this is from interactive mode.
    interactive @1 :Bool;
    # Whether to suppress confirmation prompts.
    force @2 :Bool;
    # Override output format for this command.
    format @3 :OutputFormat;
    # Input pipe data (for piped commands).
    pipeInput @4 :Data;
    # Execution timeout (0 = no timeout).
    timeout @5 :T.Duration;
}

struct CommandResult {
    # Exit code (0 = success).
    exitCode @0 :Int32;
    # Human-readable output.
    output @1 :Text;
    # Structured data output (JSON-like).
    data @2 :Data;
    # Error message (if exitCode != 0).
    error @3 :Text;
    # Suggestion for fixing the error.
    suggestion @4 :Text;
    # Duration of execution.
    duration @5 :T.Duration;
    # Whether this command is undoable.
    undoable @6 :Bool;
    # Undo command (if undoable).
    undoCommand @7 :Text;
    # Warnings (non-fatal).
    warnings @8 :List(Text);
    # Whether output was truncated.
    truncated @9 :Bool;
    # Total items available (if paginated).
    totalItems @10 :UInt32;
}

# ── Completions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Completion {
    text @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    kind @2 :CompletionKind;
    # Whether this completion requires a value after it.
    requiresValue @3 :Bool;
    # Example value if requiresValue is true.
    valueExample @4 :Text;
    # Relevance score for sorting.
    relevance @5 :Float32;
}

enum CompletionKind {
    command @0;
    domain @1;
    action @2;
    selector @3;
    file @4;
    directory @5;
    app @6;
    service @7;
    process @8;
    window @9;
    device @10;
    value @11;
    flag @12;
    alias @13;
    variable @14;
    keyword @15;
    naturalLanguage @16;
    custom @17;
}

struct SelectorCompletion {
    # The completed selector path.
    path @0 :Text;
    # Current value (if readable).
    currentValue @1 :Text;
    # Type of the value.
    valueType @2 :Text;
    # Description.
    description @3 :Text;
}

struct DomainCompletion {
    command @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    syntax @2 :Text;
    examples @3 :List(Text);
}

# ── History ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct HistoryEntry {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    command @1 :Text;
    timestamp @2 :T.Timestamp;
    exitCode @3 :Int32;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    directory @5 :Text;
    # Whether this entry is pinned.
    pinned @6 :Bool;
    # Tags for organization.
    tags @7 :List(Text);
}

struct HistoryFilter {
    pattern @0 :Text;
    exitCode @1 :Int32;             # -1 = any
    directory @2 :Text;
    since @3 :T.Timestamp;
    tags @4 :List(Text);
    pinnedOnly @5 :Bool;
}

# ── Aliases ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Alias {
    name @0 :Text;
    expansion @1 :Text;
    # Number of times used.
    useCount @2 :UInt64;
    # When created.
    createdAt @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Variables ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ShellVariable {
    name @0 :Text;
    value @1 :Text;
    # Whether this is exported to child processes.
    exported @2 :Bool;
    # Whether this is read-only.
    readOnly @3 :Bool;
    # Source (user-set, script, default).
    source @4 :Text;
}

struct EnvVariable {
    name @0 :Text;
    value @1 :Text;
    source @2 :Text;   # "system", "shell", "app"
}

# ── Jobs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Job {
    id @0 :UInt32;
    command @1 :Text;
    pid @2 :T.ProcessId;
    state @3 :JobState;
    startedAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
    # Whether the job has produced output.
    hasOutput @5 :Bool;
    # Output preview (last N lines).
    outputPreview @6 :Text;
}

enum JobState {
    running @0;
    stopped @1;
    completed @2;
    failed @3;
    cancelled @4;
}

# ── Undo ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct UndoResult {
    success @0 :Bool;
    description @1 :Text;     # What was undone/redone
    command @2 :Text;         # The command that was undone
    error @3 :Text;
}

struct UndoEntry {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    command @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
    # What domain this affected.
    domain @4 :Text;
    # Whether this can be undone.
    undoable @5 :Bool;
    # The reverse operation.
    reverseCommand @6 :Text;
}

struct UndoableOperation {
    command @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    domain @2 :Text;
    # Function to undo this operation.
    undoCommand @3 :Text;
    # Expiry (some operations can only be undone within a window).
    expiresAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Bookmarks ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Bookmark {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    label @1 :Text;
    command @2 :Text;
    createdAt @3 :T.Timestamp;
    useCount @4 :UInt64;
    tags @5 :List(Text);
}

# ── Watchers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct WatcherInfo {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    domain @1 :Text;
    command @2 :Text;
    startedAt @3 :T.Timestamp;
    eventCount @4 :UInt64;
    lastEvent @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Script ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ScriptError {
    line @0 :UInt32;
    column @1 :UInt32;
    message @2 :Text;
    severity @3 :ScriptSeverity;
}

enum ScriptSeverity {
    error @0;
    warning @1;
    info @2;
    hint @3;
}

struct ScriptContext {
    path @0 :Text;
    line @1 :UInt32;
    variables @2 :List(ShellVariable);
    # Call stack for nested scripts.
    callStack @3 :List(Text);
}

# ── Shell Theme ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ShellTheme {
    # Color scheme name.
    name @0 :Text;
    # Primary accent color.
    accent @1 :Text;
    # Success color.
    successColor @2 :Text;
    # Error color.
    errorColor @3 :Text;
    # Warning color.
    warningColor @4 :Text;
    # Info color.
    infoColor @5 :Text;
    # Muted/dim color.
    mutedColor @6 :Text;
    # Whether to use Unicode symbols.
    unicode @7 :Bool;
    # Whether to use emoji.
    emoji @8 :Bool;
    # Table style.
    tableStyle @9 :TableStyle;
}

enum TableStyle {
    rounded @0;
    sharp @1;
    double @2;
    ascii @3;
    minimal @4;
    custom @5;
}

# ── Key Bindings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

enum KeyBindingProfile {
    emacs @0;
    vi @1;
    custom @2;
}

# ── Guided Mode ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct GuidedSession {
    sessionId @0 :UInt64;
    domain @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    totalSteps @3 :UInt32;
    currentStep @4 :UInt32;
}

struct GuidedStep {
    stepNumber @0 :UInt32;
    title @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    # What kind of input is expected.
    inputType @3 :GuidedInputType;

    # Example input.
    example @5 :Text;
    # Whether this step is optional.
    optional @6 :Bool;
    # Default value.

}

enum GuidedInputType {
    text @0;
    number @1;

    choice @3;

    color @5;

}

struct GuidedOption {

struct GuidedStepResult {

# ── Shell Snapshots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CLI — the command-line interface configuration and extension system
#
# This schema defines the CLI's self-configuration: how it discovers
# domains, loads extensions, manages output themes, handles errors,
# and provides the universal command surface. It is the meta-schema
# that governs how all other domains are presented to the user.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface CliService {
    # Get CLI configuration.
    getConfig @0 () -> (config :CliConfig);

    # Set CLI configuration.
    setConfig @1 (config :CliConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List all available domains.
    listDomains @2 () -> (domains :List(DomainInfo));

    # Get help for a domain.
    getDomainHelp @3 (domain :Text) -> (help :DomainHelp);

    # Get help for a specific command.
    getCommandHelp @4 (domain :Text, action :Text) -> (help :CommandHelp);

    # Get syntax reference for a domain.
    getSyntaxRef @5 (domain :Text) -> (syntax :SyntaxReference);

    # ── Extensions ─────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List CLI extensions (third-party domain plugins).
    listExtensions @6 () -> (extensions :List(CliExtension));

    # Install a CLI extension.
    installExtension @7 (extension :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Remove a CLI extension.
    removeExtension @8 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Enable/disable an extension.
    toggleExtension @9 (name :Text, enabled :Bool) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Themes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List available output themes.
    listThemes @10 () -> (themes :List(CliTheme));

    # Set the active theme.
    setTheme @11 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get the active theme.
    getTheme @12 () -> (theme :CliTheme);

    # ── Diagnostics ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Run CLI self-diagnostics.
    diagnose @13 () -> (report :DiagnosticReport);

    # Check protocol connectivity.
    ping @14 () -> (result :PingResult);

    # Get CLI version and build info.
    version @15 () -> (info :VersionInfo);

    # ── Output Control ─────────────────────────────────────────

    # Set global output format.
    setOutputFormat @16 (format :OutputFormat) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get current output format.
    getOutputFormat @17 () -> (format :OutputFormat);

    # Set verbosity level.
    setVerbosity @18 (level :VerbosityLevel) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Command Registry ───────────────────────────────────────

    # Register a custom command (for extensions).
    registerCommand @19 (command :CommandRegistration) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Unregister a custom command.
    unregisterCommand @20 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List all registered commands (including extensions).
    listCommands @21 () -> (commands :List(CommandRegistration));

    # ── Learning & Discovery ───────────────────────────────────

    # Get "what can I do?" for a context.
    getSuggestions @22 (context :Text) -> (suggestions :List(CommandSuggestion));

    # Get tutorial for a domain.
    getTutorial @23 (domain :Text) -> (tutorial :Tutorial);

    # Get cheat sheet (commonly used commands).
    getCheatSheet @24 () -> (sheet :CheatSheet);
}

# ── CLI Config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CliConfig {
    # Default output format.
    defaultFormat @0 :OutputFormat;
    # Active theme name.
    theme @1 :Text;
    # Verbosity level.
    verbosity @2 :VerbosityLevel;
    # Whether to confirm destructive operations.
    confirmDestructive @3 :Bool;
    # Whether to enable AI-assisted interpretation.
    aiAssist @4 :Bool;
    # Whether to show tips on startup.
    showTips @5 :Bool;
    # Whether to enable auto-correction.
    autoCorrect @6 :Bool;
    # Maximum completion items to show.
    maxCompletions @7 :UInt32;
    # History file location.
    historyPath @8 :Text;
    # Config file location.
    configPath @9 :Text;
    # Enabled extensions.
    enabledExtensions @10 :List(Text);
    # Disabled domains (hidden from completion).
    disabledDomains @11 :List(Text);
    # Custom key bindings.
    keybindings @12 :List(KeyBinding);
    # Startup message.
    startupMessage @13 :Text;
    # Whether to check for updates on startup.
    checkUpdates @14 :Bool;
    # Remote hosts configuration.
    remoteHosts @15 :List(RemoteHostConfig);
}

enum VerbosityLevel {
    quiet @0;       # Minimal output (for scripting)
    normal @1;      # Standard output
    verbose @2;     # Detailed output
    debug @3;       # Debug output
    trace @4;       # Trace output (every protocol call)
}

# ── Domain Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DomainInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    # Number of commands in this domain.
    commandCount @2 :UInt32;
    # Whether this domain is available (protocol connected).
    available @3 :Bool;
    # Schema version backing this domain.
    schemaVersion @4 :T.Version;
    # Whether this is a built-in or extension domain.
    extension @5 :Bool;
    # Commands in this domain.
    commands @6 :List(CommandBrief);
    # Category this domain belongs to.
    category @7 :DomainCategory;
}

enum DomainCategory {
    system @0;
    hardware @1;
    display @2;
    networking @3;
    media @4;
    security @5;
    files @6;
    apps @7;
    data @8;
    settings @9;
    management @10;
    developer @11;
    custom @12;
}

struct CommandBrief {
    name @0 :Text;
    syntax @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    destructive @3 :Bool;
}

# ── Help ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DomainHelp {
    domain @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    commands @2 :List(CommandHelp);
    selectors @3 :List(SelectorHelp);
    examples @4 :List(Text);
    seeAlso @5 :List(Text);
}

struct CommandHelp {
    name @0 :Text;
    syntax @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    arguments @3 :List(ArgumentHelp);
    options @4 :List(OptionHelp);
    examples @5 :List(Text);
    destructive @6 :Bool;
    undoable @7 :Bool;
    requiresCapability @8 :Text;
    seeAlso @9 :List(Text);
}

struct ArgumentHelp {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    required @2 :Bool;
    type @3 :Text;
    default @4 :Text;
    example @5 :Text;
}

struct OptionHelp {
    name @0 :Text;
    short @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    type @3 :Text;
    default @4 :Text;
}

struct SelectorHelp {
    path @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    type @2 :Text;
    example @3 :Text;
}

# ── Syntax Reference ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SyntaxReference {
    domain @0 :Text;
    # All commands in syntax form.
    commands @1 :List(Text);
    # Rules that apply to this domain.
    rules @2 :List(Text);
    # Common patterns.
    patterns @3 :List(Text);
}

# ── Extensions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CliExtension {
    name @0 :Text;
    version @1 :T.Version;
    description @2 :Text;
    author @3 :Text;
    # Domains this extension provides.
    domains @4 :List(Text);
    # Whether the extension is enabled.
    enabled @5 :Bool;
    # Dependencies (other extensions or schemas).
    dependencies @6 :List(Text);
}

# ── Themes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CliTheme {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    # Whether this is a dark or light theme.
    dark @2 :Bool;
    # Color definitions.
    colors @3 :ThemeColors;
    # Table style.
    tableStyle @4 :Text;
    # Whether to use Unicode.
    unicode @5 :Bool;
    # Whether to use emoji icons.
    emoji @6 :Bool;
}

struct ThemeColors {
    primary @0 :Text;
    success @1 :Text;
    error @2 :Text;
    warning @3 :Text;
    info @4 :Text;
    muted @5 :Text;
    accent @6 :Text;
    background @7 :Text;
    foreground @8 :Text;
}

# ── Diagnostics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DiagnosticReport {
    # CLI version and build.
    cliVersion @0 :Text;
    # Protocol connectivity status.
    protocolConnected @1 :Bool;
    # Protocol version.
    protocolVersion @2 :Text;
    # Available domains.
    availableDomains @3 :UInt32;
    # Unavailable domains.
    unavailableDomains @4 :UInt32;
    # Schema versions matched.
    schemaVersionsMatch @5 :Bool;
    # Extensions loaded.
    extensionsLoaded @6 :UInt32;
    # Extensions failed.
    extensionsFailed @7 :UInt32;
    # Issues found.
    issues @8 :List(DiagnosticIssue);
    # Recommendations.
    recommendations @9 :List(Text);
    # Latency to protocol daemon.
    latencyMs @10 :Float32;
}

struct DiagnosticIssue {
    severity @0 :IssueSeverity;
    domain @1 :Text;
    message @2 :Text;
    suggestion @3 :Text;
}

enum IssueSeverity {
    info @0;
    warning @1;
    error @2;
    critical @3;
}

struct PingResult {
    reachable @0 :Bool;
    latencyMs @1 :Float32;
    protocolVersion @2 :Text;
    daemonVersion @3 :Text;
    uptime @4 :T.Duration;
}

struct VersionInfo {
    cliVersion @0 :Text;
    protocolVersion @1 :Text;
    buildDate @2 :Text;
    gitHash @3 :Text;
    rustVersion @4 :Text;
    targetTriple @5 :Text;
    features @6 :List(Text);
}

# ── Command Registration ─────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CommandRegistration {
    name @0 :Text;
    domain @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    syntax @3 :Text;
    handler @4 :Text;           # Handler identifier (extension-specific)
    destructive @5 :Bool;
    undoable @6 :Bool;
}

# ── Suggestions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CommandSuggestion {
    command @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    relevance @2 :Float32;
    # Why this was suggested.
    reason @3 :Text;
}

# ── Tutorial ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Tutorial {
    domain @0 :Text;
    title @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    steps @3 :List(TutorialStep);
    estimatedMinutes @4 :UInt32;
}

struct TutorialStep {
    title @0 :Text;
    instruction @1 :Text;
    command @2 :Text;
    expectedOutput @3 :Text;

}

# ── Cheat Sheet ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CheatSheet {

}

struct CheatSheetSection {
    title @0 :Text;
    entries @1 :List(CheatSheetEntry);
}

struct CheatSheetEntry {
    command @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
}

# ── Key Binding ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct KeyBinding {
    key @0 :Text;

# ── Remote Host Config ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct RemoteHostConfig {

    user @3 :Text;
    autoConnect @4 :Bool;
}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Diagnostics — system health, self-test, profiling, and alerting
#
# Not a logging system. Not a monitoring system. This is the system's
# ability to diagnose itself: "am I healthy?", "what's wrong?",
# "why is it slow?", "what will fail soon?". The answers are structured
# data, not log lines.
#
# Every subsystem can register health checks. The diagnostics engine
# aggregates them into a unified health picture. Alerts are typed,
# not strings.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface DiagnosticsService {
    # Get overall system health.
    getHealth @0 () -> (health :SystemHealth);

    # Run all health checks.
    runChecks @1 (scope :HealthScope) -> (results :List(HealthCheckResult));

    # Run a specific health check.
    runCheck @2 (checkId :Text) -> (result :HealthCheckResult);

    # List available health checks.
    listChecks @3 () -> (checks :List(HealthCheck));

    # ── Alerts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List active alerts.
    listAlerts @4 (filter :AlertFilter) -> (alerts :List(Alert));

    # Acknowledge an alert.
    acknowledgeAlert @5 (alertId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Dismiss an alert.
    dismissAlert @6 (alertId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Configure alert thresholds.
    setAlertThreshold @7 (threshold :AlertThreshold) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List configured thresholds.
    listThresholds @8 () -> (thresholds :List(AlertThreshold));

    # Subscribe to alerts.
    subscribeAlerts @9 () -> (subscription :AlertSubscription);

    # ── Performance Profiling ──────────────────────────────────

    # Start a performance profile.
    startProfile @10 (target :ProfileTarget) -> (profileId :UInt64);

    # Stop a profile and get results.
    stopProfile @11 (profileId :UInt64) -> (result :ProfileResult);

    # Get a snapshot of current performance.
    snapshot @12 () -> (snapshot :PerformanceSnapshot);

    # ── Self-Test ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Run system self-test suite.
    runSelfTest @13 (suite :SelfTestSuite) -> (result :SelfTestResult);

    # List available self-test suites.
    listSelfTestSuites @14 () -> (suites :List(SelfTestSuite));

    # ── Diagnostics Report ─────────────────────────────────────

    # Generate a full diagnostic report.
    generateReport @15 (scope :ReportScope) -> (report :DiagnosticReport);

    # Export report to file.
    exportReport @16 (reportId :UInt64, format :ReportFormat, path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Predictive ─────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get failure predictions (disk, battery, memory, etc).
    getPredictions @17 () -> (predictions :List(FailurePrediction));

    # Get resource trend analysis.
    getTrend @18 (resource :Text, duration :T.Duration) -> (trend :ResourceTrend);
}

# ── System Health ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SystemHealth {
    # Overall status.
    status @0 :HealthStatus;
    # Individual subsystem health.
    subsystems @1 :List(SubsystemHealth);
    # Active alert count.
    alertCount @2 :UInt32;
    # Critical alert count.
    criticalAlertCount @3 :UInt32;
    # Last full check timestamp.
    lastCheck @4 :T.Timestamp;
    # Uptime.
    uptime @5 :T.Duration;
    # System load indicators.
    load @6 :SystemLoadIndicators;
}

enum HealthStatus {
    healthy @0;
    degraded @1;
    unhealthy @2;
    critical @3;
    unknown @4;
}

struct SubsystemHealth {
    name @0 :Text;
    status @1 :HealthStatus;
    message @2 :Text;
    lastCheck @3 :T.Timestamp;
    # Metrics for this subsystem.
    metrics @4 :List(HealthMetric);
}

struct HealthMetric {
    name @0 :Text;
    value @1 :Float64;
    unit @2 :Text;
    # Normal range.
    minNormal @3 :Float64;
    maxNormal @4 :Float64;
    # Whether current value is in normal range.
    normal @5 :Bool;
}

struct SystemLoadIndicators {
    cpuUsage @0 :Float32;          # 0.0-1.0
    memoryUsage @1 :Float32;       # 0.0-1.0
    diskUsage @2 :Float32;         # 0.0-1.0
    networkUsage @3 :Float32;      # 0.0-1.0
    swapUsage @4 :Float32;         # 0.0-1.0
    gpuUsage @5 :Float32;          # 0.0-1.0
    ioWait @6 :Float32;            # 0.0-1.0
    thermalPressure @7 :Float32;   # 0.0-1.0
}

# ── Health Checks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct HealthCheck {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    subsystem @3 :Text;
    # How often to run (0 = manual only).
    interval @4 :T.Duration;
    # Whether this check is enabled.
    enabled @5 :Bool;
    # Severity if this check fails.
    failureSeverity @6 :AlertSeverity;
}

struct HealthCheckResult {
    checkId @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    status @2 :HealthStatus;
    message @3 :Text;
    details @4 :T.StringMap;
    duration @5 :T.Duration;
    timestamp @6 :T.Timestamp;
    # Remediation suggestion.
    remediation @7 :Text;
}

enum HealthScope {
    quick @0;       # Critical checks only (~5 seconds)
    standard @1;    # All enabled checks (~30 seconds)
    deep @2;        # All checks including slow ones (~5 minutes)
    custom @3;      # Specific checks
}

# ── Alerts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Alert {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    severity @1 :AlertSeverity;
    title @2 :Text;
    message @3 :Text;
    subsystem @4 :Text;
    source @5 :Text;
    timestamp @6 :T.Timestamp;
    # Whether this alert has been acknowledged.
    acknowledged @7 :Bool;
    # Acknowledged by whom.
    acknowledgedBy @8 :Text;
    # When acknowledged.
    acknowledgedAt @9 :T.Timestamp;
    # Remediation steps.
    remediation @10 :List(Text);
    # Related metrics.
    metrics @11 :List(HealthMetric);
    # Whether this alert is auto-resolvable.
    autoResolvable @12 :Bool;
    # Auto-resolve command.
    autoResolveCommand @13 :Text;
}

enum AlertSeverity {
    info @0;
    warning @1;
    error @2;
    critical @3;
    emergency @4;
}

struct AlertFilter {
    severities @0 :List(AlertSeverity);
    subsystems @1 :List(Text);
    since @2 :T.Timestamp;
    acknowledged @3 :T.BoolFilter;
    unresolved @4 :Bool;
}

struct AlertThreshold {
    id @0 :Text;
    metric @1 :Text;
    subsystem @2 :Text;
    # Threshold values.
    warningThreshold @3 :Float64;
    errorThreshold @4 :Float64;
    criticalThreshold @5 :Float64;
    # Direction: above or below threshold triggers alert.
    direction @6 :ThresholdDirection;
    # Duration the condition must persist before alerting.
    sustainedDuration @7 :T.Duration;
    # Whether this threshold is enabled.
    enabled @8 :Bool;
}

enum ThresholdDirection {
    above @0;
    below @1;
    change @2;     # Alert on rapid change regardless of value
}

interface AlertSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (alerts :List(Alert));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Performance Profiling ────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProfileTarget {
    union {
        system @0 :Void;               # Profile entire system
        process @1 :T.ProcessId;       # Profile specific process
        service @2 :Text;              # Profile specific service
        domain @3 :Text;               # Profile specific domain (audio, network, etc)
        custom @4 :Text;
    }
    # Profile duration (0 = until stopped).
    duration @5 :T.Duration;
    # What to profile.
    metrics @6 :List(ProfileMetricType);
}

enum ProfileMetricType {
    cpu @0;
    memory @1;
    io @2;
    network @3;
    gpu @4;
    latency @5;
    throughput @6;
    custom @7;
}

struct ProfileResult {
    profileId @0 :UInt64;
    target @1 :ProfileTarget;
    startTime @2 :T.Timestamp;
    endTime @3 :T.Timestamp;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    samples @5 :List(ProfileSample);
    summary @6 :ProfileSummary;
}

struct ProfileSample {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    metric @1 :ProfileMetricType;
    value @2 :Float64;
    unit @3 :Text;
}

struct ProfileSummary {
    cpu @0 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    memory @1 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    io @2 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    network @3 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    # Hotspots (top consumers).
    hotspots @4 :List(Hotspot);
}

struct ProfileMetricSummary {
    min @0 :Float64;
    max @1 :Float64;
    avg @2 :Float64;
    p50 @3 :Float64;
    p95 @4 :Float64;
    p99 @5 :Float64;
}

struct Hotspot {
    name @0 :Text;
    percentage @1 :Float32;
    description @2 :Text;
}

struct PerformanceSnapshot {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    cpu @1 :CpuSnapshot;
    memory @2 :MemorySnapshot;
    io @3 :IoSnapshot;
    network @4 :NetworkSnapshot;
    gpu @5 :GpuSnapshot;
}

struct CpuSnapshot {
    overallUsage @0 :Float32;
    perCoreUsage @1 :List(Float32);
    frequency @2 :List(UInt64);      # MHz per core
    temperature @3 :List(Float32);    # Per core
    contextSwitches @4 :UInt64;
    interrupts @5 :UInt64;
    loadAverage @6 :T.LoadAverage;
}

struct MemorySnapshot {
    totalBytes @0 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @1 :UInt64;
    availableBytes @2 :UInt64;
    cachedBytes @3 :UInt64;
    bufferBytes @4 :UInt64;
    swapTotalBytes @5 :UInt64;
    swapUsedBytes @6 :UInt64;
    # Top memory consumers.
    topConsumers @7 :List(MemoryConsumer);
}

struct MemoryConsumer {
    name @0 :Text;
    pid @1 :T.ProcessId;
    bytes @2 :UInt64;
    percentage @3 :Float32;
}

struct IoSnapshot {
    readBytesPerSec @0 :UInt64;
    writeBytesPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    iops @2 :UInt32;
    readLatencyMs @3 :Float32;
    writeLatencyMs @4 :Float32;
    # Per-device stats.
    devices @5 :List(DeviceIoStats);
}

struct DeviceIoStats {
    device @0 :Text;
    readBytesPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    writeBytesPerSec @2 :UInt64;
    iops @3 :UInt32;
    utilization @4 :Float32;
}

struct NetworkSnapshot {
    totalBytesPerSec @0 :UInt64;
    bytesInPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    bytesOutPerSec @2 :UInt64;
    packetsInPerSec @3 :UInt64;
    packetsOutPerSec @4 :UInt64;
    connections @5 :UInt32;
    errors @6 :UInt32;
    # Per-interface stats.
    interfaces @7 :List(InterfaceStats);
}

struct InterfaceStats {
    name @0 :Text;
    bytesInPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    bytesOutPerSec @2 :UInt64;
    linkSpeed @3 :UInt64;
    utilization @4 :Float32;
}

struct GpuSnapshot {
    usage @0 :Float32;
    memoryUsed @1 :UInt64;
    memoryTotal @2 :UInt64;
    temperature @3 :Float32;
    fanSpeed @4 :Float32;
    powerWatts @5 :Float32;
}

# ── Self-Test ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SelfTestSuite {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    tests @2 :List(SelfTest);
    estimatedDuration @3 :T.Duration;
    # Whether this suite requires elevated privileges.
    requiresPrivilege @4 :Bool;
}

struct SelfTest {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    subsystem @3 :Text;
    # Estimated duration.
    estimatedDuration @4 :T.Duration;
    # Whether this test is destructive (may affect system state).
    destructive @5 :Bool;
}

struct SelfTestResult {
    suite @0 :Text;
    passed @1 :UInt32;
    failed @2 :UInt32;
    skipped @3 :UInt32;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    results @5 :List(SelfTestItemResult);
    timestamp @6 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct SelfTestItemResult {
    testId @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    passed @2 :Bool;
    message @3 :Text;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    # Remediation if failed.
    remediation @5 :Text;
}

# ── Diagnostic Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ReportScope {
    # Include system info.
    includeSystem @0 :Bool;
    # Include health checks.
    includeHealth @1 :Bool;
    # Include performance snapshot.
    includePerformance @2 :Bool;
    # Include recent alerts.
    includeAlerts @3 :Bool;
    # Include hardware details.
    includeHardware @4 :Bool;
    # Include network details.
    includeNetwork @5 :Bool;
    # Include process list.
    includeProcesses @6 :Bool;
    # Include service status.
    includeServices @7 :Bool;
    # Include kernel info.
    includeKernel @8 :Bool;
    # Time range for historical data.
    since @9 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum ReportFormat {
    text @0;
    json @1;
    html @2;
    markdown @3;
    pdf @4;
    custom @5;
}

struct DiagnosticReport {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    generatedAt @1 :T.Timestamp;
    scope @2 :ReportScope;
    system @3 :SystemSummary;
    health @4 :SystemHealth;
    performance @5 :PerformanceSnapshot;
    alerts @6 :List(Alert);
    hardware @7 :HardwareSummary;
    network @8 :NetworkSummary;
    processes @9 :ProcessSummary;
    services @10 :ServiceSummary;
    kernel @11 :KernelSummary;
    recommendations @12 :List(Recommendation);
}

struct SystemSummary {
    hostname @0 :Text;
    os @1 :Text;
    kernelVersion @2 :Text;
    architecture @3 :Text;
    uptime @4 :T.Duration;
    bootTime @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct HardwareSummary {
    cpu @0 :Text;
    cpuCores @1 :UInt32;
    memoryBytes @2 :UInt64;
    gpus @3 :List(Text);
    disks @4 :List(DiskSummary);
    thermals @5 :ThermalSummary;
}

struct DiskSummary {
    device @0 :Text;
    sizeBytes @1 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @2 :UInt64;
    health @3 :Text;
    temperature @4 :Float32;
}

struct ThermalSummary {
    cpuTemp @0 :Float32;
    gpuTemp @1 :Float32;
    ambientTemp @2 :Float32;
    fanSpeeds @3 :List(FanSpeed);
}

struct FanSpeed {
    name @0 :Text;
    rpm @1 :UInt32;
}

struct NetworkSummary {
    interfaces @0 :UInt32;
    connected @1 :Bool;
    ssid @2 :Text;
    ip @3 :Text;
    publicIp @4 :Text;
    dnsServers @5 :List(Text);
}

struct ProcessSummary {
    total @0 :UInt32;
    running @1 :UInt32;
    sleeping @2 :UInt32;
    zombie @3 :UInt32;
    topCpu @4 :List(Text);
    topMemory @5 :List(Text);
}

struct ServiceSummary {
    total @0 :UInt32;
    active @1 :UInt32;
    failed @2 :UInt32;
    failedServices @3 :List(Text);
}

struct KernelSummary {
    type @0 :Text;
    version @1 :Text;
    architecture @2 :Text;
    capabilities @3 :List(Text);
    extensions @4 :UInt32;
}

struct Recommendation {
    severity @0 :AlertSeverity;
    title @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    action @3 :Text;
    command @4 :Text;      # Command to execute the recommendation
}

# ── Predictive ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct FailurePrediction {
    component @0 :Text;
    # What might fail.
    failureType @1 :FailureType;
    # Confidence (0.0-1.0).
    confidence @2 :Float32;
    # Estimated time until failure.
    estimatedTimeToFailure @3 :T.Duration;
    # Current health indicator.
    currentHealth @4 :Float32;
    # Recommendation.
    recommendation @5 :Text;
    # When this prediction was made.
    predictedAt @6 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum FailureType {
    diskFailure @0;
    memoryDegradation @1;
    batteryDegradation @2;
    thermalThrottling @3;
    networkDegradation @4;
    serviceInstability @5;
    custom @6;
}

struct ResourceTrend {
    resource @0 :Text;
    duration @1 :T.Duration;
    direction @2 :TrendDirection;
    changeRate @3 :Float32;        # Units per hour
    currentValue @4 :Float64;
    predictedValue @5 :Float64;    # Predicted value at duration end
    samples @6 :List(TrendSample);
    # When trend will hit critical threshold (if applicable).
    criticalAt @7 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum TrendDirection {
    stable @0;
    increasing @1;
    decreasing @2;
    volatile @3;
    cyclic @4;
}

struct TrendSample {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    value @1 :Float64;
}
