using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Init — the init system, service supervision, and boot orchestration
#
# This is not systemd. This is not OpenRC. This is the init contract:
# what the first process must provide. Services, dependencies, ordering,
# socket activation, timer management, and boot stages. The backend
# decides how — the protocol decides what.
#
# The init system IS a smart-protocol service. It speaks Cap'n Proto
# from the first moment the kernel enters userspace. There is no
# "before the protocol" phase.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface InitService {
    # Get the current boot state.
    getBootState @0 () -> (state :BootState);

    # Get the current target (runlevel equivalent).
    getTarget @1 () -> (target :BootTarget);

    # Set the target (change runlevel).
    setTarget @2 (target :BootTarget) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List all defined targets.
    listTargets @3 () -> (targets :List(BootTargetInfo));

    # ── Service Management ─────────────────────────────────────

    # List all services (all states).
    listServices @4 (filter :ServiceFilter) -> (services :List(ServiceInfo), total :UInt32);

    # Get a specific service.
    getService @5 (name :Text) -> (service :ServiceInfo);

    # Start a service.
    start @6 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Stop a service.
    stop @7 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Restart a service.
    restart @8 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Reload a service (send reload signal without full restart).
    reload @9 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Enable a service (start at boot).
    enable @10 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Disable a service (don't start at boot).
    disable @11 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Mask a service (prevent from being started at all).
    mask @12 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Unmask a service.
    unmask @13 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get service dependency tree.
    getDependencies @14 (name :Text) -> (deps :ServiceDependencyTree);

    # Get services that depend on this service.
    getDependents @15 (name :Text) -> (dependents :List(Text));

    # ── Logs ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get service logs.
    getServiceLogs @16 (name :Text, filter :LogFilter) -> (logs :List(ServiceLogEntry), total :UInt32);

    # Stream service logs.
    watchServiceLogs @17 (name :Text) -> (subscription :LogSubscription);

    # ── Socket Activation ──────────────────────────────────────

    # List socket-activated services.
    listSockets @18 () -> (sockets :List(SocketInfo));

    # Get socket state.
    getSocketState @19 (name :Text) -> (state :SocketState);

    # ── Timers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List timer-triggered services.
    listTimers @20 () -> (timers :List(TimerInfo));

    # Get timer state.
    getTimerState @21 (name :Text) -> (state :TimerState);

    # Manually trigger a timer.
    triggerTimer @22 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Boot History ───────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get boot history.
    getBootHistory @23 (pagination :T.Pagination) -> (boots :List(BootRecord), total :UInt32);

    # Get boot chart (timing breakdown).
    getBootChart @24 (bootId :UInt64) -> (chart :BootChart);

    # ── Service Events ─────────────────────────────────────────

    # Subscribe to service state changes.
    subscribe @25 () -> (subscription :InitSubscription);

    # ── Emergency ──────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Enter emergency mode (minimal services only).
    enterEmergency @26 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # Exit emergency mode.
    exitEmergency @27 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Boot State ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct BootState {
    phase @0 :BootPhase;
    currentTarget @1 :Text;
    targetProgress @2 :Float32;    # 0.0-1.0
    servicesTotal @3 :UInt32;
    servicesStarted @4 :UInt32;
    servicesFailed @5 :UInt32;
    bootTime @6 :T.Duration;
    # Whether we're in emergency mode.
    emergency @7 :Bool;
    # Boot ID (unique per boot).
    bootId @8 :UInt64;
}

enum BootPhase {
    firmware @0;       # Firmware/BIOS phase
    bootloader @1;     # Bootloader phase
    kernelInit @2;     # Kernel initialization
    initStart @3;      # Init process starting
    servicesStarting @4; # Services starting
    servicesReady @5;  # All services started
    userSession @6;    # User session active
    shutdown @7;       # System shutting down
    reboot @8;         # System rebooting
    emergency @9;      # Emergency mode
    custom @10;
}

# ── Boot Target ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct BootTarget {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
}

struct BootTargetInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    # Whether this is the default target.
    default @2 :Bool;
    # Whether this is the current target.
    active @3 :Bool;
    # Services included in this target.
    services @4 :List(Text);
    # Dependencies (other targets).
    dependencies @5 :List(Text);
}

# ── Service Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ServiceInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    state @2 :ServiceState;
    subState @3 :Text;
    pid @4 :T.ProcessId;
    # Whether the service is enabled at boot.
    enabled @5 :Bool;
    # Whether the service is masked.
    masked @6 :Bool;
    # Service type.
    type @7 :ServiceType;
    # When the service was started.
    activeSince @8 :T.Timestamp;
    # Exit status (if stopped/failed).
    exitStatus @9 :T.ExitStatus;
    # Memory usage.
    memoryBytes @10 :UInt64;
    # CPU time used.
    cpuTime @11 :T.Duration;
    # Restart count.
    restartCount @12 :UInt32;
    # Dependencies.
    requires @13 :List(Text);
    wants @14 :List(Text);
    after @15 :List(Text);
    before @16 :List(Text);
    # Watchdog status.
    watchdog @17 :WatchdogStatus;
    # Resource limits.
    resourceLimits @18 :ServiceResourceLimits;
    # Security context.
    security @19 :ServiceSecurity;
}

enum ServiceState {
    active @0;
    inactive @1;
    activating @2;
    deactivating @3;
    failed @4;
    masked @5;
    notFound @6;
    maintenance @7;
}

enum ServiceType {
    simple @0;         # Main process is the service process
    forking @1;        # Service forks a child
    oneshot @2;        # Runs once and exits
    notify @3;         # Sends readiness notification
    dbus @4;           # Acquires a D-Bus name
    socket @5;         # Socket-activated
    timer @6;          # Timer-triggered
    idle @7;           # Starts when nothing else is queued
    exec @8;           # Like simple but exec() only
    custom @9;
}

struct WatchdogStatus {
    enabled @0 :Bool;
    interval @1 :T.Duration;
    lastPing @2 :T.Timestamp;
    # Whether the watchdog is currently healthy.
    healthy @3 :Bool;
}

struct ServiceResourceLimits {
    maxMemoryBytes @0 :UInt64;
    maxCpuPercent @1 :Float32;
    maxOpenFiles @2 :UInt32;
    maxProcesses @3 :UInt32;
    ioWeight @4 :UInt32;
    niceLevel @5 :Int8;
}

struct ServiceSecurity {
    # User the service runs as.
    user @0 :Text;
    # Group the service runs as.
    group @1 :Text;
    # Whether to use a private /tmp.
    privateTmp @2 :Bool;
    # Whether to protect system directories.
    protectSystem @3 :Bool;
    # Whether to protect home directories.
    protectHome @4 :Bool;
    # Capability bounding set.
    capabilityBoundingSet @5 :List(Text);
    # System call filter.
    systemCallFilter @6 :List(Text);
    # Whether to use a new network namespace.
    privateNetwork @7 :Bool;
    # Read-only paths.
    readOnlyPaths @8 :List(Text);
    # Read-write paths.
    readWritePaths @9 :List(Text);
}

struct ServiceFilter {
    state @0 :ServiceState;
    type @1 :ServiceType;
    enabled @2 :T.BoolFilter;
    pattern @3 :Text;
    target @4 :Text;         # Only services in this target
}

struct ServiceDependencyTree {
    service @0 :Text;
    # Services this one requires.
    requires @1 :List(ServiceDependencyTree);
    # Services this one wants.
    wants @2 :List(ServiceDependencyTree);
    # Ordering constraints.
    after @3 :List(Text);
    # Circular dependency detected?
    circular @4 :Bool;
}

# ── Service Logs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ServiceLogEntry {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    service @1 :Text;
    level @2 :LogLevel;
    message @3 :Text;
    pid @4 :T.ProcessId;
    # Structured fields (key-value pairs from the service).
    fields @5 :T.StringMap;
}

enum LogLevel {
    emergency @0;
    alert @1;
    critical @2;
    error @3;
    warning @4;
    notice @5;
    info @6;
    debug @7;
}

struct LogFilter {
    levels @0 :List(LogLevel);
    since @1 :T.Timestamp;
    until @2 :T.Timestamp;
    pattern @3 :Text;
    maxEntries @4 :UInt32;
}

interface LogSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (entries :List(ServiceLogEntry));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Socket Activation ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SocketInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    # The service this socket activates.
    service @1 :Text;
    # Socket type.
    type @2 :SocketType;
    # Address (path for Unix socket, host:port for TCP).
    address @3 :Text;
    # Current state.
    state @4 :SocketState;
    # Number of connections.
    connections @5 :UInt32;
    # Whether the socket is accepting connections.
    accepting @6 :Bool;
}

enum SocketType {
    unix @0;
    tcp @1;
    udp @2;
    netlink @3;
    custom @4;
}

enum SocketState {
    waiting @0;        # Waiting for connections
    running @1;        # Service activated and running
    failed @2;         # Socket creation failed
    inactive @3;       # Not yet listening
}

# ── Timers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct TimerInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    # The service this timer triggers.
    service @1 :Text;
    # Timer schedule.
    schedule @2 :TimerSchedule;
    # Current state.
    state @3 :TimerState;
    # Last trigger time.
    lastTriggered @4 :T.Timestamp;
    # Next trigger time.
    nextTrigger @5 :T.Timestamp;
    # Number of times triggered.
    triggerCount @6 :UInt64;
    # Whether the timer is persistent (runs missed triggers).

# ── Boot History ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SocketActivatedEvent {

struct TimerTriggeredEvent {

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Task Scheduler — scheduling policies, priorities, affinity, and
#                  real-time scheduling
#
# How tasks are scheduled is a kernel implementation detail. But what
# policies exist, what priorities are available, and what affinity
# constraints can be expressed — that is a protocol contract.
#
# This schema is what apps and system tools observe and request.
# The backend (CFS, EEVDF, BFS, deadline scheduler, etc.) is invisible.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface SchedulerService {
    # Get scheduler info.
    getInfo @0 () -> (info :SchedulerInfo);

    # Get the scheduling policy for a process.
    getPolicy @1 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (policy :ProcessSchedulingPolicy);

    # Set scheduling policy for a process.
    setPolicy @2 (pid :T.ProcessId, policy :ProcessSchedulingPolicy) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get CPU affinity for a process.
    getAffinity @3 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (affinity :CpuAffinity);

    # Set CPU affinity for a process.
    setAffinity @4 (pid :T.ProcessId, affinity :CpuAffinity) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get NUMA policy for a process.
    getNumaPolicy @5 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (policy :NumaPolicy);

    # Set NUMA policy for a process.
    setNumaPolicy @6 (pid :T.ProcessId, policy :NumaPolicy) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── SMP Topology ───────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get CPU topology.
    getTopology @7 () -> (topology :CpuTopology);

    # Get per-CPU load.
    getCpuLoad @8 () -> (load :List(CpuLoadInfo));

    # Get current CPU for calling context.
    getCurrentCpu @9 () -> (cpu :UInt32);

    # Subscribe to topology changes (hotplug, frequency changes).
    subscribeTopology @10 () -> (subscription :TopologySubscription);

    # ── Scheduling Domains ─────────────────────────────────────

    # List scheduling domains.
    listDomains @11 () -> (domains :List(SchedulingDomain));

    # Get domain for a CPU.
    getDomain @12 (cpu :UInt32) -> (domain :SchedulingDomain);

    # ── Load Balancing ─────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get load balancing statistics.
    getLoadBalanceStats @13 () -> (stats :LoadBalanceStats);

    # Trigger manual load rebalance.
    rebalance @14 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Real-Time Scheduling ───────────────────────────────────

    # Get RT scheduling bandwidth.
    getRtBandwidth @15 () -> (bandwidth :RtBandwidth);

    # Set RT scheduling bandwidth.
    setRtBandwidth @16 (bandwidth :RtBandwidth) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get deadline scheduling info for a process.
    getDeadlineInfo @17 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (info :DeadlineInfo);

    # Set deadline scheduling for a process.
    setDeadline @18 (pid :T.ProcessId, info :DeadlineInfo) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Fair Scheduling ────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get cgroup scheduler config.
    getCgroupConfig @19 (cgroup :Text) -> (config :CgroupSchedulerConfig);

    # Set cgroup scheduler config.
    setCgroupConfig @20 (cgroup :Text, config :CgroupSchedulerConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Subscribe to scheduling events (migration, throttle, etc).
    subscribe @21 () -> (subscription :SchedulerSubscription);
}

# ── Scheduler Info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SchedulerInfo {
    # Name of the scheduling algorithm.
    name @0 :Text;
    # Version of the scheduler.
    version @1 :Text;
    # Supported policies.
    supportedPolicies @2 :List(SchedulingPolicy);
    # Number of scheduling domains.
    domainCount @3 :UInt32;
    # Whether NUMA balancing is enabled.
    numaBalancing @4 :Bool;
    # Whether autogroup is enabled.
    autogroup @5 :Bool;
    # Timer tick rate (Hz).
    tickRate @6 :UInt32;
    # Minimum granularity (ns).
    minGranularityNs @7 :UInt64;
    # Latency target (ns).
    latencyTargetNs @8 :UInt64;
}

enum SchedulingPolicy {
    other @0;          # SCHED_OTHER — default fair scheduling
    batch @1;          # SCHED_BATCH — batch scheduling
    idle @2;           # SCHED_IDLE — very low priority
    fifo @3;           # SCHED_FIFO — real-time FIFO
    roundRobin @4;     # SCHED_RR — real-time round-robin
    deadline @5;       # SCHED_DEADLINE — deadline scheduling
    custom @6;
}

# ── Process Scheduling Policy ────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessSchedulingPolicy {
    policy @0 :SchedulingPolicy;
    # Nice value (-20 to 19, only for OTHER/BATCH/IDLE).
    nice @1 :Int8;
    # RT priority (1-99, only for FIFO/RR).
    rtPriority @2 :UInt8;
    # Deadline parameters (only for DEADLINE).
    deadline @3 :DeadlineInfo;
    # I/O scheduling class.
    ioClass @4 :IoSchedulingClass;
    # I/O priority.
    ioPriority @5 :Int8;
}

enum IoSchedulingClass {
    none @0;
    realtime @1;
    bestEffort @2;
    idle @3;
}

# ── CPU Affinity ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CpuAffinity {
    # Bitmask of allowed CPUs.
    mask @0 :UInt64;
    # Human-readable list of allowed CPUs.
    cpus @1 :List(UInt32);
    # Whether this is a soft affinity (hint) or hard affinity (binding).
    soft @2 :Bool;
    # NUMA node affinity.
    numaNodes @3 :List(UInt32);
}

# ── NUMA Policy ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct NumaPolicy {
    mode @0 :NumaMode;
    # Target nodes.
    nodes @1 :List(UInt32);
    # Interleave weight per node.
    weights @2 :List(UInt32);
}

enum NumaMode {
    default @0;
    bind @1;            # Allocate only from specified nodes
    interleave @2;      # Round-robin across nodes
    prefer @3;          # Prefer specified nodes
    local @4;           # Allocate from local node
    custom @5;
}

# ── CPU Topology ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CpuTopology {
    # Total CPUs (logical).
    totalCpus @0 :UInt32;
    # Physical cores.
    physicalCores @1 :UInt32;
    # Threads per core.
    threadsPerCore @2 :UInt32;
    # Sockets/packages.
    sockets @3 :UInt32;
    # NUMA nodes.
    numaNodes @4 :UInt32;
    # Per-CPU details.
    cpus @5 :List(CpuInfo);
    # NUMA topology.
    numa @6 :List(NumaNodeInfo);
}

struct CpuInfo {
    id @0 :UInt32;
    # Physical core ID.
    coreId @1 :UInt32;
    # Socket ID.
    socketId @2 :UInt32;
    # NUMA node.
    numaNode @3 :UInt32;
    # Current frequency (MHz).
    frequency @4 :UInt64;
    # Max frequency (MHz).
    maxFrequency @5 :UInt64;
    # Min frequency (MHz).
    minFrequency @6 :UInt64;
    # Whether this CPU is online.
    online @7 :Bool;
    # Whether this CPU supports hyperthreading.
    hyperthread @8 :Bool;
    # Cache sizes.
    cacheL1 @9 :UInt64;
    cacheL2 @10 :UInt64;
    cacheL3 @11 :UInt64;
    # Current temperature.
    temperature @12 :Float32;
    # Instruction set extensions (SSE, AVX, NEON, etc).
    flags @13 :List(Text);
}

struct NumaNodeInfo {
    nodeId @0 :UInt32;
    # CPUs in this node.
    cpus @1 :List(UInt32);
    # Total memory in this node.
    memoryBytes @2 :UInt64;
    # Free memory in this node.
    freeMemoryBytes @3 :UInt64;
    # Distance to other nodes.
    distances @4 :List(UInt32);
}

struct CpuLoadInfo {
    cpuId @0 :UInt32;
    # Current utilization (0.0-1.0).
    utilization @1 :Float32;
    # User time.
    userTime @2 :Float32;
    # System time.
    systemTime @3 :Float32;
    # Idle time.
    idleTime @4 :Float32;
    # I/O wait time.
    ioWaitTime @5 :Float32;
    # Steal time (VM hypervisor).
    stealTime @6 :Float32;
    # Current frequency (MHz).
    frequency @7 :UInt64;
    # Temperature.
    temperature @8 :Float32;
}

# ── Scheduling Domain ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SchedulingDomain {
    name @0 :Text;
    level @1 :UInt32;          # 0 = core, 1 = package, 2 = NUMA, etc.
    cpus @2 :List(UInt32);
    # Load balance interval.
    balanceInterval @3 :T.Duration;
    # Cache-hot time.
    cacheHotTime @4 :T.Duration;
    # Whether idle balancing is enabled.
    idleBalance @5 :Bool;
    # Whether this domain is degenerate (single CPU).
    degenerate @6 :Bool;
}

# ── Load Balance ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct LoadBalanceStats {
    # Total migrations.
    migrations @0 :UInt64;
    # Migrations per second.
    migrationsPerSec @1 :Float32;
    # Failed migrations (no idle CPU found).
    failedMigrations @2 :UInt64;
    # Load imbalance ratio (0.0 = perfect balance).
    imbalanceRatio @3 :Float32;
    # Per-domain stats.
    domainStats @4 :List(DomainStats);
}

struct DomainStats {
    name @0 :Text;
    balanceCalls @1 :UInt64;
    idleBalance @2 :UInt64;
    migrations @3 :UInt64;
    imbalance @4 :Float32;
}

# ── RT Bandwidth ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct RtBandwidth {
    # Total RT bandwidth (microseconds per period).
    periodUs @0 :UInt64;
    # RT runtime allowed per period.
    runtimeUs @1 :UInt64;
    # Whether RT throttling is enabled.
    throttling @2 :Bool;
    # Number of RT throttled tasks.
    throttledCount @3 :UInt32;
}

# ── Deadline Scheduling ──────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DeadlineInfo {
    # Runtime (execution time budget in nanoseconds).
    runtimeNs @0 :UInt64;
    # Deadline (relative to start, in nanoseconds).
    deadlineNs @1 :UInt64;
    # Period (repeating interval, in nanoseconds).
    periodNs @2 :UInt64;
}

# ── Cgroup Scheduler Config ─────────────────────────────────────────

struct CgroupSchedulerConfig {
    # CPU weight (relative share, 1-10000).
    cpuWeight @0 :UInt32;
    # Maximum CPU bandwidth (percentage, 0 = unlimited).
    cpuMaxPercent @1 :Float32;
    # Maximum CPU bandwidth period (microseconds).
    cpuMaxPeriodUs @2 :UInt64;
    # Nice value for this cgroup.
    nice @3 :Int8;
    # Whether this cgroup can use RT scheduling.
    rtRuntimeUs @4 :UInt64;
    rtPeriodUs @5 :UInt64;
    # I/O weight.
    ioWeight @6 :UInt32;
    # Memory low protection (bytes).
    memoryLow @7 :UInt64;
    # Memory high threshold (bytes).
    memoryHigh @8 :UInt64;
    # Memory max limit (bytes).
    memoryMax @9 :UInt64;
}

# ── Topology Subscription ────────────────────────────────────────────

interface TopologySubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(TopologyEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct TopologyEvent {
    union {
        cpuOnline @0 :UInt32;
        cpuOffline @1 :UInt32;
        frequencyChanged @2 :FrequencyChangeEvent;
        temperatureChanged @3 :TemperatureChangeEvent;
        numaChanged @4 :Void;
        custom @5 :Data;
    }
}

struct FrequencyChangeEvent {
    cpuId @0 :UInt32;
    previousFreq @1 :UInt64;
    currentFreq @2 :UInt64;

}

struct TemperatureChangeEvent {
    cpuId @0 :UInt32;
    temperature @1 :Float32;
    throttleActive @2 :Bool;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Scheduler Events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface SchedulerSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(SchedulerEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct SchedulerEvent {
    union {
        processMigrated @0 :ProcessMigrationEvent;
        processThrottled @1 :ProcessThrottleEvent;
        priorityChanged @2 :PriorityChangeEvent;
        loadBalanceTriggered @3 :Void;
        custom @4 :Data;
    }
}

struct ProcessMigrationEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    fromCpu @1 :UInt32;
    toCpu @2 :UInt32;
    reason @3 :Text;
    timestamp @4 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct ProcessThrottleEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    reason @1 :Text;

}

struct PriorityChangeEvent {

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Signal — signal registration, delivery, masking, and queuing
#
# Signals are the OS's asynchronous notification mechanism. In
# smart-protocol, signals are typed (T.SignalKind), not integers.
# The shell, init system, and apps all use this contract.
#
# This schema is the non-kernel side of signals: handler registration,
# signal masking, real-time signal queues, and signal events. The
# kernel-side (delivery, dispatch) lives in kernel.capnp.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface SignalService {
    # Register a signal handler for the calling process.
    register @0 (kind :T.SignalKind, handler :SignalHandler) -> (handleId :UInt64);

    # Unregister a signal handler.
    unregister @1 (handleId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List registered handlers for the calling process.
    listHandlers @2 () -> (handlers :List(RegisteredHandler));

    # ── Signal Masking ─────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get the current signal mask.
    getMask @3 () -> (mask :SignalMask);

    # Set the signal mask (block/unblock signals).
    setMask @4 (mask :SignalMask) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Block specific signals.
    block @5 (signals :List(T.SignalKind)) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Unblock specific signals.
    unblock @6 (signals :List(T.SignalKind)) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Signal Sending ─────────────────────────────────────────

    # Send a signal to a process.
    send @7 (target :T.ProcessId, signal :T.SignalKind, data :Data) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Send a signal to a process group.
    sendGroup @8 (groupId :UInt32, signal :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Broadcast a signal to all processes.
    broadcast @9 (signal :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Send a real-time signal with payload.
    sendRt @10 (target :T.ProcessId, signalNumber :UInt8, payload :Data) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Signal Queue ───────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get pending signals for the calling process.
    getPending @11 () -> (pending :List(PendingSignal));

    # Clear pending signals.
    clearPending @12 (kind :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get signal queue info.
    getQueueInfo @13 () -> (info :SignalQueueInfo);

    # ── Signal Wait ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Wait for a specific signal (blocking).
    wait @14 (kind :T.SignalKind, timeout :T.Duration) -> (signal :PendingSignal);

    # Wait for any signal.
    waitAny @15 (timeout :T.Duration) -> (signal :PendingSignal);

    # ── Signal Events (non-blocking subscription) ──────────────

    # Subscribe to signals (for shell/event-driven use).
    subscribe @16 (filter :SignalFilter) -> (subscription :SignalSubscription);

    # ── Signal Information ─────────────────────────────────────

    # Get info about a signal kind.
    getInfo @17 (kind :T.SignalKind) -> (info :SignalInfo);

    # List all supported signal kinds.
    listSupported @18 () -> (signals :List(SignalInfo));
}

# ── Signal Handler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalHandler {
    union {
        # Default action (terminate, ignore, stop, continue).
        default @0 :Void;
        # Ignore the signal.
        ignore @1 :Void;
        # Run a callback (in-process).
        callback @2 :Data;
        # Forward to another process.
        forward @3 :T.ProcessId;
        # Log the signal.
        log @4 :Void;
        # Custom backend-defined action.
        custom @5 :Data;
    }
}

struct RegisteredHandler {
    handleId @0 :UInt64;
    kind @1 :T.SignalKind;
    handler @2 :SignalHandler;
    # How many times this handler has been invoked.
    invocationCount @3 :UInt64;
    # When the handler was registered.
    registeredAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Signal Mask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalMask {
    # Blocked signals.
    blocked @0 :List(T.SignalKind);
    # Pending-while-blocked signals.
    pending @1 :List(T.SignalKind);
}

# ── Pending Signal ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct PendingSignal {
    kind @0 :T.SignalKind;
    # Sending process.
    sender @1 :T.ProcessId;
    # When the signal was sent.
    sentAt @2 :T.Timestamp;
    # Opaque payload (for real-time signals).
    data @3 :Data;
    # Real-time signal number (for RT signals).
    rtNumber @4 :UInt8;
}

struct SignalQueueInfo {
    # Maximum queued signals.
    maxQueued @0 :UInt32;
    # Currently queued count.
    queued @1 :UInt32;
    # Signals dropped due to full queue.
    dropped @2 :UInt64;
}

# ── Signal Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalInfo {
    kind @0 :T.SignalKind;
    # Default action for this signal.
    defaultAction @1 :SignalDefaultAction;
    # Whether this signal can be caught.
    catchable @2 :Bool;
    # Whether this signal can be blocked.
    blockable @3 :Bool;
    # Whether this signal generates core dump.
    coreDump @4 :Bool;
    # Human-readable description.
    description @5 :Text;
    # Typical cause.
    typicalCause @6 :Text;
}

enum SignalDefaultAction {
    terminate @0;
    terminateAndCore @1;
    ignore @2;
    stop @3;
    continueProc @4;
    custom @5;
}

# ── Signal Filter & Subscription ─────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalFilter {
    # Only these signal kinds (empty = all).
    kinds @0 :List(T.SignalKind);
    # Only from these processes (empty = any).
    fromProcesses @1 :List(T.ProcessId);
    # Include data payload.
    includeData @2 :Bool;
}

interface SignalSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (signals :List(PendingSignal));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Boot — boot parameters, boot stages, boot splash, and recovery
#
# The boot contract is what the bootloader, kernel, and init system
# all agree on. It is backend-agnostic: EFI, coreboot, U-Boot, or
# a custom bootloader — the contract is the same.
#
# A/B slot management lives in kernel.capnp (KernelSwapService).
# This schema covers the user-facing boot surface.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface BootService {
    # Get boot information.
    getInfo @0 () -> (info :BootInfo);

    # Get boot parameters.
    getParameters @1 () -> (params :BootParameters);

    # Set boot parameters (for next boot).
    setParameters @2 (params :BootParameters) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Boot Entries ───────────────────────────────────────────

    # List boot entries (OS/kernel options).
    listEntries @3 () -> (entries :List(BootEntry));

    # Get the default boot entry.
    getDefaultEntry @4 () -> (entry :BootEntry);

    # Set the default boot entry.
    setDefaultEntry @5 (entryId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Set the boot entry for next boot only (one-shot).
    setNextBootEntry @6 (entryId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Boot Log ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get boot log.
    getBootLog @7 (filter :BootLogFilter) -> (entries :List(BootLogEntry), total :UInt32);

    # ── Boot Splash ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get boot splash configuration.
    getSplashConfig @8 () -> (config :BootSplashConfig);

    # Set boot splash configuration.
    setSplashConfig @9 (config :BootSplashConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Recovery ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Enter recovery mode on next boot.
    setRecoveryMode @10 (enable :Bool) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get recovery mode status.
    getRecoveryMode @11 () -> (enabled :Bool, reason :Text);

    # ── Secure Boot ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get secure boot status.
    getSecureBoot @12 () -> (status :SecureBootStatus);

    # List secure boot keys.
    listSecureBootKeys @13 () -> (keys :List(SecureBootKey));

    # ── Boot Counters ──────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get boot attempt counters (for A/B).
    getBootAttempts @14 () -> (attempts :BootAttempts);

    # Mark boot as successful (resets counter).
    markBootSuccessful @15 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Subscribe to boot events.
    subscribe @16 () -> (subscription :BootSubscription);
}

# ── Boot Info ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct BootInfo {
    # Current boot ID.
    bootId @0 :UInt64;
    # Boot method.
    method @1 :BootMethod;
    # Firmware type.
    firmware @2 :FirmwareType;
    # Firmware version.
    firmwareVersion @3 :Text;
    # Bootloader name.
    bootloader @4 :Text;
    # Bootloader version.
    bootloaderVersion @5 :Text;
    # Kernel command line.
    kernelCommandLine @6 :Text;
    # Boot duration (firmware to userspace).
    bootDuration @7 :T.Duration;
    # Whether this was a cold boot or warm boot.
    coldBoot @8 :Bool;
    # Architecture.
    architecture @9 :Text;
}

enum BootMethod {

    bios @1;
    coreboot @2;
    uboot @3;
    petitboot @4;
    custom @5;

struct BootParameters {

    # Default entry ID.

    # Architecture.

    # Whether this is the default entry.

    # Whether this is a recovery entry.

# ── Boot Log ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── Boot Splash ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SecureBootStatus {

    # Setup mode (user mode vs setup mode).

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Capability — the authority system
#
# Capabilities are how smart-protocol controls "who can do what."
# Every process holds a set of capabilities. Each capability grants
# specific operations on specific resources. Capabilities can be
# delegated, revoked, and audited.
#
# This is NOT POSIX permissions. This is NOT Unix DAC. This is a
# first-class capability system: unforgeable, delegatable, auditable,
# and typed. The wire format is T.CapabilityHandle (UInt64). The
# semantic is a typed grant with operations, scope, and expiry.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface CapabilityService {
    # Issue a new capability.
    issue @0 (request :IssueRequest) -> (handle :T.CapabilityHandle);

    # Revoke a capability.
    revoke @1 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Delegate a capability to another process (subset of operations).
    delegate @2 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle, request :DelegateRequest) -> (newHandle :T.CapabilityHandle);

    # Publish a capability to another process.
    publish @3 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle, recipient :T.ProcessId) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Query what a capability grants.
    inspect @4 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> (info :CapabilityInfo);

    # List capabilities held by the calling process.
    listHeld @5 () -> (capabilities :List(CapabilityInfo));

    # List capabilities published to another process.
    listPublished @6 (target :T.ProcessId) -> (capabilities :List(CapabilityInfo));

    # Check if the calling process has a specific capability.
    check @7 (resource :Text, operation :Operation) -> (allowed :Bool, reason :Text);

    # ── Capability Sets ────────────────────────────────────────

    # Create a capability set (group of capabilities).
    createSet @8 (name :Text, capabilities :List(T.CapabilityHandle)) -> (setId :UInt64);

    # Revoke an entire capability set.
    revokeSet @9 (setId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # List capability sets.
    listSets @10 () -> (sets :List(CapabilitySet));

    # ── Capability Templates ───────────────────────────────────

    # List available capability templates.
    listTemplates @11 () -> (templates :List(CapabilityTemplate));

    # Issue capabilities from a template.
    issueFromTemplate @12 (templateName :Text, recipient :T.ProcessId) -> (handle :T.CapabilityHandle);

    # ── Audit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get capability audit trail for a handle.
    getAuditTrail @13 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> (events :List(CapabilityEvent));

    # Subscribe to capability events.
    subscribe @14 (filter :CapabilityFilter) -> (subscription :CapabilitySubscription);

    # ── Proof Level ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get the proof level for a capability.
    getProofLevel @15 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> (proof :ProofInfo);

    # ── Capability Scoping ─────────────────────────────────────

    # Create a sandboxed capability scope.
    createScope @16 (config :ScopeConfig) -> (scopeId :UInt64);

    # Enter a capability scope.
    enterScope @17 (scopeId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Exit a capability scope.
    exitScope @18 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # List active scopes.
    listScopes @19 () -> (scopes :List(CapabilityScope));
}

# ── Issue Request ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct IssueRequest {
    # Resource identifier (e.g., "audio", "display/brightness", "file:/home/user/doc.txt").
    resource @0 :Text;
    # Operations granted.
    operations @1 :List(Operation);
    # Recipient process.
    recipient @2 :T.ProcessId;
    # Expiry (0 = no expiry).
    expiry @3 :T.Duration;
    # Maximum number of uses (0 = unlimited).
    maxUses @4 :UInt32;
    # Whether this capability can be delegated.
    delegatable @5 :Bool;
    # Maximum delegation depth (0 = no delegation allowed).
    maxDelegationDepth @6 :UInt32;
    # Scope (if restricted to a specific scope).
    scope @7 :UInt64;
    # Reason for issuance (audit).
    reason @8 :Text;
}

# ── Operations ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

enum Operation {
    read @0;
    write @1;
    execute @2;
    create @3;
    delete @4;
    list @5;
    subscribe @6;
    configure @7;
    admin @8;
    delegate @9;
    custom @10;
}

# ── Delegate Request ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DelegateRequest {
    # Operations to delegate (must be subset of parent).
    operations @0 :List(Operation);
    # Recipient process.
    recipient @1 :T.ProcessId;
    # Expiry (must be <= parent expiry).
    expiry @2 :T.Duration;
    # Maximum uses.
    maxUses @3 :UInt32;
    # Whether the recipient can further delegate.
    delegatable @4 :Bool;
    # Maximum further delegation depth.
    maxDelegationDepth @5 :UInt32;
}

# ── Capability Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityInfo {
    handle @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    # Resource identifier.
    resource @1 :Text;
    # Granted operations.
    operations @2 :List(Operation);
    # Issuing process.
    issuer @3 :T.ProcessId;
    # When issued.
    issuedAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
    # Expiry (null = no expiry).
    expiresAt @5 :T.Timestamp;
    # Remaining uses (0 = unlimited).
    remainingUses @6 :UInt32;
    # Whether this capability can be delegated.
    delegatable @7 :Bool;
    # Delegation depth from original issuer.
    delegationDepth @8 :UInt32;
    # Number of times this has been used.
    useCount @9 :UInt64;
    # Current scope (if scoped).
    scope @10 :UInt64;
}

# ── Capability Set ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilitySet {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    name @1 :Text;
    capabilities @2 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    # When this set was created.
    createdAt @3 :T.Timestamp;
    # Number of capabilities in the set.
    count @4 :UInt32;
}

# ── Capability Template ─────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityTemplate {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    # Default resources and operations.
    grants @2 :List(TemplateGrant);
    # Default expiry.
    defaultExpiry @3 :T.Duration;
    # Default delegation policy.
    delegatable @4 :Bool;
    # Category.
    category @5 :Text;
}

struct TemplateGrant {
    resource @0 :Text;
    operations @1 :List(Operation);
}

# ── Proof Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProofInfo {
    proofLevel @0 :ProofLevel;
    # Verification tool.
    verifier @1 :Text;
    # Specification hash.
    specHash @2 :Data;
    # When the proof was verified.
    verifiedAt @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum ProofLevel {
    unverified @0;
    tested @1;
    staticAnalysis @2;
    formalPartial @3;
    formalComplete @4;
    formalEndToEnd @5;
}

# ── Capability Scope ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityScope {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    name @1 :Text;
    # Capabilities active in this scope.
    capabilities @2 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    # Whether this scope is a sandbox.
    sandbox @3 :Bool;
    # When this scope was created.
    createdAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
    # Parent scope (if nested).
    parentScope @5 :UInt64;
}

struct ScopeConfig {
    name @0 :Text;
    # Whether to sandbox (isolate from outer scope).
    sandbox @1 :Bool;
    # Capabilities to include (empty = inherit all from parent).
    includeCapabilities @2 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    # Resources to deny (deny-by-default if sandboxed).
    denyResources @3 :List(Text);
    # Maximum capabilities in this scope.
    maxCapabilities @4 :UInt32;
}

# ── Capability Events ───────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityFilter {
    handles @0 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    operations @1 :List(Operation);
    since @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

interface CapabilitySubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(CapabilityEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct CapabilityEvent {
    union {
        issued @0 :CapabilityInfo;
        revoked @1 :T.CapabilityHandle;
        delegated @2 :DelegationEvent;
        published @3 :PublishEvent;
        used @4 :UseEvent;
        expired @5 :T.CapabilityHandle;
        scopeCreated @6 :CapabilityScope;
        scopeEntered @7 :UInt64;
        scopeExited @8 :UInt64;
        custom @9 :Data;
    }
}

struct DelegationEvent {
    parent @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    child @1 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    from @2 :T.ProcessId;
    to @3 :T.ProcessId;
    operations @4 :List(Operation);
    timestamp @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct PublishEvent {
    handle @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    from @1 :T.ProcessId;
    to @2 :T.ProcessId;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct UseEvent {
    handle @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    operation @1 :Operation;
    resource @2 :Text;
    pid @3 :T.ProcessId;
    success @4 :Bool;
    timestamp @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Process — process lifecycle, cgroups, namespaces, and resource
#           accounting beyond what kernel.capnp provides
#
# kernel.capnp owns the kernel-level process primitives (spawn, fork,
# exec, signal, memory regions). This schema owns the higher-level
# process management: cgroups, namespaces, resource accounting,
# process groups, sessions, and the process tree.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface ProcessService {
    # ── Process Info ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get detailed process info.
    getInfo @0 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (info :ProcessInfo);

    # List all processes matching a filter.
    list @1 (filter :ProcessFilter, pagination :T.Pagination) -> (processes :List(ProcessInfo), total :UInt32);

    # Get the process tree rooted at a PID.
    getTree @2 (rootPid :T.ProcessId) -> (tree :ProcessTree);

    # Get the full system process tree.
    getFullTree @3 () -> (tree :ProcessTree);

    # ── Process Lifecycle ──────────────────────────────────────

    # Kill a process.
    kill @4 (pid :T.ProcessId, signal :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Nice a process (change priority).
    renice @5 (pid :T.ProcessId, nice :Int8) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Suspend a process (SIGSTOP).
    suspend @6 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Resume a process (SIGCONT).
    resume @7 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Wait for a process to exit.
    waitProcess @8 (pid :T.ProcessId, timeout :T.Duration) -> (exitStatus :T.ExitStatus);

    # ── Process Groups & Sessions ──────────────────────────────

    # Get the process group for a PID.
    getProcessGroup @9 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (pgid :UInt32);

    # Set the process group for a PID.
    setProcessGroup @10 (pid :T.ProcessId, pgid :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get the session for a PID.
    getSession @11 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (sessionId :UInt32);

    # List sessions.
    listSessions @12 () -> (sessions :List(ProcessSession));

    # List process groups.
    listProcessGroups @13 () -> (groups :List(ProcessGroup));

    # ── Resource Accounting ────────────────────────────────────

    # Get resource usage for a process.
    getResourceUsage @14 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (usage :ProcessResourceUsage);

    # Get resource usage for a process group.
    getGroupResourceUsage @15 (pgid :UInt32) -> (usage :ProcessResourceUsage);

    # Get total system resource usage breakdown.
    getSystemResourceUsage @16 () -> (usage :SystemResourceUsage);

    # ── Cgroups ────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List cgroups.
    listCgroups @17 () -> (cgroups :List(CgroupInfo));

    # Get cgroup info.
    getCgroup @18 (path :Text) -> (info :CgroupInfo);

    # Create a cgroup.
    createCgroup @19 (path :Text, config :CgroupConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Delete a cgroup.
    deleteCgroup @20 (path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Move a process to a cgroup.
    moveToCgroup @21 (pid :T.ProcessId, cgroup :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get cgroup resource usage.
    getCgroupUsage @22 (path :Text) -> (usage :ProcessResourceUsage);

    # ── Namespaces ─────────────────────────────────────────────

    # List namespaces for a process.
    listNamespaces @23 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (namespaces :List(NamespaceInfo));

    # Get namespace details.
    getNamespace @24 (pid :T.ProcessId, type :NamespaceType) -> (info :NamespaceInfo);

    # ── Open Files & Connections ───────────────────────────────

    # List open files for a process.
    listOpenFiles @25 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (files :List(OpenFile));

    # List network connections for a process.
    listConnections @26 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (connections :List(ProcessConnection));

    # ── Environment ────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get environment variables for a process.
    getEnvironment @27 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (env :T.StringMap);

    # ── Events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Subscribe to process events.
    subscribe @28 (filter :ProcessEventFilter) -> (subscription :ProcessSubscription);
}

# ── Process Info ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessInfo {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    parentPid @1 :T.ProcessId;
    name @2 :Text;
    command @3 :Text;
    arguments @4 :List(Text);
    executable @5 :Text;
    workingDirectory @6 :Text;
    user @7 :Text;
    group @8 :Text;
    state @9 :ProcessState;
    nice @10 :Int8;
    priority @11 :Int32;
    # Process group ID.
    pgid @12 :UInt32;
    # Session ID.
    sessionId @13 :UInt32;
    # Controlling terminal.
    tty @14 :Text;
    # Resource usage.
    resourceUsage @15 :ProcessResourceUsage;
    # When the process started.
    startedAt @16 :T.Timestamp;
    # CPU time consumed.
    cpuTime @17 :T.Duration;
    # Thread count.
    threadCount @18 :UInt32;
    # Child processes.
    children @19 :List(T.ProcessId);
    # Cgroup.
    cgroup @20 :Text;
    # Capabilities held.
    capabilityCount @21 :UInt32;
    # Security context (SELinux/AppArmor label).
    securityContext @22 :Text;
}

enum ProcessState {
    running @0;
    sleeping @1;
    waiting @2;
    stopped @3;
    zombie @4;
    dead @5;
    traced @6;
    idle @7;
}

# ── Process Tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessTree {
    root @0 :ProcessTreeNode;
    totalProcesses @1 :UInt32;
    maxDepth @2 :UInt32;
}

struct ProcessTreeNode {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    name @1 :Text;
    state @2 :ProcessState;
    cpuPercent @3 :Float32;
    memoryBytes @4 :UInt64;
    children @5 :List(ProcessTreeNode);
    depth @6 :UInt32;
}

# ── Process Filter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessFilter {
    name @0 :Text;
    state @1 :ProcessState;
    user @2 :Text;
    minCpu @3 :Float32;
    maxCpu @4 :Float32;
    minMemory @5 :UInt64;
    maxMemory @6 :UInt64;
    cgroup @7 :Text;
    sessionId @8 :UInt32;
    pgid @9 :UInt32;
    tty @10 :Text;
}

# ── Resource Usage ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessResourceUsage {
    # CPU usage (0.0-1.0 per core, can exceed 1.0 for multi-threaded).
    cpuPercent @0 :Float32;
    # Resident memory (bytes).
    memoryRss @1 :UInt64;
    # Virtual memory (bytes).
    memoryVirtual @2 :UInt64;
    # Shared memory (bytes).
    memoryShared @3 :UInt64;
    # Memory usage percentage.
    memoryPercent @4 :Float32;
    # Swap usage (bytes).
    swapBytes @5 :UInt64;
    # Disk read bytes.
    diskReadBytes @6 :UInt64;
    # Disk write bytes.
    diskWriteBytes @7 :UInt64;
    # Network bytes sent.
    networkBytesSent @8 :UInt64;
    # Network bytes received.
    networkBytesReceived @9 :UInt64;
    # Open file descriptors.
    openFiles @10 :UInt32;
    # Thread count.
    threads @11 :UInt32;
    # Context switches (voluntary).
    contextSwitchesVoluntary @12 :UInt64;
    # Context switches (involuntary).
    contextSwitchesInvoluntary @13 :UInt64;
    # Page faults (minor).
    pageFaultsMinor @14 :UInt64;
    # Page faults (major).
    pageFaultsMajor @15 :UInt64;
    # I/O wait time.
    ioWaitTime @16 :T.Duration;
}

struct SystemResourceUsage {
    totalProcesses @0 :UInt32;
    totalThreads @1 :UInt32;
    cpuUsageTotal @2 :Float32;
    memoryUsed @3 :UInt64;
    memoryTotal @4 :UInt64;
    swapUsed @5 :UInt64;
    swapTotal @6 :UInt64;
    diskReadTotal @7 :UInt64;
    diskWriteTotal @8 :UInt64;
    networkTotal @9 :UInt64;
    # Top consumers.
    topCpu @10 :List(ProcessInfo);
    topMemory @11 :List(ProcessInfo);
    topDisk @12 :List(ProcessInfo);
    topNetwork @13 :List(ProcessInfo);
}

# ── Cgroup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CgroupInfo {
    path @0 :Text;
    # Processes in this cgroup.
    processCount @1 :UInt32;
    # Resource limits.
    config @2 :CgroupConfig;
    # Current resource usage.
    usage @3 :ProcessResourceUsage;
    # Child cgroups.
    children @4 :List(Text);
    # Whether this cgroup is frozen.
    frozen @5 :Bool;
}

struct CgroupConfig {
    # CPU weight (1-10000).
    cpuWeight @0 :UInt32;
    # CPU max (percentage * period, e.g., "50% 100000us").
    cpuMax @1 :Text;
    # Memory low (bytes).
    memoryLow @2 :UInt64;
    # Memory high (bytes).
    memoryHigh @3 :UInt64;
    # Memory max (bytes).
    memoryMax @4 :UInt64;
    # Memory swap max (bytes).
    memorySwapMax @5 :UInt64;
    # I/O weight.
    ioWeight @6 :UInt32;
    # PIDs max.
    pidsMax @7 :UInt32;
}

# ── Namespaces ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct NamespaceInfo {
    type @0 :NamespaceType;
    # Namespace ID (inode number).
    id @1 :UInt64;
    # Processes sharing this namespace.
    processes @2 :List(T.ProcessId);
    # Whether this is the initial namespace.
    initial @3 :Bool;
}

enum NamespaceType {
    pid @0;
    net @1;
    mount @2;
    uts @3;
    ipc @4;
    user @5;
    cgroup @6;
    time @7;
}

# ── Open Files & Connections ─────────────────────────────────────────

struct OpenFile {
    fd @0 :UInt32;
    path @1 :Text;
    type @2 :OpenFileType;
    mode @3 :Text;          # "r", "w", "rw"
    offset @4 :UInt64;
    size @5 :UInt64;
}

enum OpenFileType {
    regular @0;
    directory @1;
    socket @2;
    pipe @3;
    device @4;
    symlink @5;
    unknown @6;
}

struct ProcessConnection {
    fd @0 :UInt32;
    type @1 :ConnectionType;
    localAddress @2 :Text;
    localPort @3 :UInt16;
    remoteAddress @4 :Text;
    remotePort @5 :UInt16;
    state @6 :ConnectionState;
    protocol @7 :Text;
}

enum ConnectionType {
    tcp @0;
    udp @1;
    unix @2;
    netlink @3;
    custom @4;
}

enum ConnectionState {
    established @0;
    synSent @1;
    synRecv @2;
    finWait1 @3;
    finWait2 @4;
    timeWait @5;
    close @6;
    closeWait @7;
    lastAck @8;
    listen @9;
    closing @10;
}

# ── Process Session & Group ─────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessSession {
    sessionId @0 :UInt32;
    leader @1 :T.ProcessId;
    controllingTty @2 :Text;
    processes @3 :List(T.ProcessId);
    foregroundGroup @4 :UInt32;
}

struct ProcessGroup {
    pgid @0 :UInt32;
    leader @1 :T.ProcessId;
    session @2 :UInt32;
    processes @3 :List(T.ProcessId);
}

# ── Process Events ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessEventFilter {
    pids @0 :List(T.ProcessId);
    eventTypes @1 :List(ProcessEventKind);
    since @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum ProcessEventKind {
    spawned @0;
    exited @1;
    signaled @2;
    stopped @3;
    resumed @4;
    cgroupChanged @5;
    resourceExceeded @6;
    custom @7;
}

interface ProcessSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(ProcessEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct ProcessEvent {
    union {
        spawned @0 :ProcessInfo;
        exited @1 :ProcessExitEvent;
        signaled @2 :ProcessSignalEvent;
        stopped @3 :T.ProcessId;
        resumed @4 :T.ProcessId;
        resourceExceeded @5 :ResourceExceededEvent;
        custom @6 :Data;
    }
}

struct ProcessExitEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    exitStatus @1 :T.ExitStatus;
    timestamp @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct ProcessSignalEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    signal @1 :T.SignalKind;
    sender @2 :T.ProcessId;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct ResourceExceededEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    resource @1 :Text;
    limit @2 :UInt64;
    actual @3 :UInt64;
    timestamp @4 :T.Timestamp;
}

system.capnp (Enriched)
capnpcapnp@0xa1b2c3d4e5f60090;

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# System — system information, hardware details, and system-wide
#          operations
#
# The "what is this machine?" schema. Hardware, firmware, thermal,
# fans, power supply, chassis, and the identity of the system itself.
# Every "system info" tool reads from here. Every dashboard renders
# from here.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface SystemService {
    # Get system overview.
    getInfo @0 () -> (info :SystemInfo);

    # Get hostname.
    getHostname @1 () -> (hostname :Text);

    # Set hostname.
    setHostname @2 (hostname :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Hardware ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get CPU info.
    getCpuInfo @3 () -> (cpu :CpuInfo);

    # Get memory info.
    getMemoryInfo @4 () -> (memory :MemoryInfo);

    # Get swap info.
    getSwapInfo @5 () -> (swap :SwapInfo);

    # Get disk info.
    getDiskInfo @6 () -> (disks :List(DiskInfo>);

    # Get GPU info.
    getGpuInfo @7 () -> (gpus :List(GpuInfo>);

    # ── Thermal ────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get temperature sensors.
    getTemperatures @8 () -> (sensors :List<TemperatureSensor>);

    # Get fan speeds.
    getFans @9 () -> (fans :List<FanInfo>);

    # Get thermal zone info.
    getThermalZones @10 () -> (zones :List<ThermalZone>);

    # ── Power ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get power supply info.
    getPowerSupplies @11 () -> (supplies :List<PowerSupply>);

    # ── System State ───────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get system load averages.
    getLoad @12 () -> (load :LoadInfo);

    # Get uptime.
    getUptime @13 () -> (uptime :UptimeInfo);

    # Get logged-in users.
    getUsers @14 () -> (users :List<LoggedInUser>);

    # Get system time.
    getTime @15 () -> (time :SystemTime);

    # Set system time.
    setTime @16 (time :T.Timestamp) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Get timezone.
    getTimezone @17 () -> (timezone :TimezoneInfo);

    # Set timezone.
    setTimezone @18 (timezone :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # ── Firmware & BIOS ────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get firmware info.
    getFirmwareInfo @19 () -> (firmware :FirmwareInfo);

    # ── Chassis ────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get chassis info.
    getChassisInfo @20 () -> (chassis :ChassisInfo);

    # ── Kernel ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get kernel info.
    getKernelInfo @21 () -> (kernel :KernelInfo);

    # ── Architecture ───────────────────────────────────────────

    # Get architecture info.
    getArchitecture @22 () -> (arch :ArchitectureInfo);

    # ── Capabilities ───────────────────────────────────────────

    # List system capabilities.
    getCapabilities @23 () -> (capabilities :List(SystemCapability>);

    # ── Events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Subscribe to system events.
    subscribe @24 () -> (subscription :SystemSubscription);

    # ── Operations ─────────────────────────────────────────────

    # Shutdown the system.
    shutdown @25 (delay :T.Duration, reason :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Reboot the system.
    reboot @26 (delay :T.Duration, reason :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Suspend the system.
    suspend @27 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # Hibernate the system.
    hibernate @28 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # Cancel a pending shutdown/reboot.
    cancelShutdown @29 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── System Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SystemInfo {
    hostname @0 :Text;
    kernel @1 :Text;
    kernelVersion @2 :T.Version;
    architecture @3 :Text;
    os @4 :Text;
    osVersion @5 :T.Version;
    uptime @6 :T.Duration;
    bootTime @7 :T.Timestamp;
    cpu @8 :CpuInfo;
    memory @9 :MemoryInfo;
    swap @10 :SwapInfo;
    load @11 :LoadInfo;
    users @12 :UInt32;
    timezone @13 :Text;
    firmware @14 :Text;
    chassis @15 :Text;
}

# ── CPU Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CpuInfo {
    model @0 :Text;
    vendor @1 :Text;
    # Physical cores.
    cores @2 :UInt32;
    # Logical processors (threads).
    threads @3 :UInt32;
    # Base frequency (MHz).
    baseFrequency @4 :UInt64;
    # Max turbo frequency (MHz).
    maxFrequency @5 :UInt64;
    # Current frequency (MHz).
    currentFrequency @6 :UInt64;
    # Architecture.
    architecture @7 :Text;
    # Instruction set extensions.
    flags @8 :List(Text);
    # Cache sizes.
    cacheL1d @9 :UInt64;
    cacheL1i @10 :UInt64;
    cacheL2 @11 :UInt64;
    cacheL3 @12 :UInt64;
    # Sockets.
    sockets @13 :UInt32;
    # NUMA nodes.
    numaNodes @14 :UInt32;
    # Current temperature.
    temperature @15 :Float32;
    # CPU usage (0.0-1.0).
    usage @16 :Float32;
}

# ── Memory Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct MemoryInfo {
    totalBytes @0 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @1 :UInt64;
    availableBytes @2 :UInt64;
    freeBytes @3 :UInt64;
    cachedBytes @4 :UInt64;
    bufferBytes @5 :UInt64;
    sharedBytes @6 :UInt64;
    # Usage percentage.
    usagePercent @7 :Float32;
    # DIMM slots info.
    dimms @8 :List(DimmInfo>;
    # Maximum supported memory.
    maxCapacity @9 :UInt64;
}

struct DimmInfo {
    slot @0 :Text;
    sizeBytes @1 :UInt64;
    type @2 :Text;          # DDR4, DDR5, etc
    speed @3 :UInt64;       # MHz
    manufacturer @4 :Text;
    partNumber @5 :Text;
    # Whether this slot is populated.
    populated @6 :Bool;
}

# ── Swap Info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SwapInfo {
    totalBytes @0 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @1 :UInt64;
    freeBytes @2 :UInt64;
    usagePercent @3 :Float32;
    # Swap devices.
    devices @4 :List<SwapDevice>;
}

struct SwapDevice {
    device @0 :Text;
    sizeBytes @1 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @2 :UInt64;
    priority @3 :Int32;
}

# ── Disk Info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DiskInfo {
    device @0 :Text;
    model @1 :Text;
    vendor @2 :Text;
    serial @3 :Text;
    sizeBytes @4 :UInt64;
    type @5 :DiskType;
    # Rotational (HDD) or solid state (SSD).
    rotational @6 :Bool;
    # Interface type (SATA, NVMe, USB, etc).
    interface @7 :Text;
    # Temperature.
    temperature @8 :Float32;
    # Health percentage.
    healthPercent @9 :Float32;
    # Power-on hours.
    powerOnHours @10 :UInt64;
    # Total bytes written.
    totalWritten @11 :UInt64;
    # Partition count.
    partitionCount @12 :UInt32;
    # SMART status.
    smartStatus @13 :SmartStatus;
}

enum DiskType {
    hdd @0;
    ssd @1;
    nvme @2;
    emmc @3;
    usb @4;
    optical @5;
    custom @6;
}

enum SmartStatus {
    ok @0;
    degraded @1;
    failing @2;
    unknown @3;
}

# ── GPU Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct GpuInfo {
    model @0 :Text;
    vendor @1 :Text;
    # VRAM total bytes.
    vramBytes @2 :UInt64;
    # VRAM used bytes.
    vramUsedBytes @3 :UInt64;
    # GPU usage (0.0-1.0).
    usage @4 :Float32;
    # Temperature.
    temperature @5 :Float32;
    # Fan speed (RPM).
    fanSpeed @6 :UInt32;
    # Power consumption (watts).
    powerWatts @7 :Float32;
    # Driver version.
    driverVersion @8 :Text;
    # PCI address.
    pciAddress @9 :Text;
    # Whether this is the primary GPU.
    primary @10 :Bool;
}

# ── Temperature Sensor ───────────────────────────────────────────────

struct TemperatureSensor {
    name @0 :Text;
    # Current temperature (Celsius).
    temperature @1 :Float32;
    # High threshold.
    high @2 :Float32;
    # Critical threshold.
    critical @3 :Float32;
    # Sensor type (cpu, gpu, motherboard, etc).
    type @4 :Text;
    # Whether throttling is active.
    throttleActive @5 :Bool;
}

# ── Fan Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct FanInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    # Current speed (RPM).
    speed @1 :UInt32;
    # Maximum speed (RPM).
    maxSpeed @2 :UInt32;
    # Whether the fan is controllable.
    controllable @3 :Bool;
    # Current fan mode.
    mode @4 :FanMode;
}

enum FanMode {
    auto @0;
    manual @1;
    fullSpeed @2;
    quiet @3;
    custom @4;
}

# ── Thermal Zone ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ThermalZone {
    name @0 :Text;
    type @1 :Text;
    temperature @2 :Float32;
    # Trip points.
    tripPoints @3 :List<TripPoint>;
    # Current policy.
    policy @4 :Text;
}

struct TripPoint {
    temperature @0 :Float32;
    type @1 :TripPointType;
    action @2 :Text;
}

enum TripPointType {
    passive @0;
    active @1;
    hot @2;
    critical @3;
}

# ── Power Supply ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct PowerSupply {
    name @0 :Text;
    type @1 :PowerSupplyType;
    # Whether this supply is online.
    online @2 :Bool;
    # Status (charging, discharging, full, not charging).
    status @3 :Text;
    # Current capacity (percentage).
    capacity @4 :Float32;
    # Voltage (millivolts).
    voltage @5 :UInt32;
    # Current (milliamps).
    current @6 :Int32;
    # Power (microwatts).
    power @7 :UInt64;
    # Energy full (microwatt-hours).
    energyFull @8 :UInt64;
    # Energy now (microwatt-hours).
    energyNow @9 :UInt64;
    # Health percentage.
    health @10 :Float32;
    # Cycle count.
    cycleCount @11 :UInt32;
    # Manufacturer.
    manufacturer @12 :Text;
    # Model name.
    modelName @13 :Text;
    # Serial number.
    serialNumber @14 :Text;
    # Technology (Li-ion, Li-poly, etc).
    technology @15 :Text;
    # Time to empty (seconds, if discharging).
    timeToEmpty @16 :UInt32;
    # Time to full (seconds, if charging).
    timeToFull @17 :UInt32;
    # Temperature (tenths of degree Celsius).
    temperature @18 :Float32;
}

enum PowerSupplyType {
    battery @0;
    mains @1;
    usb @2;
    wireless @3;
    custom @4;
}

# ── Load Info ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct LoadInfo {
    # 1-minute load average.
    load1 @0 :Float32;
    # 5-minute load average.
    load5 @1 :Float32;
    # 15-minute load average.
    load15 @2 :Float32;
    # Number of running processes.
    running @3 :UInt32;
    # Total processes.
    total @4 :UInt32;
    # Last PID.
    lastPid @5 :UInt32;
}

# ── Uptime Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct UptimeInfo {
    # System uptime.
    uptime @0 :T.Duration;
    # Idle time (sum across all CPUs).
    idleTime @1 :T.Duration;
    # Boot time.
    bootTime @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Logged-in User ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct LoggedInUser {
    user @0 :Text;
    # Login terminal.
    terminal @1 :Text;
    # Remote host (if SSH).
    host @2 :Text;
    # Login time.
    loginTime @3 :T.Timestamp;
    # Idle time.
    idleTime @4 :T.Duration;
}

# ── System Time ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SystemTime {
    local @0 :T.Timestamp;
    utc @1 :T.Timestamp;
    timezone @2 :Text;
    # Hardware clock time.
    hardwareClock @3 :T.Timestamp;
    # Whether NTP synchronized.
    ntpSynced @4 :Bool;
    # NTP server.
    ntpServer @5 :Text;
    # Clock source.
    clockSource @6 :Text;
    # Clock drift (ppm).
    driftPpm @7 :Float32;
}

struct TimezoneInfo {
    name @0 :Text;           # IANA timezone name
    abbreviation @1 :Text;   # e.g., "CEST"
    utcOffset @2 :Int32;     # Seconds from UTC
    dstActive @3 :Bool;      # Whether DST is currently active
    dstOffset @4 :Int32;     # DST offset in seconds
}

# ── Firmware Info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct FirmwareInfo {
    type @0 :Text;           # UEFI, BIOS, etc
    vendor @1 :Text;
    version @2 :Text;
    date @3 :Text;
    # SMBIOS/DMI version.
    smbiosVersion @4 :Text;
}

# ── Chassis Info ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ChassisInfo {
    manufacturer @0 :Text;
    model @1 :Text;
    serial @2 :Text;
    type @3 :ChassisType;
    # Asset tag.
    assetTag @4 :Text;
}

enum ChassisType {
    desktop @0;
    laptop @1;
    server @2;
    tablet @3;
    phone @4;
    embedded @5;
    virtual @6;
    custom @7;
}

# ── Kernel Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct KernelInfo {
    name @0 :Text;           # e.g., "smart-kernel", "linux"
    version @1 :T.Version;
    release @2 :Text;        # Full release string
    architecture @3 :Text;
    # Build date.
    buildDate @4 :Text;
    # Compiler used.
    compiler @5 :Text;
    # Kernel type (from kernel.capnp KernelType enum).
    type @6 :Text;
    # Command line.
    commandLine @7 :Text;
}

# ── Architecture Info ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ArchitectureInfo {
    cpuArch @0 :Text;        # x86_64, aarch64, riscv64
    byteOrder @1 :Text;      # little-endian, big-endian
    addressSize @2 :UInt32;  # 32 or 64
    # Supported instruction sets.
    instructionSets @3 :List(Text>;
    # Virtualization support.
    virtualization @4 :Bool;
    # Hypervisor (if VM).
    hypervisor @5 :Text;
}

# ── System Capability ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SystemCapability {
    name @0 :Text;
    available @1 :Bool;
    description @2 :Text;
    version @3 :Text;
}

# ── System Events ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface SystemSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(SystemEvent>);
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct SystemEvent {
    union {
        hostnameChanged @0 :Text;
        timezoneChanged @1 :Text;
        temperatureAlert @2 :TemperatureAlertEvent;
        fanAlert @3 :FanAlertEvent;
        powerEvent @4 :PowerEvent;
        shutdownScheduled @5 :ShutdownScheduledEvent;
        shutdownCancelled @6 :Void;
        userLogin @7 :LoggedInUser;
        userLogout @8 :Text;
        custom @9 :Data;
    }
}

struct TemperatureAlertEvent {
    sensor @0 :Text;
    temperature @1 :Float32;
    threshold @2 :Float32;
    throttleActive @3 :Bool;
    timestamp @4 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct FanAlertEvent {
    fan @0 :Text;
    speed @1 :UInt32;
    maxSpeed @2 :UInt32;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct PowerEvent {
    type @0 :PowerEventType;
    # Battery level (if applicable).
    batteryLevel @1 :Float32;
    timestamp @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum PowerEventType {
    acConnected @0;
    acDisconnected @1;
    batteryLow @2;
    batteryCritical @3;
    batteryFull @4;
    chargerConnected @5;
    chargerDisconnected @6;
}

struct ShutdownScheduledEvent {
    action @0 :ShutdownAction;
    scheduledAt @1 :T.Timestamp;
    delay @2 :T.Duration;
    reason @3 :Text;
}

enum ShutdownAction {
    shutdown @0;
    reboot @1;
    suspend @2;
    hibernate @3;
}

Batch 0: Foundation CLI Methods
bashbash# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# BATCH 0: FOUNDATION
# The universal primitives every domain uses
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── SHELL ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Shell state
shell                              # show shell state (session, mode, uptime, commands run)
shell mode                         # get current mode
shell mode guided                  # switch to guided mode
shell mode interactive             # switch to interactive mode
shell mode script                  # switch to script mode

# Prompt
shell prompt                       # show current prompt config
shell prompt template              # show prompt template
shell prompt set "❯ "              # set prompt character
shell prompt git on                # show git branch in prompt
shell prompt battery on            # show battery in prompt
shell prompt duration on           # show command duration
shell prompt time on               # show time in prompt

UX Rules (Universal)
texttext╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  UX RULES — Every command follows these                            ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                      ║
║  1. SAFE BY DEFAULT                                                  ║
║     • Destructive commands require confirmation                      ║
║     • Use --force / -y to skip confirmation                          ║
║     • Always show what will change before changing it                ║
║     • Every change is undoable (if the domain supports it)           ║
║                                                                      ║
║  2. READABLE BY HUMANS                                               ║
║     • Beautiful formatted output (tables, trees, progress bars)      ║
║     • Icons: ✓ success, ✗ error, ⚠ warning, ◉ active, ○ inactive  ║
║     • Progress bars for long operations                              ║
║     • Spinners for indeterminate operations                          ║
║     • Color: green=ok, red=error, yellow=warn, blue=info, dim=muted ║
║                                                                      ║
║  3. PARSABLE BY MACHINES                                             ║
║     • --json flag on every command                                   ║
║     • --tsv flag for tab-separated values                            ║
║     • --capnp flag for raw Cap'n Proto binary                       ║
║     • --minimal flag for values only (no decoration)                 ║
║     • --quiet flag for scripting (suppress confirmations)            ║
║                                                                      ║
║  4. CONSISTENT ACROSS ALL DOMAINS                                    ║
║     • domain → show state                                            ║
║     • domain property → read value                                   ║
║     • domain property value → write value                            ║
║     • domain action → perform action                                 ║
║     • domains → list all                                             ║
║     • domain where condition → filter                                ║
║     • watch domain → stream changes                                  ║
║     • @domain/property → selector                                    ║
║                                                                      ║
║  5. ERRORS ARE TEACHERS, NOT WALLS                                   ║
║     • Show what went wrong                                           ║
║     • Show why it went wrong                                         ║
║     • Show what to try next                                          ║
║     • Show a working example                                         ║
║     • Never just "Error: operation failed"                           ║
║                                                                      ║
║  6. NON-TECHNICAL USERS ARE FIRST-CLASS                              ║
║     • 'guide' mode for step-by-step interactive                      ║
║     • 'ask' for natural language                                     ║
║     • 'tutorial' for learning any domain                             ║
║     • 'cheat-sheet' for quick reference                              ║
║     • 'suggest' for contextual help                                  ║
║     • Tab completion everywhere                                      ║
║     • ? shows help for current context                               ║
║                                                                      ║
║  7. EVERYTHING IS OBSERVABLE                                         ║
║     • 'watch' on every domain                                        ║
║     • 'status' shows full system dashboard                           ║
║     • 'health' shows system health                                   ║
║     • 'alerts' shows active alerts                                   ║
║     • 'history' records everything                                   ║
║                                                                      ║
║  8. REMOTE IS TRANSPARENT                                            ║
║     • @server1 command works everywhere                              ║
║     • No special syntax for remote vs local                          ║
║     • Remote machines auto-discover via protocol                     ║
║     • Same output, same UX, same everything                          ║
║                                                                      ║
║  9. PRIVILEGE IS EXPLICIT                                            ║
║     • Capabilities are typed, not booleans                           ║
║     • Commands say what capability they need                         ║
║     • Expired capabilities produce clear errors                      ║
║     • Delegation chain is auditable                                  ║
║                                                                      ║
║ 10. THE SHELL LEARNS                                                 ║
║     • Frequently used commands → suggest bookmarking                 ║
║     • Patterns detected → suggest aliases                            ║
║     • Errors repeated → suggest fixes                                ║
║     • Resource trends → predictive alerts                            ║
║                                                                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

texttext┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  EDGE CASES — What happens when things go sideways                    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                       │
│  SHELL                                                               │
│  ├─ Undo after 50 commands — memory bounded by maxUndoLevels          │
│  ├─ Script running when user exits shell — background job survives    │
│  ├─ Natural language interpreted wrong — requires confirmation first  │
│  ├─ Guided mode user cancels mid-flow — clean state, no partial ops   │
│  ├─ Shell snapshot with remote variables — snapshot includes host     │
│  ├─ Tab completion with 10,000 results — paginated with filter        │
│  ├─ History grows to 1M entries — automatic rotation with pinned kept │
│  ├─ Two shells editing same variable — last-write-wins with warning   │
│  ├─ Bookmark references a removed service — clear error on run        │
│  └─ Undo of a command that was itself an undo — redo stack handling   │
│                                                                       │
│  SYSTEM                                                              │
│  ├─ Set hostname with special characters — validated, rejected if bad │
│  ├─ DIMM info not available (VM) — gracefully shows "N/A"             │

│  ├─ Fan control not supported — shows "not controllable" clearly      │
│  ├─ Set timezone to invalid value — suggests closest match            │
│  ├─ Shutdown during active capability delegation — capabilities clean │
│  ├─ Shutdown during service starting — graceful stop with timeout     │
│  ├─ Multiple power supply (UPS + battery) — shows both independently  │
│  ├─ NTP server unreachable — falls back to hardware clock with warning│
│  └─ System time set backwards — warns about cron/timer implications   │
│                                                                       │
│  PROCESS                                                             │
│  ├─ Zombie process — can query exit status before reaping             │
│  ├─ Process disappears during query — returns "process not found"     │
│  ├─ Kill zombie — "zombie processes cannot be killed, wait for parent" │
│  ├─ Process in multiple cgroups — shows all cgroups, primary listed   │
│  ├─ Open file count exceeds ulimit — shows limit, suggests increase   │
│  ├─ Process tree is 50 levels deep — paginated with depth limit       │
│  ├─ Process with 10,000 open files — paginated with search            │
│  ├─ Set nice on RT process — "nice is for fair-scheduled processes"   │
│  ├─ Process in container namespace — shows both container and host PID │
