│                                                                       │
│  INIT / SERVICES                                                     │
│  ├─ Circular dependency in services — detected and reported           │
│  ├─ Service fails to start — retry with backoff, then failed state    │
│  ├─ Socket activation during high load — connection queue manages     │
│  ├─ Timer missed (system was suspended) — catches up if persistent    │
│  ├─ Boot critical path changes — recomputed on each boot              │
│  ├─ Emergency mode entered — minimal services only, clear indication  │
│  ├─ Service masked but dependency requires it — clear error message   │
│  ├─ Boot history with 1000 entries — paginated, searchable            │
│  ├─ Service log buffer full — oldest entries rotated, not dropped     │
│  └─ Timer fires during shutdown — skipped, logged as missed           │
│                                                                       │
│  KERNEL                                                              │
│  ├─ Kernel introspect during high load — snapshot consistency         │
│  ├─ IRQ not available — clear "IRQ not supported on this system"      │
│  ├─ Port I/O on VM — "port I/O requires physical hardware"            │
│  ├─ Kernel swap during active processes — process state preserved     │
│  ├─ Mesh node goes offline — capabilities re-routed, event emitted    │
│  ├─ Watchdog timeout — process killed, event logged, alert raised     │
│  ├─ MSI allocation fails — falls back to legacy interrupt, warning    │
│  ├─ A/B slot max attempts exceeded — falls back to other slot         │
│  └─ Kernel extension incompatible — version check before install      │
│                                                                       │
│  SCHEDULER                                                           │
│  ├─ Set affinity to offline CPU — "CPU 7 is offline, choose another"  │
│  ├─ NUMA policy on non-NUMA system — "NUMA not available"             │
│  ├─ RT bandwidth exceeded — process throttled, event emitted          │
│  ├─ Deadline scheduling on non-RT kernel — "not supported"            │
│  ├─ Scheduler topology change during affinity set — atomic operation  │
│  ├─ Cgroup config exceeds system limits — validated before apply      │
│  └─ Load balance during critical section — deferred until safe        │
│                                                                       │
│  DIAGNOSTICS                                                         │
│  ├─ Health check takes too long — timeout with partial results        │
│  ├─ Alert threshold set to unreachable value — warning on configure   │
│  ├─ Profile with no data — "no measurable activity during profile"    │
│  ├─ Self-test modifies state — destructive tests require confirmation │
│  ├─ Prediction with low confidence — "uncertain, monitor recommended" │
│  ├─ Report generation during system stress — deferred or degraded     │
│  └─ Multiple simultaneous profiles — allowed, independent tracking    │
│                                                                       │
│  BOOT                                                               │
│  ├─ Boot entry kernel not found — "entry not bootable" clearly shown  │
│  ├─ Secure boot with unsigned kernel — blocked with explanation       │
│  ├─ Recovery mode entered automatically (crash recovery) — logged     │
│  ├─ Set next boot entry that doesn't exist — "entry not found"        │
│  ├─ Boot splash with missing theme — falls back to text mode          │
│  ├─ Boot parameters with invalid kernel args — warning, not blocked   │
│  └─ Boot attempts exceeded for A/B slot — automatic fallback          │
│                                                                       │
│  SIGNAL                                                              │
│  ├─ Signal queue full — oldest signal dropped, event emitted          │
│  ├─ Register handler for uncatchable signal — "cannot catch KILL"     │

│  ├─ Capability expired mid-operation — "capability expired at 14:30"  │

Thought for 21.9 secondsYou're raising exactly the right questions. Let me think through each one honestly — because you're right, once we ship this, it's permanent.

The info Question
You caught something real. Look at the inconsistency:
bashbashsystem            # shows system overview
system info       # shows... the same thing but more?
kernel            # shows kernel info
kernel info       # redundant
The fix: the base command IS the info. Always.
texttextRULE: domain = READ state (the full picture)
      domain property = READ specific value
      domain property value = WRITE
      domain action = DO something
So:
bashbashsystem              → full system state (the detailed version)
system hostname     → specific property
system hostname "x" → write

kernel              → full kernel state
kernel type         → specific property

scheduler           → full scheduler state
scheduler topology  → specific property

boot                → full boot state
boot entries        → specific property/list
No info anywhere. The base command IS the info. This is cleaner, more consistent, and a user who learns system learns kernel automatically. One rule. Every domain.
But — system currently shows a dashboard summary AND detailed info depending on how you wrote it. The question is: should system show the dashboard or the detailed info?
My take: system shows everything. If the user wants less, they target a property. The shell should paginate long output naturally. And if they're in a script, they use --minimal or --format toml.
bashbashsystem              → full detailed system info (everything)
system cpu          → just CPU
system memory       → just memory
system hostname     → just hostname string
No summary-vs-detail split. One command, full transparency.

The resources Question
You're right to question it. Let's look:
bashbashresources              → system-wide resource breakdown
resources top cpu      → top CPU consumers
resources top memory   → top memory consumers
resources top disk     → top disk consumers
resources top network  → top network consumers
The top variants are awkward. Here's why: resources already shows the breakdown including top consumers. Adding resources top cpu is like saying "show me resources but only the CPU part" — which is just a filter.
Better approach: resources shows everything including top consumers, and if you want to filter, you use pipes:
bashbashresources                          → full breakdown with top consumers
processes sort cpu desc take 5     → top 5 CPU consumers (already works)
Kill resources top. Keep resources clean. One command. The pipe system handles filtering. The user who wants top CPU consumers already knows processes sort cpu desc.
But what about resources vs having resource info in system? Right now system memory shows memory info. Is resources separate?
I think they serve different purposes:system memory = hardware info (total DIMMs, type, speed, max capacity)resources = live usage info (who's using what right now)
So both have a place. But resources top X should die.

Custom / Cross-Domain Commands
You asked a great question. Not everything belongs to a schema domain. Some commands are pure shell intelligence — they combine data from multiple domains to answer real questions.
Here's how I'd categorize all commands:
Three Types of Commands
texttextTYPE 1: Domain Commands (from schemas)
  system, kernel, processes, services, scheduler, boot, signals,
  capabilities, diagnostics, etc.
  These map directly to a capnp schema.

TYPE 2: Shell Commands (from shell.capnp / cli.capnp)
  history, aliases, vars, env, jobs, undo, bookmarks, watchers,
  snapshots, guide, ask, tutorial, suggest, cheat-sheet, script
  These are shell infrastructure.

TYPE 3: Hybrid Commands (cross-domain intelligence)
  why slow, what changed, what will fail, is it safe,
  prepare presentation, optimize battery, debug <service>,
  compare boots, network status, status, who accessed my files
  These don't come from any single schema. They're intelligence
  the shell provides by querying multiple schemas and synthesizing.
Type 3 is what makes this shell unprecedented. No bash script can do why slow — it would need to grep 15 different files and parse text. Our shell calls 5 protocol methods and structures the data.
But here's the question: how do users discover Type 3 commands?
They don't fit in any domain. A user who types domains sees system, kernel, audio — but not why slow or status.
My proposal:
bashbash# Type 3 commands live under "smart" namespace or just work bare:

smart                            # list all cross-domain commands
smart status                     # system dashboard
smart why slow                   # performance analysis
smart what changed               # change report
smart optimize battery           # battery optimization
smart prepare presentation       # presentation mode
smart debug nginx                # service debugging
smart compare boots              # boot comparison

# OR — just make them top-level (my preference):
status                           # dashboard
why slow                         # performance analysis
what changed                     # changes
optimize battery                 # battery optimization
I prefer top-level. These are the most-used commands. Putting them under smart adds friction. A user should be able to type status and get the dashboard. Period.

The Numeric ID Pattern
You liked system gpu 0. The pattern extends naturally:
bashbash# Numeric IDs for indexed items:
system gpu 0                     → first GPU
system gpu 1                     → second GPU
system disk sda                  → specific disk (by device name)
system disk 0                    → first disk (by index)
system dimm 0                    → first DIMM slot
system fan 0                     → first fan
system temperature 0             → first temperature sensor

process 1842                     → process by PID
window 3                         → window by ID
service nginx                    → service by name
workspace 2                      → workspace by number

# Plural = list, singular + ID = specific:
fans                             → list all fans
fan 0                            → specific fan
fan 0 speed                      → fan speed property
fan 0 speed 2000                 → set fan speed

disks                            → list all disks
disk sda                         → specific disk
disk sda temperature             → disk temperature

gpus                             → list all GPUs
gpu 0                            → specific GPU
gpu 0 temperature                → GPU temperature
gpu 0 temperature --watch        → stream GPU temperature
The rule: plural for lists, singular + identifier for specific items. Works with numbers, names, or device identifiers. Consistent everywhere.

Quick Design Chat
On your points, honestly:
"do we need resources top?" — No. Kill it. resources shows everything including top consumers. Filtering is what pipes are for. processes sort cpu desc take 5 handles the "show me top CPU" case already. resources top cpu is redundant abstraction.
"isn't resources good alone?" — Yes. resources is one command that shows the live usage picture. system shows the hardware/static picture. They complement each other. No overlap.
"custom commands / cross-domain" — They should be top-level, bare commands. status, why slow, optimize battery, debug nginx. These are the most human-friendly commands in the shell. Burying them under a namespace kills discoverability.
"GPU 0" — This pattern is gold. Extends to everything. fan 0, dimm 0, disk 0, sensor 0, temperature 0. Combined with named identifiers (disk sda, service nginx), it covers every access pattern.
"format agnostic" — Critical. Default is human. Every format available on every command. TOML, YAML, CSV, TSV, TXT, MD, JSON, Cap'n Proto, Raw. No format is privileged. This is what "agnostic" means — and it's what makes the shell timeless.
"errors like Rust" — This is non-negotiable. Every error tells you what went wrong, why, and what to try. No exceptions. This is UX 101 and most CLIs fail at it.

The One Nuance: Three Command Types
info applies to domain commands (backed by schemas). But not everything is a domain command. There are three types:

Syntax Contract (Permanent)
texttext╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  SMART-SHELL SYNTAX — THE PERMANENT CONTRACT                             ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                          ║
║  DOMAIN COMMANDS (schema-backed):                                        ║
║  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ║
║  domain info               → full state (the ONE way to see everything)  ║
║  domain property           → read a specific value                       ║
║  domain property value     → write a value                               ║
║  domain action             → perform an action                           ║
║  domains (plural)          → list all items                              ║
║  domain id                 → target a specific item                      ║
║  domain id info            → full state of specific item                 ║
║  domain id property        → read specific item's property               ║
║  domain id property value  → set specific item's property                ║
║  domain where condition    → filter a list                               ║
║  watch domain              → stream changes                              ║
║  @domain/property          → selector                                    ║
║                                                                          ║
║  SHELL BUILTINS (infrastructure):                                        ║
║  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ║
║  command                   → show all (history, jobs, aliases, etc.)     ║
║                                                                          ║
║  HYBRID COMMANDS (cross-domain intelligence):                            ║
║  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ║
║  command                   → execute (status, why slow, debug, etc.)     ║
║                                                                          ║
║  UNIVERSAL FLAGS (every command):                                        ║
║  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ║
║  --format <type>           → human|json|toml|yaml|md|csv|tsv|txt|raw    ║
║  --json / --toml / etc     → shorthand for --format                     ║
║  --quiet                   → suppress confirmations (for scripts)        ║
║  --force / -y              → skip safety prompts                         ║
║  --remote <host>           → run on remote machine                       ║
║  --help                    → show help for this command                  ║
║                                                                          ║
║  RULES:                                                                  ║
║  • info = the universal "full state" verb. Always. Every nesting level.  ║
║  • No abbreviations. Full words always.                                  ║
║  • No arguments on a domain verb = do the default action of that verb.   ║
║  • Plural = list. Singular + id = specific item.                         ║
║  • Errors always show: what happened, why, what to try.                  ║
║  • Default output format is always human (beautiful formatted).          ║
║                                                                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

texttext╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  UX RULES — Every command follows these. No exceptions.                  ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                          ║
║  1. SAFE BY DEFAULT                                                      ║
║     Destructive commands require confirmation.                           ║
║     Use --force / -y to skip. Always show what will change first.        ║
║                                                                          ║
║  2. READABLE BY HUMANS                                                   ║
║     Beautiful formatted output. Icons: ✓ ✗ ⚠ ◉ ○ ● ▶                   ║
║     Progress bars. Spinners. Color: green/red/yellow/blue/dim.           ║
║                                                                          ║
║  3. PARSABLE BY MACHINES                                                 ║
║     --format on every command. human|json|toml|yaml|md|csv|tsv|          ║
║     txt|raw|capnp. Default: human.                                       ║
║                                                                          ║
║  4. CONSISTENT ACROSS ALL DOMAINS                                        ║
║     Same syntax everywhere. info, property, action, list, filter,        ║
║     watch, selector. One pattern, every domain.                          ║
║                                                                          ║
║  5. ERRORS ARE TEACHERS                                                  ║
║     Every error: what happened + why + what to try + example.            ║

║                                                                          ║
║  6. NON-TECHNICAL USERS ARE FIRST-CLASS                                  ║
║     guide (step-by-step), ask (natural language), tutorial,              ║
║     suggest (contextual), cheat-sheet. Tab completion everywhere.        ║
║                                                                          ║
║  7. EVERYTHING IS OBSERVABLE                                             ║
║     watch on every domain. status shows dashboard. health shows          ║
║     system health. alerts shows active alerts.                           ║
║                                                                          ║
║  8. REMOTE IS TRANSPARENT                                                ║
║     @server1 command works everywhere. Same UX, same everything.         ║
║                                                                          ║
║  9. PRIVILEGE IS EXPLICIT                                                ║
║     Capabilities are typed. Commands declare what capability they        ║
║     need. Expired capabilities produce clear errors with path forward.   ║
║                                                                          ║
║ 10. THE SHELL LEARNS                                                     ║
║     Frequently used → suggest bookmark. Patterns → suggest alias.        ║
║     Errors repeated → suggest fix. Resource trends → predictive alert.   ║
║                                                                          ║
║ 11. THE USER ALWAYS WINS                                                 ║
║     Every dead end has a door. Every error has a suggestion. Every       ║

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Shell — the universal interactive environment
#
# Not a terminal emulator. The shell itself: the environment that
# interprets commands, manages state, handles completion, and
# provides the interactive experience. Backend-agnostic: could run
# on a VT100, graphical terminal, phone screen, spaceship console,
# or voice interface. The shell IS the OS interface.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface ShellService {
    # Shell state
    getState @0 () -> (state :ShellState);
    start @1 (config :ShellConfig) -> (session :ShellSession);
    end @2 (sessionId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Execution
    execute @3 (input :CommandInput) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # Natural language interpretation
    interpret @4 (request :NaturalLanguageRequest) -> (interpreted :InterpretedCommand);
    confirmAndExecute @5 (interpreted :InterpretedCommand, confirm :Bool) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # Completion
    complete @6 (input :Text, cursorPosition :UInt32) -> (completions :List(Completion));
    completeSelector @7 (selector :Text) -> (completions :List(SelectorCompletion));
    completeDomain @8 (domain :Text, partial :Text) -> (completions :List(DomainCompletion));

    # History
    getHistory @9 (filter :HistoryFilter, pagination :T.Pagination) -> (entries :List(HistoryEntry), totalCount :UInt32);
    searchHistory @10 (pattern :Text, pagination :T.Pagination) -> (entries :List(HistoryEntry), totalCount :UInt32);
    clearHistory @11 () -> T.VoidResult;
    pinHistoryEntry @12 (entryId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Aliases
    setAlias @13 (name :Text, expansion :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    removeAlias @14 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listAliases @15 () -> (aliases :List(Alias));

    # Variables
    setVariable @16 (name :Text, value :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    getVariable @17 (name :Text) -> (value :Text, exists :Bool);
    listVariables @18 () -> (variables :List(ShellVariable));

    # Environment
    getEnv @19 (name :Text) -> (value :Text, exists :Bool);
    setEnv @20 (name :Text, value :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listEnv @21 () -> (env :List(EnvVariable));

    # Jobs
    listJobs @22 () -> (jobs :List(Job));
    fg @23 (jobId :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;
    bg @24 (jobId :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;
    cancelJob @25 (jobId :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;
    waitForJob @26 (jobId :UInt32, timeout :T.Duration) -> (result :CommandResult);

    # Undo / Redo
    undo @27 () -> (result :UndoResult);
    redo @28 () -> (result :UndoResult);
    getUndoStack @29 () -> (stack :List(UndoEntry));
    isUndoable @30 (command :Text) -> (undoable :Bool, description :Text);
    registerUndoable @31 (operation :UndoableOperation) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Prompt
    getPrompt @32 () -> (prompt :PromptConfig);
    setPrompt @33 (config :PromptConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Script mode
    runScript @34 (path :Text, args :List(Text)) -> (result :CommandResult);
    validateScript @35 (path :Text) -> (errors :List(ScriptError));
    getScriptContext @36 () -> (context :ScriptContext);

    # Watchers
    listWatchers @37 () -> (watchers :List(WatcherInfo));
    cancelWatcher @38 (watcherId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Bookmarks
    bookmark @39 (command :Text, label :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listBookmarks @40 () -> (bookmarks :List(Bookmark));
    runBookmark @41 (bookmarkId :UInt64) -> (result :CommandResult);
    removeBookmark @42 (bookmarkId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Guided mode (for non-technical users)
    enterGuidedMode @43 (domain :Text) -> (guide :GuidedSession);
    guideNext @44 (sessionId :UInt64) -> (step :GuidedStep);
    guideInput @45 (sessionId :UInt64, input :Text) -> (result :GuidedStepResult);
    exitGuidedMode @46 (sessionId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Session snapshots
    saveSnapshot @47 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    restoreSnapshot @48 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listSnapshots @49 () -> (snapshots :List(ShellSnapshot));
    deleteSnapshot @50 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Shell State ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ShellState {
    sessionId @0 :UInt64;
    mode @1 :ShellMode;
    currentDirectory @2 :Text;
    lastExitCode @3 :Int32;
    lastCommand @4 :Text;
    activeJobs @5 :UInt32;
    activeWatchers @6 :UInt32;
    uptime @7 :T.Duration;
    commandCount @8 :UInt64;
    undoStackSize @9 :UInt32;
    userId @10 :Text;
    aiAssistEnabled @11 :Bool;
    theme @12 :ShellTheme;
}

enum ShellMode {
    interactive @0;
    guided @1;
    script @2;
    batch @3;
    remote @4;
    voice @5;
    minimal @6;
    custom @7;
}

# ── Shell Config ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ShellConfig {
    mode @0 :ShellMode;
    theme @1 :ShellTheme;
    historySize @2 :UInt32;
    prompt @3 :PromptConfig;
    aiAssistEnabled @4 :Bool;
    confirmDestructive @5 :Bool;
    autoCorrect @6 :Bool;
    smartSuggestions @7 :Bool;
    verboseErrors @8 :Bool;
    colorOutput @9 :Bool;
    compactMode @10 :Bool;
    maxUndoLevels @11 :UInt32;
    keybindings @12 :KeyBindingProfile;
    defaultFormat @13 :OutputFormat;
}

enum OutputFormat {
    human @0;

    yaml @3;
    markdown @4;
    csv @5;
    tsv @6;
    txt @7;
    raw @8;
    capnp @9;
    custom @10;
}

# ── Prompt ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct PromptConfig {
    # Variables: ${user} ${hostname} ${cwd} ${git_branch} ${exit_code}
    #           ${battery} ${time} ${job_count} ${depth}
    template @0 :Text;
    rightTemplate @1 :Text;
    char @2 :Text;           # default "❯"
    errorChar @3 :Text;      # default "✗"
    showGit @4 :Bool;

    showTime @6 :Bool;
    showJobs @7 :Bool;
    showDuration @8 :Bool;
    durationThreshold @9 :Float32;
    lines @10 :List(Text);
}

# ── Natural Language ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct NaturalLanguageRequest {
    text @0 :Text;
    context @1 :InterpretContext;
    autoExecute @2 :Bool;
    confidenceThreshold @3 :Float32;
}

struct InterpretContext {
    currentDirectory @0 :Text;
    recentCommands @1 :List(Text);
    currentDomain @2 :Text;
    availableApps @3 :List(Text);
    systemState @4 :Text;
}

struct InterpretedCommand {
    commands @0 :List(Text);
    confidence @1 :Float32;
    explanation @2 :Text;
    destructive @3 :Bool;
    domains @4 :List(Text);
    requiresConfirmation @5 :Bool;
    alternatives @6 :List(InterpretedCommand);
    undoDescription @7 :Text;
}

# ── Command Input/Result ──────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CommandInput {
    text @0 :Text;
    interactive @1 :Bool;
    force @2 :Bool;
    format @3 :OutputFormat;
    pipeInput @4 :Data;
    timeout @5 :T.Duration;
    remoteHost @6 :Text;
}

struct CommandResult {
    exitCode @0 :Int32;
    output @1 :Text;
    structuredData @2 :Data;
    error @3 :Text;
    suggestion @4 :Text;
    duration @5 :T.Duration;
    undoable @6 :Bool;
    undoCommand @7 :Text;
    warnings @8 :List(Text);
    truncated @9 :Bool;
    totalItems @10 :UInt32;
    # Capability required for this command (if permission denied).
    requiredCapability @11 :Text;
    # Example of a working command (if error).
    exampleCommand @12 :Text;
}

# ── Completions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Completion {
    text @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    kind @2 :CompletionKind;
    requiresValue @3 :Bool;
    valueExample @4 :Text;
    relevance @5 :Float32;
}

enum CompletionKind {
    command @0;
    domain @1;
    action @2;
    selector @3;
    file @4;
    directory @5;
    app @6;
    service @7;
    process @8;
    window @9;
    device @10;
    value @11;
    flag @12;
    alias @13;
    variable @14;
    keyword @15;
    info @16;
    property @17;
    id @18;
    format @19;
    naturalLanguage @20;
    custom @21;
}

struct SelectorCompletion {
    path @0 :Text;
    currentValue @1 :Text;
    valueType @2 :Text;
    description @3 :Text;
}

struct DomainCompletion {
    command @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    syntax @2 :Text;
    examples @3 :List(Text);
}

# ── History ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct HistoryEntry {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    command @1 :Text;
    timestamp @2 :T.Timestamp;
    exitCode @3 :Int32;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    directory @5 :Text;
    pinned @6 :Bool;
    tags @7 :List(Text);
    # The formatted output (for replay).
    outputPreview @8 :Text;
}

struct HistoryFilter {
    pattern @0 :Text;
    exitCode @1 :Int32;
    directory @2 :Text;
    since @3 :T.Timestamp;
    tags @4 :List(Text);
    pinnedOnly @5 :Bool;
    # Filter by domain (e.g., "audio", "system").
    domain @6 :Text;
}

# ── Aliases ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Alias {
    name @0 :Text;
    expansion @1 :Text;

# ── Variables ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CLI — configuration, domain discovery, extensions, themes, help,
#       diagnostics, tutorials, and the meta-schema that governs how
#       all domains are presented to the user.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface CliService {
    # Configuration
    getConfig @0 () -> (config :CliConfig);
    setConfig @1 (config :CliConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Domains
    listDomains @2 () -> (domains :List(DomainInfo));
    getDomainHelp @3 (domain :Text) -> (help :DomainHelp);
    getCommandHelp @4 (domain :Text, action :Text) -> (help :CommandHelp);
    getSyntaxRef @5 (domain :Text) -> (syntax :SyntaxReference);

    # Extensions
    listExtensions @6 () -> (extensions :List(CliExtension));
    installExtension @7 (extension :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    removeExtension @8 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    toggleExtension @9 (name :Text, enabled :Bool) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Themes
    listThemes @10 () -> (themes :List(CliTheme));
    setTheme @11 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    getTheme @12 () -> (theme :CliTheme);

    # Diagnostics
    diagnose @13 () -> (report :DiagnosticReport);
    ping @14 () -> (result :PingResult);
    version @15 () -> (info :VersionInfo);

    # Output control
    setOutputFormat @16 (format :OutputFormat) -> T.VoidResult;
    getOutputFormat @17 () -> (format :OutputFormat);
    setVerbosity @18 (level :VerbosityLevel) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Command registry
    registerCommand @19 (command :CommandRegistration) -> T.VoidResult;
    unregisterCommand @20 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listCommands @21 () -> (commands :List(CommandRegistration));

    # Learning & discovery
    getSuggestions @22 (context :Text) -> (suggestions :List(CommandSuggestion));
    getTutorial @23 (domain :Text) -> (tutorial :Tutorial);
    getCheatSheet @24 () -> (sheet :CheatSheet);

    # Hybrid command registry
    listHybridCommands @25 () -> (commands :List(HybridCommandInfo));
    getHybridHelp @26 (name :Text) -> (help :HybridCommandHelp);
}

# ── CLI Config ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CliConfig {
    defaultFormat @0 :OutputFormat;
    theme @1 :Text;
    verbosity @2 :VerbosityLevel;
    confirmDestructive @3 :Bool;
    aiAssist @4 :Bool;
    showTips @5 :Bool;
    autoCorrect @6 :Bool;
    maxCompletions @7 :UInt32;
    historyPath @8 :Text;
    configPath @9 :Text;
    enabledExtensions @10 :List(Text);
    disabledDomains @11 :List(Text);
    keybindings @12 :List(KeyBinding);
    startupMessage @13 :Text;
    checkUpdates @14 :Bool;
    remoteHosts @15 :List(RemoteHostConfig);
    # Default number of items to show before paginating.
    pageLimit @16 :UInt32;
    # Whether to show inline help tips on errors.
    showHelpOnErrors @17 :Bool;
    # Whether to suggest corrections for typos.
    suggestCorrections @18 :Bool;
    # Whether to auto-detect and suggest format based on pipe target.
    smartPipe @19 :Bool;
}

enum VerbosityLevel {
    quiet @0;
    normal @1;
    verbose @2;
    debug @3;
    trace @4;
}

# ── Domain Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DomainInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    commandCount @2 :UInt32;
    available @3 :Bool;
    schemaVersion @4 :T.Version;
    extension @5 :Bool;
    commands @6 :List(CommandBrief);
    category @7 :DomainCategory;
    # The schema file backing this domain.
    schemaFile @8 :Text;
    # Whether this domain requires elevated capabilities.
    requiresCapability @9 :Text;
}

enum DomainCategory {
    system @0;
    hardware @1;
    display @2;
    networking @3;
    media @4;
    security @5;
    files @6;
    apps @7;
    data @8;
    settings @9;
    management @10;
    developer @11;
    custom @12;
}

struct CommandBrief {
    name @0 :Text;
    syntax @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    destructive @3 :Bool;
    requiresCapability @4 :Text;
}

# ── Help ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DomainHelp {
    domain @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    commands @2 :List(CommandHelp);
    selectors @3 :List(SelectorHelp);
    examples @4 :List(Text);
    seeAlso @5 :List(Text);
    # Common patterns for this domain.
    patterns @6 :List(Text);
}

struct CommandHelp {
    name @0 :Text;
    syntax @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    arguments @3 :List(ArgumentHelp);
    options @4 :List(OptionHelp);
    examples @5 :List(Text);
    destructive @6 :Bool;
    undoable @7 :Bool;
    requiresCapability @8 :Text;
    seeAlso @9 :List(Text);
    # What happens on success.
    successDescription @10 :Text;
    # What happens on failure.
    failureDescription @11 :Text;
}

struct ArgumentHelp {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    required @2 :Bool;
    type @3 :Text;
    default @4 :Text;
    example @5 :Text;
    # Valid values (for enums).
    validValues @6 :List(Text);
}

struct OptionHelp {
    name @0 :Text;
    short @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    type @3 :Text;
    default @4 :Text;
}

struct SelectorHelp {
    path @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    type @2 :Text;
    example @3 :Text;
}

# ── Syntax Reference ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SyntaxReference {
    domain @0 :Text;
    commands @1 :List(Text);
    rules @2 :List(Text);
    patterns @3 :List(Text);
}

# ── Extensions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CliExtension {
    name @0 :Text;
    version @1 :T.Version;
    description @2 :Text;
    author @3 :Text;
    domains @4 :List(Text);
    enabled @5 :Bool;
    dependencies @6 :List(Text);
    # Hybrid commands provided by this extension.
    hybridCommands @7 :List(Text);
}

# ── Themes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CliTheme {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    dark @2 :Bool;
    colors @3 :ThemeColors;
    tableStyle @4 :Text;
    unicode @5 :Bool;
    emoji @6 :Bool;
}

struct ThemeColors {
    primary @0 :Text;
    success @1 :Text;
    error @2 :Text;
    warning @3 :Text;
    info @4 :Text;
    muted @5 :Text;
    accent @6 :Text;
    background @7 :Text;
    foreground @8 :Text;
}

# ── Diagnostics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DiagnosticReport {
    cliVersion @0 :Text;
    protocolConnected @1 :Bool;
    protocolVersion @2 :Text;
    availableDomains @3 :UInt32;
    unavailableDomains @4 :UInt32;
    schemaVersionsMatch @5 :Bool;
    extensionsLoaded @6 :UInt32;
    extensionsFailed @7 :UInt32;
    issues @8 :List(DiagnosticIssue);
    recommendations @9 :List(Text);
    latencyMs @10 :Float32;
    # System info (if connected).
    systemHostname @11 :Text;
    systemKernel @12 :Text;
    systemUptime @13 :T.Duration;
}

struct DiagnosticIssue {
    severity @0 :IssueSeverity;
    domain @1 :Text;
    message @2 :Text;
    suggestion @3 :Text;
}

enum IssueSeverity {
    info @0;
    warning @1;
    error @2;
    critical @3;
}

struct PingResult {
    reachable @0 :Bool;
    latencyMs @1 :Float32;
    protocolVersion @2 :Text;
    daemonVersion @3 :Text;
    uptime @4 :T.Duration;
}

struct VersionInfo {
    cliVersion @0 :Text;
    protocolVersion @1 :Text;
    buildDate @2 :Text;
    gitHash @3 :Text;
    rustVersion @4 :Text;
    targetTriple @5 :Text;
    features @6 :List(Text);
}

# ── Command Registration ─────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CommandRegistration {
    name @0 :Text;
    domain @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    syntax @3 :Text;
    handler @4 :Text;
    destructive @5 :Bool;
    undoable @6 :Bool;
}

# ── Suggestions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CommandSuggestion {
    command @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    relevance @2 :Float32;
    reason @3 :Text;
}

# ── Tutorial ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Tutorial {
    domain @0 :Text;
    title @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    steps @3 :List(TutorialStep);
    estimatedMinutes @4 :UInt32;
}

struct TutorialStep {
    title @0 :Text;
    instruction @1 :Text;
    command @2 :Text;
    expectedOutput @3 :Text;
    tip @4 :Text;
    # Whether this step is interactive (user must type).
    interactive @5 :Bool;
}

# ── Cheat Sheet ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CheatSheet {
    sections @0 :List(CheatSheetSection);
}

struct CheatSheetSection {
    title @0 :Text;
    entries @1 :List(CheatSheetEntry);
}

struct CheatSheetEntry {
    command @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
}

# ── Key Binding ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct KeyBinding {
    key @0 :Text;
    action @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
}

# ── Remote Host Config ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct RemoteHostConfig {
    name @0 :Text;
    address @1 :Text;
    port @2 :UInt16;
    user @3 :Text;
    autoConnect @4 :Bool;
    # Last connection time.
    lastConnected @5 :T.Timestamp;
    # Connection status.
    status @6 :RemoteHostStatus;
}

enum RemoteHostStatus {
    disconnected @0;
    connected @1;
    unreachable @2;
    connecting @3;
}

# ── Hybrid Command ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct HybridCommandInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    # Which domains this command queries.
    domains @2 :List(Text);
    # Whether this is destructive.
    destructive @3 :Bool;
    # Example usage.
    example @4 :Text;
    # Category (performance, security, preparation, debugging, etc).
    category @5 :Text;
}

struct HybridCommandHelp {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    whatItDoes @0 :Text;
    domainsQueried @1 :List(Text);
    examples @2 :List(Text);
    relatedCommands @3 :List(Text);
}

# ── Output Format ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# (shared with shell.capnp — defined here for CLI schema)

enum OutputFormat {
    human @0;
    json @1;
    toml @2;
    yaml @3;
    markdown @4;
    csv @5;
    tsv @6;
    txt @7;
    raw @8;
    capnp @9;
    custom @10;
}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Diagnostics — system health, self-test, profiling, alerting,
#               failure prediction, and trend analysis
#
# Not a logging system. Not monitoring. This is "am I healthy?",
# "what's wrong?", "why is it slow?", "what will fail soon?".
# Every subsystem registers health checks. Aggregated into a
# unified health picture. Alerts are typed, not strings.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface DiagnosticsService {
    # Health
    getHealth @0 () -> (health :SystemHealth);
    runChecks @1 (scope :HealthScope) -> (results :List(HealthCheckResult));
    runCheck @2 (checkId :Text) -> (result :HealthCheckResult);
    listChecks @3 () -> (checks :List(HealthCheck));

    # Alerts
    listAlerts @4 (filter :AlertFilter) -> (alerts :List(Alert));
    acknowledgeAlert @5 (alertId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;
    dismissAlert @6 (alertId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;
    setAlertThreshold @7 (threshold :AlertThreshold) -> T.VoidResult;
    listThresholds @8 () -> (thresholds :List(AlertThreshold));
    subscribeAlerts @9 () -> (subscription :AlertSubscription);

    # Performance profiling
    startProfile @10 (target :ProfileTarget) -> (profileId :UInt64);
    stopProfile @11 (profileId :UInt64) -> (result :ProfileResult);
    snapshot @12 () -> (snapshot :PerformanceSnapshot);

    # Self-test
    runSelfTest @13 (suite :SelfTestSuite) -> (result :SelfTestResult);
    listSelfTestSuites @14 () -> (suites :List(SelfTestSuite));

    # Reports
    generateReport @15 (scope :ReportScope) -> (report :DiagnosticReport);
    exportReport @16 (reportId :UInt64, format :ReportFormat, path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Predictive
    getPredictions @17 () -> (predictions :List(FailurePrediction));
    getTrend @18 (resource :Text, duration :T.Duration) -> (trend :ResourceTrend);
}

# ── System Health ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SystemHealth {
    status @0 :HealthStatus;
    subsystems @1 :List(SubsystemHealth);
    alertCount @2 :UInt32;
    criticalAlertCount @3 :UInt32;
    lastCheck @4 :T.Timestamp;
    uptime @5 :T.Duration;
    load @6 :SystemLoadIndicators;
    # Overall health score (0-100).
    score @7 :UInt32;
    # One-line summary.
    summary @8 :Text;
}

enum HealthStatus {
    healthy @0;
    degraded @1;
    unhealthy @2;
    critical @3;
    unknown @4;
}

struct SubsystemHealth {
    name @0 :Text;
    status @1 :HealthStatus;
    message @2 :Text;
    lastCheck @3 :T.Timestamp;
    metrics @4 :List(HealthMetric);
    # Remediation if unhealthy.
    remediation @5 :Text;
}

struct HealthMetric {
    name @0 :Text;
    value @1 :Float64;
    unit @2 :Text;
    minNormal @3 :Float64;
    maxNormal @4 :Float64;
    normal @5 :Bool;
}

struct SystemLoadIndicators {
    cpuUsage @0 :Float32;
    memoryUsage @1 :Float32;
    diskUsage @2 :Float32;
    networkUsage @3 :Float32;
    swapUsage @4 :Float32;
    gpuUsage @5 :Float32;
    ioWait @6 :Float32;
    thermalPressure @7 :Float32;
}

# ── Health Checks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct HealthCheck {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    subsystem @3 :Text;
    interval @4 :T.Duration;
    enabled @5 :Bool;
    failureSeverity @6 :AlertSeverity;
    # Estimated duration of this check.
    estimatedDuration @7 :T.Duration;
    # Whether this check requires elevated privileges.
    requiresPrivilege @8 :Bool;
    # Whether this check is destructive (affects system state).
    destructive @9 :Bool;
}

struct HealthCheckResult {
    checkId @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    status @2 :HealthStatus;
    message @3 :Text;
    details @4 :T.StringMap;
    duration @5 :T.Duration;
    timestamp @6 :T.Timestamp;
    remediation @7 :Text;
    # Command to fix the issue.
    fixCommand @8 :Text;
}

enum HealthScope {
    quick @0;
    standard @1;
    deep @2;
    custom @3;
}

# ── Alerts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct Alert {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    severity @1 :AlertSeverity;
    title @2 :Text;
    message @3 :Text;
    subsystem @4 :Text;
    source @5 :Text;
    timestamp @6 :T.Timestamp;
    acknowledged @7 :Bool;
    acknowledgedBy @8 :Text;
    acknowledgedAt @9 :T.Timestamp;
    remediation @10 :List(Text);
    metrics @11 :List(HealthMetric);
    autoResolvable @12 :Bool;
    autoResolveCommand @13 :Text;
    # How long this alert has been active.
    activeDuration @14 :T.Duration;
    # How many times this condition has been triggered.
    occurrenceCount @15 :UInt32;
}

enum AlertSeverity {
    info @0;
    warning @1;
    error @2;
    critical @3;
    emergency @4;
}

struct AlertFilter {
    severities @0 :List(AlertSeverity);
    subsystems @1 :List(Text);
    since @2 :T.Timestamp;
    acknowledged @3 :T.BoolFilter;
    unresolved @4 :Bool;
}

struct AlertThreshold {
    id @0 :Text;
    metric @1 :Text;
    subsystem @2 :Text;
    warningThreshold @3 :Float64;
    errorThreshold @4 :Float64;
    criticalThreshold @5 :Float64;
    direction @6 :ThresholdDirection;
    sustainedDuration @7 :T.Duration;
    enabled @8 :Bool;
}

enum ThresholdDirection {
    above @0;
    below @1;
    change @2;
}

interface AlertSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (alerts :List(Alert));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── Performance Profiling ────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProfileTarget {
    union {
        system @0 :Void;
        process @1 :T.ProcessId;
        service @2 :Text;
        domain @3 :Text;
        custom @4 :Text;
    }
    duration @5 :T.Duration;
    metrics @6 :List(ProfileMetricType);
}

enum ProfileMetricType {
    cpu @0;
    memory @1;
    io @2;
    network @3;
    gpu @4;
    latency @5;
    throughput @6;
    custom @7;
}

struct ProfileResult {
    profileId @0 :UInt64;
    target @1 :ProfileTarget;
    startTime @2 :T.Timestamp;
    endTime @3 :T.Timestamp;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    samples @5 :List(ProfileSample);
    summary @6 :ProfileSummary;
}

struct ProfileSample {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    metric @1 :ProfileMetricType;
    value @2 :Float64;
    unit @3 :Text;
}

struct ProfileSummary {
    cpu @0 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    memory @1 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    io @2 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    network @3 :ProfileMetricSummary;
    hotspots @4 :List(Hotspot);
}

struct ProfileMetricSummary {
    min @0 :Float64;
    max @1 :Float64;
    avg @2 :Float64;
    p50 @3 :Float64;
    p95 @4 :Float64;
    p99 @5 :Float64;
}

struct Hotspot {
    name @0 :Text;
    percentage @1 :Float32;
    description @2 :Text;
    # Suggestion to fix.
    suggestion @3 :Text;
}

struct PerformanceSnapshot {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    cpu @1 :CpuSnapshot;
    memory @2 :MemorySnapshot;
    io @3 :IoSnapshot;
    network @4 :NetworkSnapshot;
    gpu @5 :GpuSnapshot;
}

struct CpuSnapshot {
    overallUsage @0 :Float32;
    perCoreUsage @1 :List(Float32);
    frequency @2 :List(UInt64);
    temperature @3 :List(Float32);
    contextSwitches @4 :UInt64;
    interrupts @5 :UInt64;
    loadAverage @6 :T.LoadAverage;
}

struct MemorySnapshot {
    totalBytes @0 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @1 :UInt64;
    availableBytes @2 :UInt64;
    cachedBytes @3 :UInt64;
    bufferBytes @4 :UInt64;
    swapTotalBytes @5 :UInt64;
    swapUsedBytes @6 :UInt64;
    topConsumers @7 :List(MemoryConsumer);
}

struct MemoryConsumer {
    name @0 :Text;
    pid @1 :T.ProcessId;
    bytes @2 :UInt64;
    percentage @3 :Float32;
}

struct IoSnapshot {
    readBytesPerSec @0 :UInt64;
    writeBytesPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    iops @2 :UInt32;
    readLatencyMs @3 :Float32;
    writeLatencyMs @4 :Float32;
    devices @5 :List(DeviceIoStats);
}

struct DeviceIoStats {
    device @0 :Text;
    readBytesPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    writeBytesPerSec @2 :UInt64;
    iops @3 :UInt32;
    utilization @4 :Float32;
}

struct NetworkSnapshot {
    totalBytesPerSec @0 :UInt64;
    bytesInPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    bytesOutPerSec @2 :UInt64;
    packetsInPerSec @3 :UInt64;
    packetsOutPerSec @4 :UInt64;
    connections @5 :UInt32;
    errors @6 :UInt32;
    interfaces @7 :List(InterfaceStats);
}

struct InterfaceStats {
    name @0 :Text;
    bytesInPerSec @1 :UInt64;
    bytesOutPerSec @2 :UInt64;
    linkSpeed @3 :UInt64;
    utilization @4 :Float32;
}

struct GpuSnapshot {
    usage @0 :Float32;
    memoryUsed @1 :UInt64;
    memoryTotal @2 :UInt64;
    temperature @3 :Float32;
    fanSpeed @4 :Float32;
    powerWatts @5 :Float32;
}

# ── Self-Test ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SelfTestSuite {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    tests @2 :List(SelfTest);
    estimatedDuration @3 :T.Duration;
    requiresPrivilege @4 :Bool;
    # Whether tests in this suite are destructive.
    destructive @5 :Bool;
}

struct SelfTest {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    subsystem @3 :Text;
    estimatedDuration @4 :T.Duration;
    destructive @5 :Bool;
}

struct SelfTestResult {
    suite @0 :Text;
    passed @1 :UInt32;
    failed @2 :UInt32;
    skipped @3 :UInt32;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    results @5 :List(SelfTestItemResult);
    timestamp @6 :T.Timestamp;
    # Overall pass rate.
    passRate @7 :Float32;
}

struct SelfTestItemResult {
    testId @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    passed @2 :Bool;
    message @3 :Text;
    duration @4 :T.Duration;
    remediation @5 :Text;
    fixCommand @6 :Text;
}

# ── Diagnostic Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ReportScope {
    includeSystem @0 :Bool;
    includeHealth @1 :Bool;
    includePerformance @2 :Bool;
    includeAlerts @3 :Bool;
    includeHardware @4 :Bool;
    includeNetwork @5 :Bool;
    includeProcesses @6 :Bool;
    includeServices @7 :Bool;
    includeKernel @8 :Bool;
    since @9 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum ReportFormat {
    text @0;
    json @1;
    toml @2;
    yaml @3;
    html @4;
    markdown @5;
    pdf @6;
    custom @7;
}

struct DiagnosticReport {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    generatedAt @1 :T.Timestamp;
    scope @2 :ReportScope;
    system @3 :SystemSummary;
    health @4 :SystemHealth;
    performance @5 :PerformanceSnapshot;
    alerts @6 :List(Alert);
    hardware @7 :HardwareSummary;
    network @8 :NetworkSummary;
    processes @9 :ProcessSummary;
    services @10 :ServiceSummary;
    kernel @11 :KernelSummary;
    recommendations @12 :List(Recommendation);
    # Overall system score (0-100).
    overallScore @13 :UInt32;
}

struct SystemSummary {
    hostname @0 :Text;
    os @1 :Text;
    kernelVersion @2 :Text;
    architecture @3 :Text;
    uptime @4 :T.Duration;
    bootTime @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct HardwareSummary {
    cpu @0 :Text;
    cpuCores @1 :UInt32;
    memoryBytes @2 :UInt64;
    gpus @3 :List(Text);
    disks @4 :List(DiskSummary);
    thermals @5 :ThermalSummary;
}

struct DiskSummary {
    device @0 :Text;
    sizeBytes @1 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @2 :UInt64;
    health @3 :Text;
    temperature @4 :Float32;
}

struct ThermalSummary {
    cpuTemp @0 :Float32;
    gpuTemp @1 :Float32;
    ambientTemp @2 :Float32;
    fanSpeeds @3 :List(FanSpeed);
    throttleActive @4 :Bool;
}

struct FanSpeed {
    name @0 :Text;
    rpm @1 :UInt32;
}

struct NetworkSummary {
    interfaces @0 :UInt32;
    connected @1 :Bool;
    ssid @2 :Text;
    ip @3 :Text;
    publicIp @4 :Text;
    dnsServers @5 :List(Text);
}

struct ProcessSummary {
    total @0 :UInt32;
    running @1 :UInt32;
    sleeping @2 :UInt32;
    zombie @3 :UInt32;
    topCpu @4 :List(Text);
    topMemory @5 :List(Text);
}

struct ServiceSummary {
    total @0 :UInt32;
    active @1 :UInt32;
    failed @2 :UInt32;
    failedServices @3 :List(Text);
}

struct KernelSummary {
    type @0 :Text;
    version @1 :Text;
    architecture @2 :Text;
    capabilities @3 :List(Text);
    extensions @4 :UInt32;
}

struct Recommendation {
    severity @0 :AlertSeverity;
    title @1 :Text;
    description @2 :Text;
    action @3 :Text;
    command @4 :Text;
    # Estimated impact (e.g., "+1h battery", "20% faster boot").
    estimatedImpact @5 :Text;
}

# ── Predictive ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct FailurePrediction {
    component @0 :Text;
    failureType @1 :FailureType;
    confidence @2 :Float32;
    estimatedTimeToFailure @3 :T.Duration;
    currentHealth @4 :Float32;
    recommendation @5 :Text;
    predictedAt @6 :T.Timestamp;
    # Action to take now.
    preventiveAction @7 :Text;
    # Command to run preventive action.
    preventiveCommand @8 :Text;
}

enum FailureType {
    diskFailure @0;
    memoryDegradation @1;
    batteryDegradation @2;
    thermalThrottling @3;
    networkDegradation @4;
    serviceInstability @5;
    custom @6;
}

struct ResourceTrend {
    resource @0 :Text;
    duration @1 :T.Duration;
    direction @2 :TrendDirection;
    changeRate @3 :Float32;
    currentValue @4 :Float64;
    predictedValue @5 :Float64;
    samples @6 :List(TrendSample);
    criticalAt @7 :T.Timestamp;
    # Recommendation based on trend.
    recommendation @8 :Text;
}

enum TrendDirection {
    stable @0;
    increasing @1;
    decreasing @2;
    volatile @3;
    cyclic @4;
}

struct TrendSample {
    timestamp @0 :T.Timestamp;
    value @1 :Float64;
}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Init — the init system, service supervision, boot orchestration
#
# Not systemd. Not OpenRC. The init contract: what the first process
# provides. Services, dependencies, ordering, socket activation,
# timers, and boot stages. Backend-agnostic.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface InitService {
    # Boot state
    getBootState @0 () -> (state :BootState);
    getTarget @1 () -> (target :BootTarget);
    setTarget @2 (target :BootTarget) -> T.VoidResult;
    listTargets @3 () -> (targets :List(BootTargetInfo));

    # Services
    listServices @4 (filter :ServiceFilter) -> (services :List(ServiceInfo), total :UInt32);
    getService @5 (name :Text) -> (service :ServiceInfo);
    start @6 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    stop @7 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    restart @8 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    reload @9 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    enable @10 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    disable @11 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    mask @12 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    unmask @13 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    getDependencies @14 (name :Text) -> (deps :ServiceDependencyTree);
    getDependents @15 (name :Text) -> (dependents :List(Text));

    # Logs
    getServiceLogs @16 (name :Text, filter :LogFilter) -> (logs :List(ServiceLogEntry), total :UInt32);
    watchServiceLogs @17 (name :Text) -> (subscription :LogSubscription);

    # Socket activation
    listSockets @18 () -> (sockets :List(SocketInfo));
    getSocketState @19 (name :Text) -> (state :SocketState);

    # Timers
    listTimers @20 () -> (timers :List(TimerInfo));
    getTimerState @21 (name :Text) -> (state :TimerState);
    triggerTimer @22 (name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Boot history
    getBootHistory @23 (pagination :T.Pagination) -> (boots :List(BootRecord), total :UInt32);
    getBootChart @24 (bootId :UInt64) -> (chart :BootChart);

    # Events
    subscribe @25 () -> (subscription :InitSubscription);

    # Emergency
    enterEmergency @26 () -> T.VoidResult;
    exitEmergency @27 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Task Scheduler — scheduling policies, priorities, affinity,
#                  real-time scheduling, NUMA, load balancing
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface SchedulerService {
    # Scheduler info
    getInfo @0 () -> (info :SchedulerInfo);

    # Per-process policy
    getPolicy @1 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (policy :ProcessSchedulingPolicy);
    setPolicy @2 (pid :T.ProcessId, policy :ProcessSchedulingPolicy) -> T.VoidResult;

    # CPU affinity
    getAffinity @3 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (affinity :CpuAffinity);
    setAffinity @4 (pid :T.ProcessId, affinity :CpuAffinity) -> T.VoidResult;

    # NUMA
    getNumaPolicy @5 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (policy :NumaPolicy);
    setNumaPolicy @6 (pid :T.ProcessId, policy :NumaPolicy) -> T.VoidResult;

    # SMP topology
    getTopology @7 () -> (topology :CpuTopology);
    getCpuLoad @8 () -> (load :List(CpuLoadInfo));
    getCurrentCpu @9 () -> (cpu :UInt32);
    subscribeTopology @10 () -> (subscription :TopologySubscription);

    # Scheduling domains
    listDomains @11 () -> (domains :List(SchedulingDomain));
    getDomain @12 (cpu :UInt32) -> (domain :SchedulingDomain);

    # Load balancing
    getLoadBalanceStats @13 () -> (stats :LoadBalanceStats);
    rebalance @14 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # RT scheduling
    getRtBandwidth @15 () -> (bandwidth :RtBandwidth);
    setRtBandwidth @16 (bandwidth :RtBandwidth) -> T.VoidResult;
    getDeadlineInfo @17 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (info :DeadlineInfo);
    setDeadline @18 (pid :T.ProcessId, info :DeadlineInfo) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Cgroup scheduler config
    getCgroupConfig @19 (cgroup :Text) -> (config :CgroupSchedulerConfig);
    setCgroupConfig @20 (cgroup :Text, config :CgroupSchedulerConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Events
    subscribe @21 () -> (subscription :SchedulerSubscription);
}

# ── Scheduler Info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SchedulerInfo {
    name @0 :Text;
    version @1 :Text;
    supportedPolicies @2 :List(SchedulingPolicy);
    domainCount @3 :UInt32;
    numaBalancing @4 :Bool;
    autogroup @5 :Bool;
    tickRate @6 :UInt32;
    minGranularityNs @7 :UInt64;
    latencyTargetNs @8 :UInt64;
}

enum SchedulingPolicy {
    other @0;

    fifo @3;
    roundRobin @4;
    deadline @5;
    custom @6;
}

# ── Process Scheduling Policy ────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessSchedulingPolicy {

    rtPriority @2 :UInt8;
    deadline @3 :DeadlineInfo;
    ioClass @4 :IoSchedulingClass;
    ioPriority @5 :Int8;
}

enum IoSchedulingClass {

}

}

}

}

interface TopologySubscription {

}

struct TopologyEvent {

struct FrequencyChangeEvent {

}

struct TemperatureChangeEvent {
    cpuId @0 :UInt32;
    temperature @1 :Float32;
    throttleActive @2 :Bool;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Scheduler Events ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface SchedulerSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(SchedulerEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct SchedulerEvent {
    union {
        processMigrated @0 :ProcessMigrationEvent;
        processThrottled @1 :ProcessThrottleEvent;

}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Signal — signal registration, delivery, masking, queuing
#
# Signals are typed (T.SignalKind), not integers. The shell, init
# system, and apps all use this contract. Kernel-side delivery
# lives in kernel.capnp.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface SignalService {
    # Handlers
    register @0 (kind :T.SignalKind, handler :SignalHandler) -> (handleId :UInt64);
    unregister @1 (handleId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;
    listHandlers @2 () -> (handlers :List(RegisteredHandler));

    # Masking
    getMask @3 () -> (mask :SignalMask);
    setMask @4 (mask :SignalMask) -> T.VoidResult;
    block @5 (signals :List(T.SignalKind)) -> T.VoidResult;
    unblock @6 (signals :List(T.SignalKind)) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Sending
    send @7 (target :T.ProcessId, signal :T.SignalKind, data :Data) -> T.VoidResult;
    sendGroup @8 (groupId :UInt32, signal :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;
    broadcast @9 (signal :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;
    sendRt @10 (target :T.ProcessId, signalNumber :UInt8, payload :Data) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Queue
    getPending @11 () -> (pending :List(PendingSignal));
    clearPending @12 (kind :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;
    getQueueInfo @13 () -> (info :SignalQueueInfo);

    # Waiting
    wait @14 (kind :T.SignalKind, timeout :T.Duration) -> (signal :PendingSignal);
    waitAny @15 (timeout :T.Duration) -> (signal :PendingSignal);

    # Events
    subscribe @16 (filter :SignalFilter) -> (subscription :SignalSubscription);

    # Info
    getInfo @17 (kind :T.SignalKind) -> (info :SignalInfo);
    listSupported @18 () -> (signals :List(SignalInfo));
}

# ── Signal Handler ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalHandler {
    union {
        default @0 :Void;
        ignore @1 :Void;
        callback @2 :Data;
        forward @3 :T.ProcessId;
        log @4 :Void;
        custom @5 :Data;
    }
}

struct RegisteredHandler {
    handleId @0 :UInt64;
    kind @1 :T.SignalKind;
    handler @2 :SignalHandler;
    invocationCount @3 :UInt64;
    registeredAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
}

# ── Signal Mask ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalMask {
    blocked @0 :List(T.SignalKind);
    pending @1 :List(T.SignalKind);
}

# ── Pending Signal ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct PendingSignal {
    kind @0 :T.SignalKind;
    sender @1 :T.ProcessId;
    sentAt @2 :T.Timestamp;
    data @3 :Data;
    rtNumber @4 :UInt8;
}

struct SignalQueueInfo {
    maxQueued @0 :UInt32;
    queued @1 :UInt32;
    dropped @2 :UInt64;
}

# ── Signal Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalInfo {
    kind @0 :T.SignalKind;
    defaultAction @1 :SignalDefaultAction;
    catchable @2 :Bool;
    blockable @3 :Bool;
    coreDump @4 :Bool;
    description @5 :Text;
    typicalCause @6 :Text;
}

enum SignalDefaultAction {
    terminate @0;
    terminateAndCore @1;
    ignore @2;
    stop @3;
    continueProc @4;
    custom @5;
}

# ── Signal Filter & Subscription ─────────────────────────────────────

struct SignalFilter {
    kinds @0 :List(T.SignalKind);
    fromProcesses @1 :List(T.ProcessId);
    includeData @2 :Bool;
}

interface SignalSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (signals :List(PendingSignal));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Boot — boot parameters, boot entries, boot splash, recovery,
#        secure boot, and boot counters
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface BootService {
    # Boot info
    getInfo @0 () -> (info :BootInfo);

    # Boot parameters
    getParameters @1 () -> (params :BootParameters);
    setParameters @2 (params :BootParameters) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Boot entries
    listEntries @3 () -> (entries :List(BootEntry));
    getDefaultEntry @4 () -> (entry :BootEntry);
    setDefaultEntry @5 (entryId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    setNextBootEntry @6 (entryId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Boot log
    getBootLog @7 (filter :BootLogFilter) -> (entries :List(BootLogEntry), total :UInt32);

    # Boot splash
    getSplashConfig @8 () -> (config :BootSplashConfig);
    setSplashConfig @9 (config :BootSplashConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Recovery
    setRecoveryMode @10 (enable :Bool) -> T.VoidResult;
    getRecoveryMode @11 () -> (enabled :Bool, reason :Text);

    # Secure boot
    getSecureBoot @12 () -> (status :SecureBootStatus);
    listSecureBootKeys @13 () -> (keys :List(SecureBootKey));

    # Boot counters
    getBootAttempts @14 () -> (attempts :BootAttempts);
    markBootSuccessful @15 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # Events
    subscribe @16 () -> (subscription :BootSubscription);
}

enum FirmwareType {

# ── Boot Parameters ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── Boot Entry ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Capability — the authority system
#
# Unforgeable, delegatable, auditable, typed. Not POSIX permissions.
# Not Unix DAC. Wire format is T.CapabilityHandle (UInt64).
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface CapabilityService {
    # Issue / revoke / delegate
    issue @0 (request :IssueRequest) -> (handle :T.CapabilityHandle);
    revoke @1 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> T.VoidResult;
    delegate @2 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle, request :DelegateRequest) -> (newHandle :T.CapabilityHandle);
    publish @3 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle, recipient :T.ProcessId) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Query
    inspect @4 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> (info :CapabilityInfo);
    listHeld @5 () -> (capabilities :List(CapabilityInfo));
    listPublished @6 (target :T.ProcessId) -> (capabilities :List(CapabilityInfo));
    check @7 (resource :Text, operation :Operation) -> (allowed :Bool, reason :Text);

    # Sets
    createSet @8 (name :Text, capabilities :List(T.CapabilityHandle)) -> (setId :UInt64);
    revokeSet @9 (setId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;
    listSets @10 () -> (sets :List(CapabilitySet));

    # Templates
    listTemplates @11 () -> (templates :List(CapabilityTemplate));
    issueFromTemplate @12 (templateName :Text, recipient :T.ProcessId) -> (handle :T.CapabilityHandle);

    # Audit
    getAuditTrail @13 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> (events :List(CapabilityEvent));
    subscribe @14 (filter :CapabilityFilter) -> (subscription :CapabilitySubscription);

    # Proof
    getProofLevel @15 (handle :T.CapabilityHandle) -> (proof :ProofInfo);

    # Scoping
    createScope @16 (config :ScopeConfig) -> (scopeId :UInt64);
    enterScope @17 (scopeId :UInt64) -> T.VoidResult;
    exitScope @18 () -> T.VoidResult;
    listScopes @19 () -> (scopes :List(CapabilityScope));
}

# ── Issue Request ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct IssueRequest {
    resource @0 :Text;
    operations @1 :List(Operation);
    recipient @2 :T.ProcessId;
    expiry @3 :T.Duration;
    maxUses @4 :UInt32;
    delegatable @5 :Bool;
    maxDelegationDepth @6 :UInt32;
    scope @7 :UInt64;
    reason @8 :Text;
}

enum Operation {
    read @0;
    write @1;
    execute @2;
    create @3;
    delete @4;
    list @5;
    subscribe @6;
    configure @7;
    admin @8;
    delegate @9;
    custom @10;
}

# ── Delegate Request ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DelegateRequest {
    operations @0 :List(Operation);
    recipient @1 :T.ProcessId;
    expiry @2 :T.Duration;
    maxUses @3 :UInt32;
    delegatable @4 :Bool;
    maxDelegationDepth @5 :UInt32;
}

# ── Capability Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityInfo {
    handle @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    resource @1 :Text;
    operations @2 :List(Operation);
    issuer @3 :T.ProcessId;
    issuedAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
    expiresAt @5 :T.Timestamp;
    remainingUses @6 :UInt32;
    delegatable @7 :Bool;
    delegationDepth @8 :UInt32;
    useCount @9 :UInt64;
    scope @10 :UInt64;
    # Whether this capability is currently valid.
    valid @11 :Bool;
    # If invalid, why.
    invalidReason @12 :Text;
}

# ── Capability Set ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilitySet {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    name @1 :Text;
    capabilities @2 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    createdAt @3 :T.Timestamp;
    count @4 :UInt32;
}

# ── Capability Template ─────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityTemplate {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    grants @2 :List(TemplateGrant);
    defaultExpiry @3 :T.Duration;
    delegatable @4 :Bool;
    category @5 :Text;
}

struct TemplateGrant {
    resource @0 :Text;
    operations @1 :List(Operation);
}

# ── Proof Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProofInfo {
    proofLevel @0 :ProofLevel;
    verifier @1 :Text;
    specHash @2 :Data;
    verifiedAt @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum ProofLevel {
    unverified @0;
    tested @1;
    staticAnalysis @2;
    formalPartial @3;
    formalComplete @4;
    formalEndToEnd @5;
}

# ── Capability Scope ────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityScope {
    id @0 :UInt64;
    name @1 :Text;
    capabilities @2 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    sandbox @3 :Bool;
    createdAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
    parentScope @5 :UInt64;
    # Number of operations performed in this scope.
    operationCount @6 :UInt64;
}

struct ScopeConfig {
    name @0 :Text;
    sandbox @1 :Bool;
    includeCapabilities @2 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    denyResources @3 :List(Text);
    maxCapabilities @4 :UInt32;
}

# ── Capability Events ───────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CapabilityFilter {
    handles @0 :List(T.CapabilityHandle);
    operations @1 :List(Operation);
    since @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

interface CapabilitySubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(CapabilityEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct CapabilityEvent {
    union {
        issued @0 :CapabilityInfo;
        revoked @1 :T.CapabilityHandle;
        delegated @2 :DelegationEvent;
        published @3 :PublishEvent;
        used @4 :UseEvent;
        expired @5 :T.CapabilityHandle;
        scopeCreated @6 :CapabilityScope;
        scopeEntered @7 :UInt64;
        scopeExited @8 :UInt64;
        custom @9 :Data;
    }
}

struct DelegationEvent {
    parent @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    child @1 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    from @2 :T.ProcessId;
    to @3 :T.ProcessId;
    operations @4 :List(Operation);
    timestamp @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct PublishEvent {
    handle @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    from @1 :T.ProcessId;
    to @2 :T.ProcessId;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct UseEvent {
    handle @0 :T.CapabilityHandle;
    operation @1 :Operation;
    resource @2 :Text;
    pid @3 :T.ProcessId;
    success @4 :Bool;
    timestamp @5 :T.Timestamp;
    # Denial reason if not success.
    denialReason @6 :Text;
}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Process — lifecycle, cgroups, namespaces, resource accounting
#
# kernel.capnp owns kernel-level primitives (spawn, fork, exec).
# This schema owns higher-level: cgroups, namespaces, resource
# accounting, process groups, sessions, process tree.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface ProcessService {
    # Info
    getInfo @0 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (info :ProcessInfo);
    list @1 (filter :ProcessFilter, pagination :T.Pagination) -> (processes :List(ProcessInfo), total :UInt32);
    getTree @2 (rootPid :T.ProcessId) -> (tree :ProcessTree);
    getFullTree @3 () -> (tree :ProcessTree);

    # Lifecycle
    kill @4 (pid :T.ProcessId, signal :T.SignalKind) -> T.VoidResult;
    renice @5 (pid :T.ProcessId, nice :Int8) -> T.VoidResult;
    suspend @6 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> T.VoidResult;
    resume @7 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> T.VoidResult;
    waitProcess @8 (pid :T.ProcessId, timeout :T.Duration) -> (exitStatus :T.ExitStatus);

    # Groups & sessions
    getProcessGroup @9 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (pgid :UInt32);
    setProcessGroup @10 (pid :T.ProcessId, pgid :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;
    getSession @11 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (sessionId :UInt32);
    listSessions @12 () -> (sessions :List(ProcessSession));
    listProcessGroups @13 () -> (groups :List(ProcessGroup));

    # Resource accounting
    getResourceUsage @14 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (usage :ProcessResourceUsage);
    getGroupResourceUsage @15 (pgid :UInt32) -> (usage :ProcessResourceUsage);
    getSystemResourceUsage @16 () -> (usage :SystemResourceUsage);

    # Cgroups
    listCgroups @17 () -> (cgroups :List(CgroupInfo));
    getCgroup @18 (path :Text) -> (info :CgroupInfo);
    createCgroup @19 (path :Text, config :CgroupConfig) -> T.VoidResult;
    deleteCgroup @20 (path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    moveToCgroup @21 (pid :T.ProcessId, cgroup :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    getCgroupUsage @22 (path :Text) -> (usage :ProcessResourceUsage);

    # Namespaces
    listNamespaces @23 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (namespaces :List(NamespaceInfo));
    getNamespace @24 (pid :T.ProcessId, type :NamespaceType) -> (info :NamespaceInfo);

    # Open files & connections
    listOpenFiles @25 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (files :List(OpenFile));
    listConnections @26 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (connections :List(ProcessConnection));

    # Environment
    getEnvironment @27 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (env :T.StringMap);

    # Events
    subscribe @28 (filter :ProcessEventFilter) -> (subscription :ProcessSubscription);
}

# ── Process Info ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessInfo {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    parentPid @1 :T.ProcessId;
    name @2 :Text;
    command @3 :Text;
    arguments @4 :List(Text);
    executable @5 :Text;
    workingDirectory @6 :Text;
    user @7 :Text;
    group @8 :Text;
    state @9 :ProcessState;
    nice @10 :Int8;
    priority @11 :Int32;
    pgid @12 :UInt32;
    sessionId @13 :UInt32;
    tty @14 :Text;
    resourceUsage @15 :ProcessResourceUsage;
    startedAt @16 :T.Timestamp;
    cpuTime @17 :T.Duration;
    threadCount @18 :UInt32;
    children @19 :List(T.ProcessId);
    cgroup @20 :Text;
    capabilityCount @21 :UInt32;
    securityContext @22 :Text;
    # Exit code (if exited).
    exitCode @23 :Int32;
}

enum ProcessState {
    running @0;
    sleeping @1;
    waiting @2;
    stopped @3;
    zombie @4;
    dead @5;
    traced @6;
    idle @7;
}

# ── Process Tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessTree {
    root @0 :ProcessTreeNode;
    totalProcesses @1 :UInt32;
    maxDepth @2 :UInt32;
}

struct ProcessTreeNode {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    name @1 :Text;
    state @2 :ProcessState;
    cpuPercent @3 :Float32;
    memoryBytes @4 :UInt64;
    children @5 :List(ProcessTreeNode);
    depth @6 :UInt32;
}

# ── Process Filter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessFilter {
    name @0 :Text;
    state @1 :ProcessState;
    user @2 :Text;
    minCpu @3 :Float32;
    maxCpu @4 :Float32;
    minMemory @5 :UInt64;
    maxMemory @6 :UInt64;
    cgroup @7 :Text;
    sessionId @8 :UInt32;
    pgid @9 :UInt32;
    tty @10 :Text;
}

# ── Resource Usage ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessResourceUsage {
    cpuPercent @0 :Float32;
    memoryRss @1 :UInt64;
    memoryVirtual @2 :UInt64;
    memoryShared @3 :UInt64;
    memoryPercent @4 :Float32;
    swapBytes @5 :UInt64;
    diskReadBytes @6 :UInt64;
    diskWriteBytes @7 :UInt64;
    networkBytesSent @8 :UInt64;
    networkBytesReceived @9 :UInt64;
    openFiles @10 :UInt32;
    threads @11 :UInt32;
    contextSwitchesVoluntary @12 :UInt64;
    contextSwitchesInvoluntary @13 :UInt64;
    pageFaultsMinor @14 :UInt64;
    pageFaultsMajor @15 :UInt64;
    ioWaitTime @16 :T.Duration;
}

struct SystemResourceUsage {
    totalProcesses @0 :UInt32;
    totalThreads @1 :UInt32;
    cpuUsageTotal @2 :Float32;
    memoryUsed @3 :UInt64;
    memoryTotal @4 :UInt64;
    swapUsed @5 :UInt64;
    swapTotal @6 :UInt64;
    diskReadTotal @7 :UInt64;
    diskWriteTotal @8 :UInt64;
    networkTotal @9 :UInt64;
    topCpu @10 :List(ProcessInfo);
    topMemory @11 :List(ProcessInfo);
    topDisk @12 :List(ProcessInfo);
    topNetwork @13 :List(ProcessInfo);
}

# ── Cgroup ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct CgroupInfo {
    path @0 :Text;
    processCount @1 :UInt32;
    config @2 :CgroupConfig;
    usage @3 :ProcessResourceUsage;
    children @4 :List(Text);
    frozen @5 :Bool;
}

struct CgroupConfig {
    cpuWeight @0 :UInt32;
    cpuMax @1 :Text;
    memoryLow @2 :UInt64;
    memoryHigh @3 :UInt64;
    memoryMax @4 :UInt64;
    memorySwapMax @5 :UInt64;
    ioWeight @6 :UInt32;
    pidsMax @7 :UInt32;
}

# ── Namespaces ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct NamespaceInfo {
    type @0 :NamespaceType;
    id @1 :UInt64;
    processes @2 :List(T.ProcessId);
    initial @3 :Bool;
}

enum NamespaceType {
    pid @0;
    net @1;
    mount @2;
    uts @3;
    ipc @4;
    user @5;
    cgroup @6;
    time @7;
}

# ── Open Files & Connections ─────────────────────────────────────────

struct OpenFile {
    fd @0 :UInt32;
    path @1 :Text;
    type @2 :OpenFileType;
    mode @3 :Text;
    offset @4 :UInt64;
    size @5 :UInt64;
}

enum OpenFileType {
    regular @0;
    directory @1;
    socket @2;
    pipe @3;
    device @4;
    symlink @5;
    unknown @6;
}

struct ProcessConnection {
    fd @0 :UInt32;
    type @1 :ConnectionType;
    localAddress @2 :Text;
    localPort @3 :UInt16;
    remoteAddress @4 :Text;
    remotePort @5 :UInt16;
    state @6 :ConnectionState;
    protocol @7 :Text;
}

enum ConnectionType {
    tcp @0;
    udp @1;
    unix @2;
    netlink @3;
    custom @4;
}

enum ConnectionState {
    established @0;
    synSent @1;
    synRecv @2;
    finWait1 @3;
    finWait2 @4;
    timeWait @5;
    close @6;
    closeWait @7;
    lastAck @8;
    listen @9;
    closing @10;
}

# ── Process Session & Group ─────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessSession {
    sessionId @0 :UInt32;
    leader @1 :T.ProcessId;
    controllingTty @2 :Text;
    processes @3 :List(T.ProcessId);
    foregroundGroup @4 :UInt32;
}

struct ProcessGroup {
    pgid @0 :UInt32;
    leader @1 :T.ProcessId;
    session @2 :UInt32;
    processes @3 :List(T.ProcessId);
}

# ── Process Events ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct ProcessEventFilter {
    pids @0 :List(T.ProcessId);
    eventTypes @1 :List(ProcessEventKind);
    since @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

enum ProcessEventKind {
    spawned @0;
    exited @1;
    signaled @2;
    stopped @3;
    resumed @4;
    cgroupChanged @5;
    resourceExceeded @6;
    custom @7;
}

interface ProcessSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(ProcessEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct ProcessEvent {
    union {
        spawned @0 :ProcessInfo;
        exited @1 :ProcessExitEvent;
        signaled @2 :ProcessSignalEvent;
        stopped @3 :T.ProcessId;
        resumed @4 :T.ProcessId;
        resourceExceeded @5 :ResourceExceededEvent;
        custom @6 :Data;
    }
}

struct ProcessExitEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    exitStatus @1 :T.ExitStatus;
    timestamp @2 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct ProcessSignalEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    signal @1 :T.SignalKind;
    sender @2 :T.ProcessId;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct ResourceExceededEvent {
    pid @0 :T.ProcessId;
    resource @1 :Text;
    limit @2 :UInt64;
    actual @3 :UInt64;
    timestamp @4 :T.Timestamp;
    # Action taken (kill, throttle, warn).
    action @5 :Text;
}

using T = import "types.capnp";

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# System — system information, hardware details, thermal, fans,
#          power supply, chassis, firmware, and system operations
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

interface SystemService {
    # System
    getInfo @0 () -> (info :SystemInfo);
    getHostname @1 () -> (hostname :Text);
    setHostname @2 (hostname :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Hardware
    getCpuInfo @3 () -> (cpu :CpuInfo);
    getMemoryInfo @4 () -> (memory :MemoryInfo);
    getSwapInfo @5 () -> (swap :SwapInfo);
    getDiskInfo @6 () -> (disks :List(DiskInfo));
    getGpuInfo @7 () -> (gpus :List(GpuInfo));

    # Thermal
    getTemperatures @8 () -> (sensors :List(TemperatureSensor));
    getFans @9 () -> (fans :List(FanInfo));
    getThermalZones @10 () -> (zones :List(ThermalZone));

    # Power
    getPowerSupplies @11 () -> (supplies :List(PowerSupply));

    # State
    getLoad @12 () -> (load :LoadInfo);
    getUptime @13 () -> (uptime :UptimeInfo);
    getUsers @14 () -> (users :List(LoggedInUser));
    getTime @15 () -> (time :SystemTime);
    setTime @16 (time :T.Timestamp) -> T.VoidResult;
    getTimezone @17 () -> (timezone :TimezoneInfo);
    setTimezone @18 (timezone :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Firmware & chassis
    getFirmwareInfo @19 () -> (firmware :FirmwareInfo);
    getChassisInfo @20 () -> (chassis :ChassisInfo);

    # Kernel
    getKernelInfo @21 () -> (kernel :KernelInfo);

    # Architecture
    getArchitecture @22 () -> (arch :ArchitectureInfo);

    # Capabilities
    getCapabilities @23 () -> (capabilities :List(SystemCapability));

    # Events
    subscribe @24 () -> (subscription :SystemSubscription);

    # Operations
    shutdown @25 (delay :T.Duration, reason :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    reboot @26 (delay :T.Duration, reason :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    suspend @27 () -> T.VoidResult;
    hibernate @28 () -> T.VoidResult;
    cancelShutdown @29 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

# ── System Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SystemInfo {

    threads @3 :UInt32;
    baseFrequency @4 :UInt64;
    maxFrequency @5 :UInt64;

# ── Memory Info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct SwapDevice {
    device @0 :Text;
    sizeBytes @1 :UInt64;
    usedBytes @2 :UInt64;
    priority @3 :Int32;
}

# ── Disk Info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct DiskInfo {

    emmc @3;

    optical @5;

    unknown @3;
}

# ── GPU Info ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

struct GpuInfo {
