using T = import "types.capnp";

# Peripherals — mouse, keyboard, trackpad, gamepad, stylus,
#               webcam, external sensors

interface PeripheralService {
    listDevices @0 (filter :PeripheralFilter) -> (devices :List(PeripheralInfo));
    getDevice @1 (deviceId :Text) -> (device :PeripheralInfo);

    # Mouse
    getMouseConfig @2 () -> (config :MouseConfig);
    setMouseConfig @3 (config :MouseConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Keyboard
    getKeyboardConfig @4 () -> (config :KeyboardConfig);
    setKeyboardConfig @5 (config :KeyboardConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Trackpad
    getTrackpadConfig @6 () -> (config :TrackpadConfig);
    setTrackpadConfig @7 (config :TrackpadConfig) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Gamepad
    getGamepad @8 (deviceId :Text) -> (gamepad :GamepadInfo);

    # Webcam
    listWebcams @9 () -> (webcams :List(WebcamInfo));
    getWebcam @10 (deviceId :Text) -> (webcam :WebcamInfo);

    # Events
    subscribe @11 () -> (subscription :PeripheralSubscription);
}

struct PeripheralInfo {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    type @2 :PeripheralType;
    vendor @3 :Text;
    product @4 :Text;
    connected @5 :Bool;
    battery @6 :Int32;       # -1 if N/A
    serial @7 :Text;
}

enum PeripheralType {
    mouse @0;
    keyboard @1;
    trackpad @2;
    gamepad @3;
    stylus @4;
    webcam @5;
    touchScreen @6;
    sensor @7;
    custom @8;
}

struct PeripheralFilter {
    type @0 :PeripheralType;
    connected @1 :T.BoolFilter;
}

struct MouseConfig {
    sensitivity @0 :Float32;       # 1.0 = default
    acceleration @1 :Float32;
    naturalScrolling @2 :Bool;
    leftHanded @3 :Bool;
    doubleClickSpeed @4 :UInt32;   # ms
    scrollSpeed @5 :Float32;
    middleEmulation @6 :Bool;
    disableTrackpadWhileTyping @7 :Bool;
    buttonMapping @8 :T.StringMap;
}

struct KeyboardConfig {
    repeatDelay @0 :UInt32;        # ms
    repeatRate @1 :UInt32;         # chars/sec
    layout @2 :Text;               # "us", "de", "fr"
    variant @3 :Text;
    numlock @4 :Bool;
    capsLockRemap @5 :Text;        # Remap capslock to: "ctrl", "escape", "none"
    composeKey @6 :Text;
}

struct TrackpadConfig {
    sensitivity @0 :Float32;
    naturalScrolling @1 :Bool;
    tapToClick @2 :Bool;
    twoFingerScroll @3 :Bool;
    threeFingerSwipe @4 :Bool;
    fourFingerSwipe @5 :Bool;
    disableWhileTyping @6 :Bool;
    palmRejection @7 :Bool;
    edgeScrolling @8 :Bool;
    clickMethod @9 :Text;         # "buttonareas", "clickfinger"
}

struct GamepadInfo {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    connected @2 :Bool;
    battery @3 :Int32;
    buttons @4 :UInt32;
    axes @5 :UInt32;
    vibration @6 :Bool;
    mapping @7 :Text;             # "standard", "custom"
}

struct WebcamInfo {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    connected @2 :Bool;
    resolution @3 :Text;          # "1920x1080"
    fps @4 :UInt32;
    inUse @5 :Bool;
    usingBy @6 :Text;             # Process name
}

interface PeripheralSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(PeripheralEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct PeripheralEvent {
    union {
        connected @0 :PeripheralInfo;
        disconnected @1 :Text;
        batteryChanged @2 :BatteryChangedEvent;
        custom @3 :Data;
    }
}

struct BatteryChangedEvent {
    deviceId @0 :Text;
    previous @1 :Int32;
    current @2 :Int32;
}
package.capnp — ADD rollback, pinned versions, orphan detection
capnpcapnp# Add to PackageManagerService interface:
    rollback @25 (packageName :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    pin @26 (packageName :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    unpin @27 (packageName :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listPinned @28 () -> (packages :List(PackageInfo));
    listOrphans @29 () -> (packages :List(PackageInfo));
    cleanOrphans @30 () -> T.VoidResult;
    history @31 (packageName :Text) -> (entries :List(PackageHistoryEntry));

# Add to PackageInfo:
    pinned @12 :Bool;
    rollbackAvailable @13 :Bool;
    orphan @14 :Bool;

struct PackageHistoryEntry {
    action @0 :Text;       # "install", "upgrade", "remove"
    version @1 :Text;
    timestamp @2 :T.Timestamp;
    by @3 :Text;           # "user", "dependency", "auto"
}
app.capnp — ADD permissions, startup impact, resource limits
capnpcapnp# Add to AppManagerService interface:
    getPermissions @20 (appId :T.AppId) -> (permissions :List(AppPermission));
    setPermission @21 (appId :T.AppId, permission :Text, granted :Bool) -> T.VoidResult;
    getStartupImpact @22 (appId :T.AppId) -> (impact :StartupImpact);
    setResourceLimit @23 (appId :T.AppId, limit :ResourceLimit) -> T.VoidResult;
    getResourceLimit @24 (appId :T.AppId) -> (limit :ResourceLimit);
    getDefaultApps @25 () -> (defaults :List(DefaultApp));
    setDefaultApp @26 (mimeType :Text, appId :T.AppId) -> T.VoidResult;

struct AppPermission {
    name @0 :Text;
    description @1 :Text;
    granted @2 :Bool;
    required @3 :Bool;
    dangerous @4 :Bool;
}

struct StartupImpact {
    appId @0 :T.AppId;
    startupTime @1 :T.Duration;
    autostart @2 :Bool;
    # Impact rating: "high", "medium", "low", "none"
    impact @3 :Text;
    cpuTimeAtStartup @4 :Float32;
}

struct ResourceLimit {
    appId @0 :T.AppId;
    maxCpuPercent @1 :Float32;
    maxMemoryBytes @2 :UInt64;
    maxIoBytesPerSec @3 :UInt64;
    maxNetworkBytesPerSec @4 :UInt64;
    nice @5 :Int32;
    ioprio @6 :UInt32;
}

struct DefaultApp {
    mimeType @0 :Text;
    appId @1 :T.AppId;
    appName @2 :Text;
}

CLI Methods — Batch 5: Hardware & Devices
bashbash# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  BATCH 5: HARDWARE & DEVICES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── CPU ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Brief summary (bare word)
cpu
# Output:
#   ⚡ CPU
#   ├─ Model     AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS
#   ├─ Cores     8C/16T
#   ├─ Usage     ██████░░░░░░  48%
#   ├─ Temp      62°C
#   ├─ Freq      3.2 GHz (base: 3.8, boost: 5.1)
#   └─ Governor  schedutil

cpu info                            → full CPU details (model, cores, caches, flags, microcode)
cpu cores                           → per-core usage
cpu usage                           → total CPU usage
cpu temp                            → temperature
cpu freq                            → current frequency
cpu freq min                        → minimum frequency
cpu freq max                        → maximum frequency
cpu freq set 3000                   → set frequency (MHz)
cpu governor                        → current governor
cpu governor list                   → available governors
cpu governor set performance        → set governor
cpu governor set powersave          → set governor
cpu governor set schedutil          → set governor
cpu cache                           → cache sizes (L1, L2, L3)
cpu flags                           → CPU feature flags (sse, avx, etc.)
cpu microcode                       → microcode version
cpu topology                        → core/thread topology map
cpu power                           → CPU power draw (watts)

watch cpu                           → stream CPU usage
watch cpu temp                      → stream temperature

# ── MEMORY ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Brief summary (bare word)
memory
# Output:
#   🧠 Memory
#   ├─ RAM       ████████░░░░  12.4 / 16.0 GB  (78%)
#   ├─ Swap      ██░░░░░░░░░░  0.8 / 8.0 GB   (10%)
#   ├─ Buffers   1.2 GB
#   └─ Cached    3.4 GB

memory info                         → full memory details
memory usage                        → RAM usage
memory swap                         → swap usage
memory buffers                      → buffer usage
memory cached                       → cached memory
memory available                    → available memory
memory total                        → total memory
memory used                         → used memory
memory shared                       → shared memory
memory map                          → memory map (who uses what)
memory top                          → top memory consumers
memory pressure                     → memory pressure status (nominal, warning, critical)
memory reclaim                      → trigger memory reclaim (drop caches)
memory reclaim safe                 → reclaim safe caches only
memory reclaim all                  → reclaim all caches

watch memory                        → stream memory changes

# ── DISKS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
disks                               → list all disks
disks where type == ssd             → SSDs only
disks where type == hdd             → HDDs only
disks where removable               → removable disks
disks where encrypted               → encrypted disks

disk /dev/sda                       → disk summary
disk /dev/sda info                  → full disk details
disk /dev/sda smart                 → SMART health (temp, life, errors, hours)
disk /dev/sda benchmark             → disk speed benchmark (seq read/write, 4K random)

# Partitions
disk /dev/sda partitions            → list partitions on disk
disk /dev/sda1 info                 → partition details
disk /dev/sda1 mount /mnt/data      → mount partition
disk /dev/sda1 unmount              → unmount partition
disk /dev/sda1 format ext4          → format partition (⚠ destructive)

# Usage
disk usage                          → disk usage for all mounts
disk usage /                        → usage for root
disk usage /home                    → usage for /home
disk free                           → free space for all disks
disk free /dev/sda                  → free space for specific disk

# I/O
disk io                             → current disk I/O
disk io /dev/sda                    → I/O for specific disk
disk iostat                         → detailed I/O statistics

# Encryption
disk /dev/sda1 encrypt              → encrypt partition
disk /dev/sda1 decrypt              → decrypt partition
disk /dev/sda1 unlock "password"    → unlock encrypted partition

# Maintenance
disk trim /dev/sda                  → run TRIM (SSD)
disk check /dev/sda1                → filesystem check
disk repair /dev/sda1               → filesystem repair

watch disks                         → stream disk events
watch disk io                       → stream disk I/O

# ── GPU ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Brief summary (bare word)
gpu
# Output:

#   ├─ Model      NVIDIA RTX 4060

gpu info                            → full GPU details
gpu vram                            → VRAM usage
gpu usage                           → GPU utilization
gpu temp                            → temperature

gpu fan set target 70               → auto target temperature
gpu power                           → power draw
gpu power limit                     → power limit
gpu power limit set 100             → set power limit (watts)
gpu clock                           → current clock speeds
gpu memory-clock                    → memory clock
gpu driver                          → driver version
gpu processes                       → GPU-accelerated processes
gpu compute-mode                    → compute mode
gpu compute-mode set default        → default compute
gpu compute-mode set exclusive      → exclusive compute
gpu compute-mode set prohibited     → prohibited compute

watch gpu                           → stream GPU events
watch gpu temp                      → stream temperature
watch gpu processes                 → stream GPU process changes

# ── FANS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
fans                                → list all fans
fan 0                               → fan 0 summary
fan 0 info                          → full fan details

fan 0 set manual 1500               → set RPM

fan 0 set profile balanced          → balanced profile
fan 0 set profile performance       → performance profile

fans profiles                       → list fan profiles
fans profile "silent"               → activate profile

watch fans                          → stream fan speed changes

# ── THERMALS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Brief summary (bare word)
thermals
# Output:

thermals zones                      → list all thermal zones
thermals zone cpu                   → CPU thermal zone
thermals zone gpu                   → GPU thermal zone
thermals zone battery               → battery thermal zone
thermals throttle                   → current throttle status
thermals throttle-history           → throttle history

watch thermals                      → stream thermal changes
watch thermals throttle             → stream throttle events

# ── PORTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
ports                               → list all ports (USB, Thunderbolt, etc.)
ports where type == usb             → USB ports
ports where type == thunderbolt     → Thunderbolt ports
ports where connected               → ports with devices
ports where type == usb where connected  → connected USB ports

port usb-1                          → port summary

port usb-1 power off                → disable port power

thunderbolt device <id> deauthorize → deauthorize device

watch ports                         → stream port events
watch usb                           → stream USB events

# List (plural = list)
peripherals                         → list all peripherals
peripherals where type == mouse     → mice

# Mouse
mouse                               → mouse config

mouse acceleration off              → disable acceleration
mouse natural-scroll on             → enable natural scrolling
mouse natural-scroll off            → disable natural scrolling
mouse left-handed on                → left-handed mode
mouse left-handed off               → right-handed mode

mouse scroll-speed 1.0              → scroll speed

# Keyboard
keyboard                            → keyboard config

keyboard layout de                  → set German layout
keyboard repeat-delay 500           → key repeat delay (ms)

keyboard numlock on                 → enable numlock at boot
keyboard numlock off                → disable numlock at boot
keyboard capslock remap ctrl        → remap capslock to ctrl
keyboard capslock remap escape      → remap capslock to escape
keyboard capslock remap none        → restore capslock

trackpad                            → trackpad config
trackpad sensitivity 1.0            → set sensitivity

trackpad tap-to-click off           → disable tap-to-click

trackpad four-finger-swipe on       → enable four-finger swipe

trackpad click-method clickfinger   → click method

# Brief summary (bare word)
audio

battery

CLI Methods — Batch 6: Apps & Packages
bashbash# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  BATCH 6: APPS & PACKAGES
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── APPS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
apps                                → list all installed apps
apps where installed                → installed apps
apps where running                  → running apps
apps where autostart                → autostart apps
apps where type == gui              → GUI apps
apps where type == cli              → CLI apps
apps where type == daemon           → daemon apps
apps where category == "Development"  → dev apps
apps where name contains "firefox"  → search apps
apps where recently-used            → recently used apps
apps where size > 100MB             → large apps

app "Firefox"                       → app summary
app "Firefox" info                  → full app details
app "Firefox" launch                → launch app
app "Firefox" launch --args "--safe-mode"  → launch with args
app "Firefox" close                 → close app gracefully
app "Firefox" close --force         → force close

# Permissions
app "Firefox" permissions           → list permissions
app "Firefox" permission camera on  → grant camera
app "Firefox" permission camera off → revoke camera
app "Firefox" permission microphone on  → grant microphone
app "Firefox" permission location on    → grant location
app "Firefox" permission files read     → grant file read
app "Firefox" permission files write    → grant file write
app "Firefox" permission network on     → grant network
app "Firefox" permission notification on  → grant notifications
app "Firefox" permission tray on        → grant system tray

# Autostart
app "Firefox" autostart             → autostart status
app "Firefox" autostart on          → enable autostart
app "Firefox" autostart off         → disable autostart

# Default apps
apps defaults                       → list default apps (browser, email, terminal, editor)
app set-default browser "Firefox"   → set default browser
app set-default terminal "Terminal" → set default terminal
app set-default editor "Code"       → set default editor
app set-default email "Thunderbird" → set default email
app set-default file-manager "Files"  → set default file manager

# Resource limits
app "Firefox" resource-limit        → current resource limits
app "Firefox" resource-limit cpu 50 → limit CPU to 50%
app "Firefox" resource-limit memory 2GB → limit memory to 2GB
app "Firefox" resource-limit off    → remove limits

# Startup impact
app "Firefox" startup-impact        → startup impact (time, CPU, autostart)

# Install / Remove
app install Firefox                 → install app
app remove Firefox                  → remove app
app remove Firefox --data           → remove app and user data

# Recently used
app recent                          → recently used apps
app recent 20                       → last 20 apps

# Windows
app "Firefox" windows               → windows belonging to app

watch apps                          → stream app events

# ── SERVICES ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
services                            → list all services
services where running              → running services
services where stopped              → stopped services
services where enabled              → enabled (auto-start) services
services where failed               → failed services
services where name contains "ssh"  → search services
services where type == system       → system services
services where type == user         → user services

service sshd                        → service summary
service sshd info                   → full service details
service sshd start                  → start service
service sshd stop                   → stop service
service sshd restart                → restart service
service sshd reload                 → reload config
service sshd status                 → service status
service sshd enable                 → enable auto-start
service sshd disable                → disable auto-start
service sshd logs                   → service logs
service sshd logs --since 1h        → logs from last hour
service sshd logs --lines 50        → last 50 log lines
service sshd logs --follow          → follow logs

# Bulk
services restart-all-failed         → restart all failed services

watch services                      → stream service events
watch services where failed         → stream failure events

# ── PROCESSES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
processes                           → list all processes
processes where cpu > 10            → high CPU
processes where memory > 1GB        → high memory
processes where user == "lufuno"    → user's processes
processes where name contains "node"  → search processes
processes where state == zombie     → zombie processes
processes where state == sleeping   → sleeping processes
processes where ppid == 1           → direct children of init

process 2103                        → process summary
process 2103 info                   → full process details
process 2103 tree                   → process tree (children)
process 2103 files                  → open files
process 2103 connections            → network connections
process 2103 env                    → environment variables
process 2103 limits                 → resource limits
process 2103 io                     → I/O statistics
process 2103 threads                → thread list
process 2103 maps                   → memory maps
process 2103 fd                     → file descriptors

# Actions
process 2103 kill                   → send SIGTERM
process 2103 kill --signal 9        → send SIGKILL
process 2103 kill --signal HUP      → send SIGHUP
process 2103 suspend                → send SIGSTOP (pause)
process 2103 resume                 → send SIGCONT (resume)
process 2103 renice 10              → set nice value
process 2103 renice -5              → higher priority

# Sorting
processes --sort cpu                → sort by CPU
processes --sort memory             → sort by memory
processes --sort pid                → sort by PID
processes --sort name               → sort by name
processes --top 20                  → top 20 processes

watch processes                     → stream process events
watch processes where cpu > 50      → stream high CPU events

# ── PACKAGES ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
packages                            → list all installed packages
packages where name contains "python"  → search packages
packages where outdated             → outdated packages
packages where orphaned             → orphaned packages (no dependents)
packages where pinned               → pinned packages
packages where explicit             → explicitly installed
packages where auto                 → installed as dependencies
packages where size > 100MB         → large packages
packages where source == "repo"     → from repository
packages where source == "local"    → locally installed

package "firefox"                   → package summary
package "firefox" info              → full package details
package "firefox" files             → files owned by package
package "firefox" deps              → dependencies
package "firefox" rdeps             → reverse dependencies (what depends on this)
package "firefox" history           → install/upgrade/remove history

# Install / Remove
package install firefox             → install package
package install firefox --version 128.0  → install specific version
package remove firefox              → remove package
package remove firefox --purge      → remove with config files
package reinstall firefox           → reinstall

# Updates
packages update                     → update package database
packages upgrade                    → upgrade all packages
packages upgrade firefox            → upgrade specific package
packages upgrade --dry-run          → preview upgrades

# Pinning
package pin firefox                 → pin at current version
package unpin firefox               → unpin

# Rollback
package rollback firefox            → rollback to previous version

# Orphans
packages orphans                    → list orphaned packages
packages orphans clean              → remove orphaned packages

watch packages                      → stream package events
watch packages where outdated       → stream outdated packages

# ── UPDATES ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

updates                             → list available updates
updates check                       → check for updates
updates install                     → install all updates
updates install --security          → security updates only
updates install --dry-run           → preview updates
updates auto                        → auto-update status
updates auto on                     → enable auto-updates
updates auto off                    → disable auto-updates
updates auto schedule "03:00"       → schedule auto-updates
updates history                     → update history
updates rollback                    → rollback last update

watch updates                       → stream update events

# ── REPOSITORIES ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
repos                               → list repositories
repos where enabled                 → enabled repos
repos where disabled                → disabled repos

repo "main"                         → repo summary
repo "main" info                    → full repo details
repo "main" enable                  → enable repo
repo "main" disable                 → disable repo
repo "main" packages                → list packages from repo
repo add "custom" "https://repo.example.com"  → add repo
repo remove "custom"                → remove repo
repo "main" refresh                 → refresh repo
repos refresh                       → refresh all repos

# ── FLATPAK ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

flatpak apps                        → list Flatpak apps
flatpak install org.mozilla.Firefox  → install Flatpak app
flatpak remove org.mozilla.Firefox   → remove Flatpak app
flatpak update                      → update all Flatpak apps
flatpak runtimes                    → list Flatpak runtimes
flatpak remotes                     → list Flatpak remotes
flatpak remote-add flathub "https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo"  → add remote

# ── SNAP ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

snap apps                           → list Snap apps
snap install firefox                → install Snap
snap remove firefox                 → remove Snap
snap refresh                       → update all Snaps
snap info firefox                   → Snap info
snap services                       → Snap services

# ── APPIMAGE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

appimages                           → list AppImages
appimage ~/App.AppImage integrate   → integrate AppImage (add to launcher)
appimage ~/App.AppImage remove      → remove integration

# ── FLATPAK PERMISSIONS ───────────────────────────────────────────────

flatpak permissions org.mozilla.Firefox  → list Flatpak permissions
flatpak permission org.mozilla.Firefox camera on  → grant
flatpak permission org.mozilla.Firefox camera off → revoke

Edge Cases
CPU / MEMORY / THERMALS
texttextcpu governor set "invalid"
  → "Governor 'invalid' not available."
  → "Available: performance, powersave, schedutil, ondemand, conservative, userspace"
  → "Run: cpu governor list"

cpu freq set 10000
  → "Frequency 10 GHz exceeds CPU maximum (5.1 GHz)."
  → "Maximum: 5100 MHz"

memory reclaim all
  → "Reclaiming all caches... 3.4 GB freed."
  → "⚠ May cause temporary slowdown as caches rebuild."

memory pressure → critical
  → "⚠ Memory pressure: CRITICAL"
  → "Available: 256 MB (1.6%)"
  → "Top consumers: firefox (2.1 GB), code (1.4 GB)"
  → "Consider: closing apps or adding swap."

memory top → all processes same
  → Paginated. "Showing 1-20 of 312 processes. Use --page 2."

thermals → critical temperature
  → "⚠ CRITICAL: CPU at 98°C! Thermal throttling active."
  → "Fan at maximum. Check cooling system."
  → "Consider: closing heavy applications."

thermals → throttle event
  → "Throttle event: CPU frequency reduced from 4.5 GHz to 2.1 GHz"
  → "Cause: thermal limit (95°C)"
  → "Duration: 12s"
DISKS
texttextdisk /dev/sda1 format ext4
  → "⚠ DESTRUCTIVE: All data on /dev/sda1 will be permanently lost."
  → "This cannot be undone."
  → "Use --force to confirm."

disk /dev/sda1 mount /mnt/data → already mounted
  → "/dev/sda1 is already mounted at /mnt/old."
  → "Unmount first: disk /dev/sda1 unmount"
  → "Or force remount: disk /dev/sda1 mount /mnt/data --force"

disk /dev/sda1 unmount → in use
  → "Cannot unmount /dev/sda1: device is busy."
  → "Processes using this mount:"
  → "  PID 2103 firefox (cwd: /mnt/data)"
  → "  PID 3421 code (file: /mnt/data/project/main.rs)"
  → "Use --force to unmount anyway."

disk trim /dev/nvme0n1 → not SSD
  → "TRIM is only supported on SSDs."
  → "/dev/sda is an HDD."

disk /dev/sda smart → SMART unavailable
  → "SMART data unavailable for /dev/sda."
  → "Disk may not support SMART or driver not loaded."

disk usage / → 95% full
  → "⚠ Root filesystem is 95% full (47 GB remaining)."
  → "Top consumers:"
  → "  /var/log     12 GB"
  → "  /home/.cache 8 GB"
  → "  /var/cache   5 GB"
  → "Consider: disk clean or: packages orphans clean"

disk check /dev/sda1 → filesystem dirty
  → "Filesystem on /dev/sda1 is dirty. Unmount required."
  → "Run: disk /dev/sda1 unmount && disk check /dev/sda1"

disk /dev/sda1 encrypt → already encrypted
  → "/dev/sda1 is already encrypted (LUKS)."

disk /dev/sda1 decrypt → not encrypted
  → "/dev/sda1 is not encrypted."

disk /dev/sdb eject → in use
  → "Cannot eject: USB device in use."
  → "Processes: file-manager (PID 4521)"
  → "Run: disk /dev/sdb1 unmount first."

using T = import "types.capnp";

interface MediaService {
    # Playback
    getInfo @0 () -> (info :PlaybackInfo);
    play @1 (path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    playUrl @2 (url :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    pause @3 () -> T.VoidResult;
    resume @4 () -> T.VoidResult;
    stop @5 () -> T.VoidResult;
    next @6 () -> T.VoidResult;
    previous @7 () -> T.VoidResult;
    seek @8 (position :T.Duration) -> T.VoidResult;
    seekRelative @9 (offset :Int64) -> T.VoidResult;
    getPosition @10 () -> (position :T.Duration);
    getDuration @11 () -> (duration :T.Duration);

    # Volume (independent from system audio)
    getVolume @12 () -> (volume :Float32);
    setVolume @13 (volume :Float32) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Speed
    getSpeed @14 () -> (speed :Float32);
    setSpeed @15 (speed :Float32) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Metadata
    getMetadata @16 (path :Text) -> (metadata :MediaMetadata);

    # Queue / Playlist
    getQueue @17 () -> (tracks :List(TrackInfo));
    addToQueue @18 (path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    removeFromQueue @19 (index :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;
    clearQueue @20 () -> T.VoidResult;
    shuffleQueue @21 () -> T.VoidResult;

    # Playlists
    listPlaylists @22 () -> (playlists :List(PlaylistInfo));
    getPlaylist @23 (id :Text) -> (playlist :PlaylistInfo);
    createPlaylist @24 (name :Text) -> (id :Text);
    deletePlaylist @25 (id :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    addToPlaylist @26 (playlistId :Text, path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    removeFromPlaylist @27 (playlistId :Text, index :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Media scanning
    scan @28 (path :Text) -> (files :List(MediaFile>);

    # Events
    subscribe @29 () -> (subscription :MediaSubscription);
}

struct PlaybackInfo {
    state @0 :PlaybackState;
    current @1 :TrackInfo;
    position @2 :T.Duration;
    duration @3 :T.Duration;
    volume @4 :Float32;
    speed @5 :Float32;
    queueLength @6 :UInt32;
    queueIndex @7 :UInt32;
    shuffle @8 :Bool;
    repeat @9 :RepeatMode;
}

enum PlaybackState {
    stopped @0;
    playing @1;
    paused @2;
    buffering @3;
    error @4;
}

enum RepeatMode {
    off @0;
    track @1;
    queue @2;
}

struct TrackInfo {
    index @0 :UInt32;
    path @1 :Text;
    title @2 :Text;
    artist @3 :Text;
    album @4 :Text;
    duration @5 :T.Duration;
    format @6 :Text;
    bitrate @7 :UInt32;
    sampleRate @8 :UInt32;
    channels @9 :UInt32;
}

struct MediaMetadata {
    title @0 :Text;
    artist @1 :Text;
    album @2 :Text;
    albumArtist @3 :Text;
    year @4 :UInt32;
    track @5 :UInt32;
    genre @6 :Text;
    duration @7 :T.Duration;
    format @8 :Text;
    bitrate @9 :UInt32;
    sampleRate @10 :UInt32;
    channels @11 :UInt32;
    coverArt @12 :Data;
}

struct PlaylistInfo {
    id @0 :Text;
    name @1 :Text;
    trackCount @2 :UInt32;
    duration @3 :T.Duration;
    tracks @4 :List(TrackInfo);
}

struct MediaFile {
    path @0 :Text;
    type @1 :Text;
    size @2 :UInt64;
    metadata @3 :MediaMetadata;
}

interface MediaSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(MediaEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct MediaEvent {
    union {
        stateChanged @0 :PlaybackState;
        trackChanged @1 :TrackInfo;
        positionChanged @2 :T.Duration;
        volumeChanged @3 :Float32;
        queueChanged @4 :Void;
        error @5 :T.Error;
        custom @6 :Data;
    }
}

interface NotificationService {

    get @1 (id :Text) -> (notification :Notification);

    clearHistory @10 () -> T.VoidResult;

}

struct Notification {
    id @0 :Text;
    app @1 :Text;
    title @2 :Text;
    body @3 :Text;
    urgency @4 :Urgency;
    category @5 :Text;
    timestamp @6 :T.Timestamp;
    read @7 :Bool;
    dismissed @8 :Bool;
    actions @9 :List(NotificationAction);
    icon @10 :Text;
    image @11 :Text;
    progress @12 :Float32;
}

struct NewNotification {
    app @0 :Text;
    title @1 :Text;

using T = import "types.capnp";

interface GitService {
    # Repository info
    getInfo @0 (path :Text) -> (info :GitInfo);
    getStatus @1 (path :Text) -> (status :GitStatus);

    # Branches
    listBranches @2 (path :Text) -> (branches :List(GitBranch));
    getBranch @3 (path :Text) -> (branch :GitBranch);
    checkout @4 (path :Text, branch :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    createBranch @5 (path :Text, name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    deleteBranch @6 (path :Text, name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Commit
    log @7 (path :Text, options :LogOptions) -> (commits :List(GitCommit));
    commit @8 (path :Text, message :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    diff @9 (path :Text, options :DiffOptions) -> (diff :Text);

    # Staging
    add @10 (path :Text, files :List(Text)) -> T.VoidResult;
    unstage @11 (path :Text, files :List(Text)) -> T.VoidResult;
    reset @12 (path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Remote
    listRemotes @13 (path :Text) -> (remotes :List(GitRemote));
    fetch @14 (path :Text, remote :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    pull @15 (path :Text, remote :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    push @16 (path :Text, remote :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Stash
    stash @17 (path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    stashPop @18 (path :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    stashList @19 (path :Text) -> (stashes :List(GitStash));

    # Tags
    listTags @20 (path :Text) -> (tags :List(GitTag));
    createTag @21 (path :Text, name :Text, message :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    deleteTag @22 (path :Text, name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Events
    subscribe @23 (path :Text) -> (subscription :GitSubscription);
}

struct GitInfo {
    path @0 :Text;
    branch @1 :Text;
    head @2 :Text;
    remote @3 :Text;
    dirty @4 :Bool;
    ahead @5 :UInt32;
    behind @6 :UInt32;
    stashCount @7 :UInt32;

}

}

    parents @6 :List(Text);
}

struct GitRemote {

}

using T = import "types.capnp";

interface DebugService {
    # Process debugging
    attach @0 (pid :T.ProcessId) -> (session :DebugSession);
    detach @1 (sessionId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Breakpoints
    setBreakpoint @2 (sessionId :Text, location :BreakpointLocation) -> (bpId :Text);
    removeBreakpoint @3 (sessionId :Text, bpId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    listBreakpoints @4 (sessionId :Text) -> (bps :List(BreakpointInfo));

    # Execution control
    continue @5 (sessionId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    stepOver @6 (sessionId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    stepInto @7 (sessionId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    stepOut @8 (sessionId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    pause @9 (sessionId :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    # Inspection
    getBacktrace @10 (sessionId :Text) -> (frames :List(StackFrame));
    getVariables @11 (sessionId :Text, frameId :Text) -> (vars :List(Variable));
    evaluate @12 (sessionId :Text, expression :Text) -> (result :EvalResult);
    getRegisters @13 (sessionId :Text) -> (registers :T.StringMap);
    getMemory @14 (sessionId :Text, address :UInt64, length :UInt32) -> (data :Data);

    # Profiling
    startProfile @15 (pid :T.ProcessId, type :ProfileType) -> (profileId :Text);
    stopProfile @16 (profileId :Text) -> (result :ProfileResult);
    getProfile @17 (profileId :Text) -> (result :ProfileResult);

    # Core dump
    listCoreDumps @18 () -> (dumps :List(CoreDumpInfo));
    analyzeCoreDump @19 (path :Text) -> (analysis :CoreDumpAnalysis);
}

struct DebugSession {
    id @0 :Text;
    pid @1 :T.ProcessId;
    processName @2 :Text;
    state @3 :DebugState;
    attachedAt @4 :T.Timestamp;
    breakpoints @5 :UInt32;
    currentFrame @6 :StackFrame;
}

enum DebugState {
    running @0;
    paused @1;
    stopped @2;
    crashed @3;
}

struct BreakpointLocation {
    union {
        file @0 :FileLocation;
        function @1 :Text;
        address @2 :UInt64;
        condition @3 :ConditionalBreakpoint;
    }
}

struct FileLocation {
    file @0 :Text;
    line @1 :UInt32;
    column @2 :UInt32;
}

struct ConditionalBreakpoint {
    location @0 :BreakpointLocation;
    condition @1 :Text;
}

struct BreakpointInfo {
    id @0 :Text;
    location @1 :BreakpointLocation;
    hitCount @2 :UInt32;
    enabled @3 :Bool;
    condition @4 :Text;
}

struct StackFrame {
    id @0 :Text;
    function @1 :Text;
    file @2 :Text;
    line @3 :UInt32;
    address @4 :UInt64;
}

struct Variable {
    name @0 :Text;
    value @1 :Text;
    type @2 :Text;
    scope @3 :Text;
    children @4 :List(Variable);
}

struct EvalResult {
    value @0 :Text;
    type @1 :Text;
    error @2 :Text;
}

enum ProfileType {
    cpu @0;
    memory @1;
    alloc @2;
    wall @3;
}

struct ProfileResult {
    id @0 :Text;
    type @1 :ProfileType;
    duration @2 :T.Duration;
    data @3 :Data;
    summary @4 :Text;
}

struct CoreDumpInfo {
    path @0 :Text;
    pid @1 :T.ProcessId;
    processName @2 :Text;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
    signal @4 :Text;
    size @5 :UInt64;
}

struct CoreDumpAnalysis {

    processName @1 :Text;

CLI Methods — Batch 6 (Fixed)
bashbash# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  BATCH 6 (FIXED): APPS & PACKAGES — universal, no backend bias
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── APPS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
apps                                → list all installed apps
apps where installed                → installed apps
apps where running                  → running apps
apps where autostart                → autostart apps
apps where type == gui              → GUI apps
apps where type == cli              → CLI apps
apps where type == daemon           → daemon apps
apps where category == "Development"  → dev apps
apps where name contains "firefox"  → search apps
apps where recently-used            → recently used
apps where size > 100MB             → large apps

app "Firefox"                       → app summary
app "Firefox" info                  → full app details
app "Firefox" launch                → launch app
app "Firefox" launch --args "--safe-mode"  → launch with args
app "Firefox" launch --new          → new instance
app "Firefox" close                 → close gracefully
app "Firefox" close --force         → force close

# Search (universal — searches all configured sources)
app search "image editor"           → search for apps
app search "firefox"                → search all sources

# Install / Remove (universal — uses whatever backend is available)
app install Firefox                 → install app
app remove Firefox                  → remove app
app remove Firefox --data           → remove app + user data
app reinstall Firefox               → reinstall

# Permissions
app "Firefox" permissions           → list permissions
app "Firefox" permission camera on  → grant camera
app "Firefox" permission camera off → revoke camera
app "Firefox" permission microphone on  → grant microphone
app "Firefox" permission location on    → grant location
app "Firefox" permission files read     → grant file read
app "Firefox" permission files write    → grant file write
app "Firefox" permission network on     → grant network
app "Firefox" permission notification on  → grant notifications
app "Firefox" permission tray on        → grant system tray

# Autostart
app "Firefox" autostart             → autostart status
app "Firefox" autostart on          → enable autostart
app "Firefox" autostart off         → disable autostart

# Default apps
apps defaults                       → list default apps
app set-default browser "Firefox"   → set default browser
app set-default terminal "Terminal" → set default terminal
app set-default editor "Code"       → set default editor
app set-default email "Thunderbird" → set default email
app set-default file-manager "Files"  → set default file manager
app set-default image-viewer "Eye of GNOME"  → set image viewer

# Resource limits
app "Firefox" resource-limit        → current limits
app "Firefox" resource-limit cpu 50 → limit CPU to 50%
app "Firefox" resource-limit memory 2GB → limit memory
app "Firefox" resource-limit off    → remove limits

# Startup impact
app "Firefox" startup-impact        → startup impact info

# Recently used
app recent                          → recently used apps
app recent 20                       → last 20 apps

# Windows belonging to app
app "Firefox" windows               → Firefox windows

# Events
watch apps                          → stream app events

# ── SERVICES ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# List (plural = list)
services                            → list all services
services where running              → running services
services where stopped              → stopped services
services where enabled              → enabled services
services where failed               → failed services
services where name contains "ssh"  → search
services where type == system       → system services
services where type == user         → user services

service sshd                        → service summary
service sshd info                   → full details
service sshd start                  → start
service sshd stop                   → stop
service sshd restart                → restart
service sshd reload                 → reload config
service sshd status                 → status
service sshd enable                 → enable auto-start
service sshd disable                → disable auto-start
service sshd logs                   → service logs
service sshd logs --since 1h        → last hour
service sshd logs --lines 50        → last 50 lines
service sshd logs --follow          → follow

services restart-all-failed         → restart all failed

watch services                      → stream events

CLI Methods — Batch 8: Containers & VMs

containers                          → list all containers

# Single container

Window ID — types.capnp
capnpcapnp# Replace WindowId. Current is UInt32 — insufficient for real use.
struct WindowId {
    union {
        number @0 :UInt32;    # Fast positional
        text @1 :Text;        # Title/app fuzzy match
        hash @2 :Text;        # 6+ hex deterministic hash
    }
}
# Resolution: hash > exact text > number > fuzzy text.
# All listings show all three: #, Hash, Title, App, State.

vcs.capnp — NEW (replaces any git-specific schema)
capnpcapnp@0xa1b2c3d4e5f60110;

using T = import "types.capnp";

# Version Control System — abstract, implementation-agnostic.
# Could back git, pijul, fossil, jujutsu, or a future VCS.
# The protocol describes branches, commits, diffs, remotes,
# stashes, tags. The backend is a runtime detail.

interface VcsService {
    getInfo @0 (repo :Text) -> (info :VcsInfo);
    getStatus @1 (repo :Text) -> (status :VcsStatus);

    listBranches @2 (repo :Text) -> (branches :List(VcsBranch));
    getBranch @3 (repo :Text) -> (branch :VcsBranch);
    checkout @4 (repo :Text, branch :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    createBranch @5 (repo :Text, name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    deleteBranch @6 (repo :Text, name :Text, force :Bool) -> T.VoidResult;

    log @7 (repo :Text, options :VcsLogOptions) -> (commits :List(VcsCommit));
    commit @8 (repo :Text, message :Text, files :List(Text)) -> T.VoidResult;
    diff @9 (repo :Text, options :VcsDiffOptions) -> (diff :Text);

    add @10 (repo :Text, files :List(Text)) -> T.VoidResult;
    unstage @11 (repo :Text, files :List(Text)) -> T.VoidResult;
    reset @12 (repo :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    listRemotes @13 (repo :Text) -> (remotes :List(VcsRemote));
    fetch @14 (repo :Text, remote :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    pull @15 (repo :Text, remote :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    push @16 (repo :Text, remote :Text, force :Bool) -> T.VoidResult;

    stash @17 (repo :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    stashPop @18 (repo :Text, index :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;
    stashList @19 (repo :Text) -> (stashes :List(VcsStash));
    stashDrop @20 (repo :Text, index :UInt32) -> T.VoidResult;
    stashClear @21 (repo :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    listTags @22 (repo :Text) -> (tags :List(VcsTag));
    createTag @23 (repo :Text, name :Text, message :Text) -> T.VoidResult;
    deleteTag @24 (repo :Text, name :Text) -> T.VoidResult;

    subscribe @25 (repo :Text) -> (subscription :VcsSubscription);
}

struct VcsInfo {
    repo @0 :Text;
    branch @1 :Text;
    head @2 :Text;
    remote @3 :Text;
    dirty @4 :Bool;
    ahead @5 :UInt32;
    behind @6 :UInt32;
    stashCount @7 :UInt32;
    lastCommit @8 :VcsCommit;
}

struct VcsStatus {
    repo @0 :Text;
    branch @1 :Text;
    staged @2 :List(VcsFileStatus);
    modified @3 :List(VcsFileStatus);
    untracked @4 :List(Text);
    deleted @5 :List(Text);
    conflicted @6 :List(Text);
}

struct VcsFileStatus {
    path @0 :Text;
    status @1 :Text;    # "added", "modified", "deleted", "renamed"
}

struct VcsBranch {
    name @0 :Text;
    current @1 :Bool;
    remote @2 :Text;
    ahead @3 :UInt32;
    behind @4 :UInt32;
    lastCommit @5 :T.Timestamp;
}

struct VcsCommit {
    hash @0 :Text;
    shortHash @1 :Text;
    author @2 :Text;
    email @3 :Text;
    message @4 :Text;
    timestamp @5 :T.Timestamp;
    parents @6 :List(Text);
}

struct VcsRemote {
    name @0 :Text;
    url @1 :Text;
    fetch @2 :Text;
    push @3 :Text;
}

struct VcsStash {
    index @0 :UInt32;
    message @1 :Text;
    timestamp @2 :T.Timestamp;
    branch @3 :Text;
}

struct VcsTag {
    name @0 :Text;
    hash @1 :Text;
    message @2 :Text;
    timestamp @3 :T.Timestamp;
    author @4 :Text;
}

struct VcsLogOptions {
    limit @0 :UInt32;
    skip @1 :UInt32;
    since @2 :T.Timestamp;
    until @3 :T.Timestamp;
    author @4 :Text;
    grep @5 :Text;
    file @6 :Text;
}

struct VcsDiffOptions {
    staged @0 :Bool;
    file @1 :Text;
    commit1 @2 :Text;
    commit2 @3 :Text;
}

interface VcsSubscription {
    pull @0 () -> (events :List(VcsEvent));
    cancel @1 () -> T.VoidResult;
}

struct VcsEvent {
    union {
        committed @0 :VcsCommit;
        branchChanged @1 :Text;
        fetched @2 :Text;
        pushed @3 :Text;
        pulled @4 :Text;
        conflict @5 :List(Text);
        custom @6 :Data;
    }
}

## User

create 3 users in your mind, 1 a developer, 2 a student, 3 a normal person, and their supposed to use the shell instead of gui trace their usages and find real gaps

## Assistant

Thought for 48.1 secondsGap Analysis: Three User Traces

User 1: Developer (Lufuno)
Morning Routine (08:00)
texttext08:00  Open laptop
       → notifications           ✓ works
       → battery                 ✓ works
       → network wifi            ✓ works

08:01  Check what's happening
       → health                  ✓ works
       → vcs status              ✓ works
       → services                ✓ works
       → containers              ✓ works

08:05  Start working on project
       → Need to navigate to project directory
       → ??? NO SHELL CONTEXT ???
       There is no concept of:
         - Current working directory
         - cd / navigation
         - Running a command
         - Piping output
         - Redirecting output
         - Chaining commands
         - Shell variables
         - Conditionals / scripting
GAP 1: Shell Execution Model — entirely missing.
The spec defines how to manage the system but not how to actually USE the shell as a shell. A developer needs:
bashbash# Navigation
cd ~/Projects/myapp                  → change working directory
pwd                                  → print working directory
pushd ~/Projects/other               → push directory
popd                                 → pop directory

# Command execution
run "cargo build"                    → run command, return output
run "cargo build" --background       → run in background
run "cargo test" --timeout 60        → with timeout
run "cargo test" | search "FAILED"   → pipe output to search
run "cargo build" > ~/build.log      → redirect output
run "cargo build" 2>&1               → merge stderr

# Variables
set $branch = @vcs/branch            → store value
echo $branch                         → use variable
set $files = run "find . -name '*.rs'"  → store command output

# Chaining
run "cargo build" && run "cargo test"   → chain on success
run "cargo build" || echo "build failed"  → chain on failure

# Scripting
fn deploy {
    vcs push
    container image build . --tag myapp:$branch
    container image push myapp:$branch
}
deploy                               → call function

# Background
run "cargo build" --background       → background job
jobs                                 → list jobs (already exists)
texttext08:10  Open editor, terminal, browser side by side
       → Need specific window layout
       → window 3 snap left          ✓ works
       → window 7 snap right         ✓ works
       → BUT: Can I save this layout?
GAP 2: Session/Layout Persistence — missing.
bashbash# Needed:
layout save "dev-morning"            → save current window arrangement
layout "dev-morning"                 → restore layout
layout list                          → saved layouts
layout delete "dev-morning"          → delete
layout export ~/layouts/dev.json     → export
layout import ~/layouts/dev.json     → import

# Auto-restore on login:
layout set-default "dev-morning"     → restore on session start
texttext08:15  Start coding. Need to query database.
       → ??? NO DATABASE DOMAIN ???
GAP 3: Database — missing entirely.
bashbash# Needed:
db connect "postgres://localhost/myapp"  → connect
db query "SELECT * FROM users LIMIT 10"  → run query
db query "SELECT count(*) FROM orders"   → simple query
db schema                                 → current schema
db tables                                 → list tables
db table users                            → table info
db table users --limit 10                 → sample data
db explain "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 1"  → query plan
db dump ~/backup.sql                      → dump database
db restore ~/backup.sql                   → restore
db migrations                             → migration status
db migration run                          → run pending migrations
db migration rollback                     → rollback last
db watch                                  → stream query results
texttext08:30  Run build. Build fails. Need to debug.
       → run "cargo build" works if we had it
       → process 2103 info             ✓ works
       → debug attach 2103             ✓ works
       → BUT: How do I run commands and get output back?
GAP 4: Command output capture — missing.
The run command needs to return structured output:
bashbashrun "cargo build"
# Returns:
#   exit code: 0
#   stdout: "   Compiling myapp v0.1.0"
#   stderr: ""
#   duration: 12.4s

run "cargo build" --json
# Returns:
#   { "exit_code": 0, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "", "duration": 12.4 }

run "cargo build" --quiet              → suppress stdout
run "cargo build" --verbose            → full output
run "cargo build" --pty                → interactive (for commands needing input)
texttext09:00  Need to check remote server
       → ??? NO SSH SESSION MANAGEMENT ???
GAP 5: Remote Access — missing.
tunnel covers VPN/port-forwarding tunnels. But there's no way to manage SSH sessions to remote machines:
bashbash# Needed:
remote list                            → saved remote connections
remote add "prod" "user@prod.example.com" --key ~/.ssh/id  → add
remote connect "prod"                  → open SSH session
remote connect "prod" --command "htop"  → run command on remote
remote connect "prod" --forward 8080:localhost:80  → with port forward
remote exec "prod" "systemctl restart nginx"  → run and return
remote file put "prod" ~/app.tar.gz /tmp/  → upload file
remote file get "prod" /var/log/app.log ~/  → download file
remote disconnect "prod"               → close session
texttext09:30  Need to transfer files to staging server
       → ??? NO FILE TRANSFER ???
GAP 6: File Transfer — missing.

## Assistant

Thought for 70.9 secondsShell Fundamentals — What's Actually Missing
The previous 11 batches defined WHAT you can control. But not HOW the shell itself works. Without this, it's a command reference, not a shell. Bash wins by default. That ends now.

1. Running Commands
bashbash# The most fundamental thing a shell does
run "cargo build"                          → execute, return structured result
run "cargo build" --timeout 60             → with timeout
run "cargo build" --background             → background job
run "cargo test" --pty                     → interactive (needs stdin)
run "curl https://api.example.com" --env "TOKEN=abc"  → with environment

# Output is STRUCTURED, not raw text
run "ls -la"
# Returns:
#   exit_code: 0
#   stdout: "total 48\ndrwxr-xr-x  ..."
#   stderr: ""
#   duration: 0.02s

# Capture into variable
let $result = run "cargo build"
echo $result.exit_code                     → 0
echo $result.stdout                        → "   Compiling myapp v0.1.0"
echo $result.duration                      → 12.4

# Background jobs
let $job = run "cargo build" --background
jobs                                       → list background jobs (already have)
job $job wait                              → wait for completion
job $job cancel                            → cancel

2. Natural Language Top-Level Verbs
Ultra-common operations work without domain prefix. These are ergonomic aliases:
bashbash# File operations — no "file" prefix needed
copy ~/a.txt ~/b.txt                       → alias: file copy
copy ~/Projects/ ~/backup/ --recursive     → recursive copy
move ~/a.txt ~/dir/                        → alias: file move
rename ~/old.txt ~/new.txt                 → alias: file move (same dir)
delete ~/old.txt                           → alias: file delete
delete ~/old/ --recursive                  → recursive delete
read ~/doc.txt                             → alias: file read
write ~/new.txt "Hello, world"             → alias: file write
append ~/log.txt "New entry"               → alias: file append
touch ~/new-file.txt                       → create empty file
mkdir ~/new-dir                            → create directory
mkdir ~/a/b/c --parents                    → create with parents
link ~/original ~/link                     → symlink
chmod 755 ~/script.sh                      → alias: file permissions
chown lufuno ~/file.txt                    → alias: file owner

# Directory
cd ~/Projects                              → change directory
cd -                                       → previous directory
cd                                         → home directory
pwd                                        → print working directory
ls                                         → list current directory
ls ~/Projects                              → list path
ls ~/Projects --all                        → include hidden
ls ~/Projects --long                       → detailed listing
ls ~/Projects --recursive                  → recursive

# Execution
run "make build"                           → run command
run "python script.py" --timeout 30        → with timeout

# Open (cross-platform: opens file in default app, URL in browser, etc.)

open "https://example.com"                 → open in browser
open ~/photo.png                           → open in image viewer

# Search
grep "error" ~/logs/app.log                → search file content
grep "error" ~/logs/ --recursive           → recursive search
grep "error" ~/logs/ --type rust           → Rust files only
find "*.rs" --path ~/Projects              → find files (alias: search file)

3. Variables and Types
bashbash# Variables — typed, not stringly-typed
let $name = "smart"                        → Text
let $count = 42                            → Int
let $ratio = 0.72                          → Float
let $active = true                         → Bool
let $path = ~/Documents/file.txt           → Path

# Compound types
let $point = { x: 100, y: 200 }           → Record
let $names = ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"]   → List<Text>
let $mixed = [1, "two", true]              → List<Any>

# Type annotations (optional, inferred)
let $count: Int = 42
let $names: List<Text> = ["Alice", "Bob"]

# Accessing compound fields
echo $point.x                              → 100
echo $names[0]                             → "Alice"
echo $names.length                         → 3

# Destructuring
let { x, y } = $point
echo $x                                    → 100

let [$first, $second, ...$rest] = $names
echo $first                                → "Alice"
echo $rest                                 → ["Charlie"]

# Mutability
let $count = 0
$count = $count + 1                        → reassign

4. Type Definitions (Enums, Compound Types)
bashbash# Enums — first-class types
type Severity = Info | Warning | Error | Critical
type PowerState = OnBattery | Charging | Full | Unknown
type WindowState = Normal | Minimized | Maximized | Fullscreen | Tiled
type TunnelState = Disconnected | Connecting | Connected | Disconnecting | Error

# Using enums
let $level: Severity = Severity.Warning

# Enum with data (algebraic data types)
type Option<T> = Some(T) | None
type Result<T, E> = Ok(T) | Err(E)

# Compound types (structs)
type Point = { x: Int, y: Int }
type Rect = { origin: Point, width: Int, height: Int }
type ServiceStatus = {
    name: Text,
    state: Text,
    pid: Int,
    cpu: Float,
    memory: UInt64
}

# Using compound types
let $svc: ServiceStatus = {
    name: "nginx",
    state: "running",
    pid: 1234,
    cpu: 2.1,
    memory: 48_000_000
}
echo $svc.name                             → "nginx"

# Type aliases for protocol types
type WindowId = Text | Int | Hash

5. Pattern Matching
bashbash# Match expressions — the centerpiece
let $state = service "sshd" | get state

match $state {
    "running"  => "Service is healthy",
    "stopped"  => "Service is down",
    "failed"   => "Service has failed",
    _          => "Unknown state: $state"
}

# Match on enums
fn power_advice($state: PowerState) -> Text {
    match $state {
        PowerState.OnBattery => "Switch to power-saver",
        PowerState.Charging  => "Balanced is fine",
        PowerState.Full      => "Performance available",
        PowerState.Unknown   => "Run diagnostics",
    }
}

# Match with destructuring
match $result {
    Ok($value)  => echo "Success: $value",
    Err($error) => echo "Failed: $error",
}

# Match with guards
match $window {
    { state: "minimized", ... } => "Hidden",
    { state: "fullscreen", ... } => "Immersive",
    { focused: true, ... } => "Active",
    _ => "Background",
}

# Match on multiple values
match ($direction, $action) {
    ("inbound", "deny")  => "Blocked inbound",
    ("inbound", "allow") => "Allowed inbound",
    ("outbound", _)      => "Outbound traffic",
    _                    => "Unknown",
}

6. Functions
bashbash# Functions — typed, composable
fn greet($name: Text) -> Text {
    return "Hello, $name"
}

fn is_low_battery() -> Bool {
    return @battery/level < 0.20
}

fn restart_if_failed($name: Text) -> Void {
    let $state = service $name | get state
    if $state == "failed" {
        service $name restart
        notify "Restarted service: $name"
    }
}

# Closures / lambdas
let $double = |$n| $n * 2
echo $double(21)                           → 42

# Higher-order functions
let $names = processes | map { $.name }
let $big_files = files | filter { $.size > 100_000_000 }

# Default parameters
fn connect_wifi($ssid: Text, $band: Text = "auto") -> Void {
    network wifi connect $ssid --band $band
}

# Multiple return values
fn get_bounds($id: WindowId) -> (Int, Int, Int, Int) {
    let $w = window $id | get bounds
    return ($w.x, $w.y, $w.width, $w.height)
}
let ($x, $y, $w, $h) = get_bounds(3)

7. Control Flow
bashbash# If / else
if @battery/level < 0.20 {
    power profile power-saver
    notify "Battery low — switching to power-saver"
} else if @battery/level < 0.50 {
    power profile balanced
} else {
    power profile performance
}

# If expressions (return values)
let $label = if $count > 10 { "many" } else { "few" }

# For loops
for $svc in services where failed {
    service $svc.name restart
    echo "Restarted: $svc.name"
}

for $file in files ~/Downloads/ where size > 100_000_000 {
    echo "Large file: $file.name ($file.size)"
}

for $i in 0..10 {
    echo $i
}

# While loops
while @battery/level > 0.10 {
    time timer 5m
    echo "Still have battery"
}

# Loop control
for $proc in processes where cpu > 90 {
    if $proc.name == "idle" { continue }
    echo "High CPU: $proc.name ($proc.cpu%)"
    if $proc.cpu > 99 { break }
}bash# If / else

8. Error Handling
bashbash# Try / catch — typed errors
try {
    container start "web"
    container start "postgres"
} catch Container.ImageNotFound($e) {
    echo "Image missing: $e.image"
    container image pull $e.image
} catch Container.PortConflict($e) {
    echo "Port $e.port already in use"
} catch $e {
    echo "Unexpected error: $e"
}

# Result type for failable operations
let $result = try connect_wifi("HomeNetwork")
match $result {
    Ok(_)       => echo "Connected",
    Err($error) => echo "Failed: $error",
}

# The ? operator (propagate errors)
fn deploy() -> Result<Text, Error> {
    vcs push ?
    container image build . --tag myapp ?
    container start "web" ?
    return Ok("Deployed successfully")
}

# Error types (from protocol)
# Every error is: error[Domain.Code]: message
# Can match on domain or code:
try {
    access unlock --password $input
} catch Access.Lockout($e) {
    echo "Locked out for $e.duration seconds"
} catch Access.WrongPassword($e) {
    echo "Wrong. $e.remaining attempts left"
}bash# Try / catch — typed errors
try {
    container start "web"
    container start "postgres"
} catch Container.ImageNotFound($e) {
    echo "Image missing: $e.image"
    container image pull $e.image
} catch Container.PortConflict($e) {
    echo "Port $e.port already in use"
} catch $e {
    echo "Unexpected error: $e"
}

# Result type for failable operations
let $result = try connect_wifi("HomeNetwork")
match $result {
    Ok(_)       => echo "Connected",
    Err($error) => echo "Failed: $error",
}

# The ? operator (propagate errors)
fn deploy() -> Result<Text, Error> {
    vcs push ?
    container image build . --tag myapp ?
    container start "web" ?
    return Ok("Deployed successfully")
}

# Error types (from protocol)
# Every error is: error[Domain.Code]: message
# Can match on domain or code:
try {
    access unlock --password $input
} catch Access.Lockout($e) {
    echo "Locked out for $e.duration seconds"
} catch Access.WrongPassword($e) {
    echo "Wrong. $e.remaining attempts left"

9. Structured Data Pipeline
The pipe operator | passes structured data, not text. This is where smart annihilates bash:
bashbash# Bash: text gymnastics
# ps aux | grep firefox | awk '{print $2}' | head -1

# Smart: structured, readable
processes where name == "firefox" | get pid | first

# Bash: curl ... | jq '.items[] | select(.active) | .name'

# Smart: structured HTTP
web get "https://api.example.com/items" | get items | filter { $.active } | map { $.name }

# Pipeline operators
processes                           → List<Process>
    | where { $.cpu > 10 }         → filter
    | sort by cpu desc              → sort
    | take 10                       → limit
    | map { name: $.name, cpu: $.cpu }  → project fields

# Equivalent in one line
processes where cpu > 10 | sort by cpu desc | take 10 | map { name: $.name, cpu: $.cpu }

# Aggregations
processes | count                   → total count
processes | sum { $.memory }        → total memory
processes | average { $.cpu }       → average CPU
processes | group by { $.user }     → group by user
processes | min { $.cpu }           → min CPU process
processes | max { $.memory }        → max memory process

# Joining data
let $windows = windows
let $procs = processes
$windows | join $procs on { $.pid } | map {
    title: $.title,
    app: $.app,
    cpu: $.right.cpu,
    memory: $.right.memory
}

# Set operations
let $running = services where running | map { $.name }
let $enabled = services where enabled | map { $.name }
let $should_be_running = $enabled - $running    → set difference
let $all = $running + $enabled                  → union
let $both = $running & $enabled                 → intersection

# Flatten / unnest
containers | flatmap { $.ports } | where { $.hostPort > 1024 }

# Unique
processes | map { $.user } | unique

10. Node System
Every smart-protocol device is a node. Nodes discover each other, share state, execute remotely:
bashbash# Discovery
nodes                                  → list all known nodes
nodes where online                     → online nodes
nodes where type == "server"           → servers only
nodes where type == "phone"            → phones only
nodes where type == "iot"              → IoT devices

node "thinkpad"                        → node summary
node "thinkpad" info                   → full details (OS, hardware, uptime)
node "thinkpad" status                 → connection status

# Remote state access (same @path syntax, any node)
@thinkpad/battery/level                → remote battery
@thinkpad/cpu/usage                    → remote CPU
@server/memory/percent                 → server memory
@phone/battery/level                   → phone battery
@iot-sensor/temperature/current        → IoT sensor reading

# Remote command execution
node "thinkpad" run "cpu usage"        → run on remote node
node "server" run "services where failed"  → check remote services
node "thinkpad" run "power suspend"    → remote control
node "server" run "container restart web"  → remote container restart

# Remote file operations
copy ~/file.txt @server:/tmp/file.txt  → copy to remote node
copy @server:/var/log/app.log ~/app.log  → copy from remote
move @phone:~/photo.jpg ~/Pictures/    → move from phone
sync ~/Projects/ @server:~/Projects/   → bidirectional sync
sync ~/Projects/ @server:~/Projects/ --dry-run  → preview sync

# Node events (cross-device)
watch @server/services where failed    → watch remote services
watch @phone/battery where < 0.20     → watch phone battery
watch @server/containers where state == "stopped"  → watch containers

# Node groups
nodes group create "production"        → create node group
nodes group "production" add server-1 server-2  → add nodes
node group "production" run "health"   → run on all in group
node group "production" run "packages upgrade --security"  → security updates everywhere

# Node trust
node "thinkpad" trust                  → trust node
node "unknown-device" deny             → deny node
nodes trust                            → trusted nodes
nodes pending                          → pending trust requests

11. Inline Math and Expressions
bashbash# Math — inline, natural
echo 2 + 2                              → 4
echo 10 * 3 + 2                         → 32
echo 2 ** 10                            → 1024 (exponent)
echo 17 % 5                             → 2 (modulo)

# Float
echo 3.14 * 2                           → 6.28
echo sqrt(144)                          → 12
echo abs(-42)                           → 42
echo min(10, 20)                        → 10
echo max(10, 20)                        → 20

# Trig
echo sin(pi / 4)                        → 0.7071
echo cos(0)                             → 1.0

# Unit conversions
echo convert(100, "km", "miles")        → 62.14
echo convert(72, "°F", "°C")           → 22.22
echo convert(1, "GB", "MB")            → 1024

# Percentage
echo 15% of 200                         → 30
echo @battery/level * 100               → 72

# String expressions
let $greeting = "Hello, " + $name
echo $name.length                       → 5
echo $name.uppercase                    → "LUFUNO"
echo $name.contains("fu")              → true
echo $name.starts_with("Lu")           → true
echo $name.replace("fu", "F")          → "Lufno"
echo $name.split("f")                  → ["lu", "uno"]
echo $path.basename                     → "file.txt"
echo $path.extension                    → "txt"
echo $path.parent                       → "~/Documents"
echo $path.exists                       → true
echo format("{:.2}", 3.14159)           → "3.14"
echo join(", ", $names)                 → "Alice, Bob, Charlie"

# Comparison and logical
echo $count > 10 && $active             → true
echo $state == "running" || $state == "paused"  → true
echo !$locked                           → true

12. Output and Formatting
bashbash# Echo / print
echo "Hello, $name"                     → print
echo --nonewline "Loading..."           → no trailing newline
echo --stderr "Warning: ..."            → to stderr

# Structured output
echo $data --format json                → JSON
echo $data --format toml                → TOML
echo $data --format yaml                → YAML
echo $data --format table               → table
echo $data --format csv                 → CSV

# Table formatting
processes | take 5 | table              → formatted table
processes | take 5 | table --columns name,cpu,memory  → select columns
processes | take 5 | table --sort cpu   → sort table
processes | take 5 | markdown           → markdown table

# Redirect
echo "Hello" > ~/output.txt             → write to file
echo "More" >> ~/output.txt             → append to file
run "cargo build" > ~/build.log 2>&1   → redirect stdout + stderr

# Tee (output to both terminal and file)
processes | tee ~/process-snapshot.txt  → save and display

13. Modules and Scripts
bashbash# Script files (.smart)
# ~/scripts/deploy.smart
#!/usr/bin/env smart

fn deploy($env: Text) -> Result<Text, Error> {
    echo "Deploying to $env..."
    vcs push ?
    node $env run "container image build /app --tag myapp:latest" ?
    node $env run "container restart web" ?
    return Ok("Deployed to $env")
}

# Run script
run ~/scripts/deploy.smart --args "production"
smart ~/scripts/deploy.smart --args "production"  → same

# Import modules
import ~/scripts/utils.smart           → import functions
import ~/scripts/utils.smart as utils  → import with alias
import { deploy, rollback } from ~/scripts/deploy.smart  → selective

# Standard library modules
import std.collections                 → data structures
import std.http                        → HTTP helpers
import std.json                        → JSON parsing
import std.time                        → time utilities

# Module exports
# In utils.smart:
export fn notify_all($msg: Text) -> Void {
    for $node in nodes where online {
        node $node.name run "notify '$msg'"
    }
}

14. Comparison: Smart vs Bash
texttext┌─────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┐
│ Task                        │ Bash                 │ Smart                │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Get PID of Firefox          │ ps aux | grep firefox│ processes where      │
│                             │ | grep -v grep       │ name == "firefox"    │
│                             │ | awk '{print $2}'   │ | get pid            │
│                             │ | head -1            │                      │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Check battery               │ cat /sys/class/power │ @battery/level       │
│                             │ _supply/BAT0/capacity│                      │
│                             │ (linux only,         │ (every platform)     │
│                             │  different on mac)   │                      │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Restart failed services     │ systemctl list-units │ services where       │
│                             │ --failed | grep      │ failed | each {      │
│                             │ ".service" | awk     │ service $.name       │
│                             │ '{print $1}' | xargs │ restart }            │
│                             │ -I{} systemctl       │                      │
│                             │ restart {}           │                      │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Top 5 memory consumers      │ ps aux --sort=-%mem  │ processes | sort     │
│                             │ | head -6 | tail -5  │ by memory desc       │
│                             │ | awk '{print $11,   │ | take 5 | map {     │
│                             │ $4}'                 │ name, memory }       │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ If disk > 90% full, notify  │ USAGE=$(df / | tail  │ if @disk/root/usage  │
│                             │ -1 | awk '{print $5}'│ > 0.90 {            │
│                             │ | tr -d '%');        │   notify "Disk full" │
│                             │ if [ "$USAGE" -gt 90 │ }                    │
│                             │ ]; then notify-send  │                      │
│                             │ "Disk full"; fi      │                      │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Remote: restart nginx       │ ssh user@server      │ node "server" run    │
│                             │ "systemctl restart   │ "service nginx       │
│                             │ nginx"               │ restart"             │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Copy file to phone          │ adb push file.txt    │ copy ~/file.txt      │
│                             │ /sdcard/             │ @phone:~/file.txt    │
│                             │ (android only)       │ (any phone)          │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Schedule daily backup       │ crontab -e           │ schedule create      │
│                             │ (cryptic syntax)     │ "backup" --every 1d  │
│                             │ 0 2 * * * /usr/local │ --at "02:00" --cmd   │
│                             │ /bin/backup.sh       │ "backup run"         │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Structured API call + filter│ curl -s https://...  │ web get "https://..."│
│                             │ | jq '.items[]       │ | get items          │
│                             │ | select(.active)    │ | where { $.active } │
│                             │ | .name'             │ | map { $.name }     │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Error handling              │ set -e; set -o       │ try {                │
│                             │ pipefail; trap ...   │   container start web│
│                             │ (fragile, verbose)   │ } catch $e {         │
│                             │                      │   echo $e            │
│                             │                      │ }                    │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Cross-platform file ops     │ Different on Linux/  │ copy ~/a ~/b         │
│                             │ Mac/Windows. Need    │ (works everywhere,   │
│                             │ platform detection.  │  every node type)    │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Type a variable             │ Everything is a      │ let $n: Int = 42    │
│                             │ string. Parse        │ let $p: Point =     │
│                             │ integers manually.   │ { x: 1, y: 2 }     │
├─────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┤
│ Watch for events            │ inotifywait + polling│ watch services where │
│                             │ + custom scripts     │ failed               │
└─────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────┴──────────────────────┘

15. Node Types
The protocol is universal. Nodes declare their type:
bashbash# Node types (self-declared)
type NodeType = Desktop    # PC, laptop, workstation
               | Mobile    # Phone, tablet
               | Server    # Rack, cloud, VPS
               | Container # Isolated environment
               | Vm        # Virtual machine
               | IoT       # Sensor, actuator, embedded
               | Vehicle   # Car, ship, spacecraft
               | Ai        # AI agent, model instance
               | Gateway   # Network gateway, router
               | Custom(Text) # Anything else

# Nodes declare capabilities
node "thinkpad" capabilities
# → [display, audio, bluetooth, wifi, gpu, camera, ...]

node "raspberry-pi" capabilities
# → [gpio, i2c, spi, camera, wifi, bluetooth, ...]

node "server" capabilities
# → [network, containers, vm, storage, compute, ...]

node "rover" capabilities
# → [navigation, camera, sensors, actuators, gps, ...]

# Commands adapt to capabilities
node "raspberry-pi" run "gpio set pin-17 high"      → IoT: valid
node "raspberry-pi" run "display brightness 50"     → error: no display capability
node "thinkpad" run "display brightness 50"         → works

# Sensor data (IoT)
@raspberry-pi/sensors/temperature/current            → 23.5
@rover/gps/position                                   → { lat: 37.77, lon: -122.41 }
@rover/battery/level                                  → 0.85
@vehicle/speed/current                                → 65

# Multi-node orchestration
for $node in nodes where type == "IoT" where online {
    let $temp = @$node.name/sensors/temperature/current
    if $temp > 30 {
        notify "High temp on $node.name: $temp°C"
    }
}

16. Schedule (Recurring Tasks)
bashbash# Schedule — recurring, conditional, cross-node
schedule list                          → all scheduled tasks
schedule "cleanup"                     → task details
schedule "cleanup" info                → full details

schedule create "cleanup" --every 1h --command "packages orphans clean"  → hourly
schedule create "backup" --every 1d --at "02:00" --command "backup run"  → daily at 2am
schedule create "report" --every mon --at "09:00" --command "health > ~/weekly-report.txt"  → weekly
schedule create "security-scan" --every 1d --at "03:00" --command "security audit"  → daily

# Conditional schedules
schedule create "low-battery" --every 5m --when "@battery/level < 0.15" --command "power profile power-saver; notify 'Battery critical'"
schedule create "disk-full" --every 10m --when "@disk/root/usage > 0.90" --command "notify 'Disk almost full'; packages orphans clean"

# Remote schedules
schedule create "server-update" --every 1d --at "04:00" --on "server" --command "packages upgrade --security"

# Node group schedules
schedule create "iot-check" --every 5m --on-group "sensors" --command "health"

# Manage
schedule "cleanup" enable              → enable
schedule "cleanup" disable             → disable
schedule "cleanup" run                 → run now (manual trigger)
schedule "cleanup" history             → execution history
schedule "cleanup" delete              → delete
schedule "cleanup" set --every 30m     → change frequencybash# Schedule — recurring, conditional, cross-node
