The Pattern
Three levels of list access. Not everything needs where:
texttextLEVEL 1 — Named views (common filters are verbs, not conditions)
  packages outdated          NOT  packages where outdated
  containers running         NOT  containers where state == running
  services failed            NOT  services where failed
  process search node        NOT  processes where name contains "node"

LEVEL 2 — Type/category filters (flag, not where)
  disks --type ssd           NOT  disks where type == ssd
  tunnels --type wireguard   NOT  tunnels where type == wireguard
  apps --type gui            NOT  apps where type == gui
  bluetooth devices --type ble   NOT  bluetooth devices where type == ble

LEVEL 3 — where (actual conditional filtering, data queries)
  processes where cpu > 50
  windows where workspace == 2
  packages where size > 100MB
  files where modified > 7dtextLEVEL 1 — Named views (common filters are verbs, not conditions)
  packages outdated          NOT  packages where outdated
  containers running         NOT  containers where state == running
  services failed            NOT  services where failed
  process search node        NOT  processes where name contains "node"

LEVEL 2 — Type/category filters (flag, not where)
  disks --type ssd           NOT  disks where type == ssd
  tunnels --type wireguard   NOT  tunnels where type == wireguard
  apps --type gui            NOT  apps where type == gui
  bluetooth devices --type ble   NOT  bluetooth devices where type == ble

LEVEL 3 — where (actual conditional filtering, data queries)
  processes where cpu > 50
  windows where workspace == 2
  packages where size > 100MB
  files where modified > 7d
Rule: If a view is used daily, it's a named verb. where is for actual data queries.

Shell Fundamentals Summary
What makes smart a shell, not just a command reference:
texttextCOMMANDS                                → run "cmd", cd, ls, copy, move, delete, grep, which, open
VARIABLES                               → let $x: Type = value
COMPOUND TYPES                          → type Point = { x: Int, y: Int }
ENUMS                                   → type State = Running | Stopped | Failed
PATTERN MATCHING                        → match $x { ... }
FUNCTIONS                               → fn name($arg: Type) -> Type { ... }
CONTROL FLOW                            → if/else, for, while, break, continue
ERROR HANDLING                          → try/catch, ?, Result<T,E>
PIPELINES                               → processes | where { ... } | map { ... }
MATH                                    → calc "2+2", inline: $x + $y
SCRIPTS                                 → run ~/script.smart
MODULES                                 → import ~/lib.smart
NODE SYSTEM                             → node "server" run "cmd", copy ~/f @node:~/f
SCHEDULE                                → schedule create --every 1h --command "..."
LOGGING                                 → log "info" "msg"
FILE PARSING                            → parse json ~/config.json
STRING METHODS                          → $text.split(",").join("-").uppercase
OUTPUT FORMATS                          → --json, --toml, --yaml, --csv, --table
Smart is a shell that happens to manage your system. Not a system manager that pretends to be a shell. Day 1, it beats bash at everything bash does, and it does things bash can't do at all.

## Assistant

Thought for 36.1 secondsFixing the Fundamentals
The previous version was bash wearing a costume. This is the real thing.

1. External Commands Just Work
No run wrapper. If it's not a smart keyword, it executes:
bashbashcargo build                            → just runs cargo build
npm install                            → just runs npm install
python script.py                       → just runs python
make test                              → just runs make
ssh user@server                        → just runs ssh
vim ~/file.txt                         → just runs vim

# Only use run() for smart-specific features:
run "cargo build" --timeout 60         → timeout (smart feature)
run "npm install" --background         → background (smart feature)
run "make test" --on "server"          → remote execution
The shell doesn't need to know about cargo. It's a process. It runs.

2. Drop POSIX Clones
texttextPOSIX              →  SMART
──────────────────────────────────────
chmod 755          →  access ~/script grant execute
chown user         →  access ~/file set owner user
mkdir -p           →  create ~/a/b/c --parents
touch              →  create ~/file
ln -s              →  link ~/original ~/link
cat                →  read ~/file
cp                 →  copy
mv                 →  move / rename
rm -rf             →  delete --recursive --force
which              →  find-command cargo
type               →  what-is cargo
No numeric modes. No rwx bitmasks. Capability model:
bashbashaccess ~/script.sh                     → full access report
#   📋 Access — ~/script.sh
#   ├─ Owner     lufuno (read, write, execute)
#   ├─ Group     developers (read, execute)
#   ├─ Others    (read)
#   └─ Capabilities
#      ├─ read     ✓ owner, ✓ group, ✓ others
#      ├─ write    ✓ owner, ✗ group, ✗ others
#      └─ execute  ✓ owner, ✓ group, ✗ others

access ~/script.sh grant execute       → grant execute to self
access ~/script.sh grant read everyone → grant read to everyone
access ~/script.sh revoke write group  → revoke group write
access ~/script.sh set owner alice     → change owner
access ~/script.sh set group devops    → change group

3. Wildcards
Glob patterns work everywhere:
bashbashdelete ~/logs/*.log                    → delete all .log files
copy ~/photos/*.jpg ~/backup/          → copy all JPGs
read ~/config.*                        → read all config files
move ~/Downloads/*.pdf ~/Documents/    → move all PDFs

# In pipelines
files ~/logs/*.log | where { $.size > 10_000_000 } | delete
files ~/Projects/**/*.rs | where { $.modified > 7d }

# In searches
processes --name "fire*"               → match processes
services --name "*ssh*"                → match services
packages --name "python*"              → match packages

4. Media — Targeting
Four players in four windows. Which one is media pause?
bashbashmedia
#   🎵 Media (4 sessions)
#   ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
#   │ #        │ Hash     │ Track                    │ App            │ Window   │ State    │
#   ├──────────┼──────────┼──────────────────────────┼────────────────┼──────────┼──────────┤
#   │  1       │ #m4u1c   │ Bohemian Rhapsody — Queen│ Firefox (#12)  │ YouTube  │ ♪ Playing│
#   │  2       │ #p1a2y   │ Podcast EP 42            │ Thunderbird(#7)│ Spotify  │ ♪ Playing│
#   │  3       │ #s0ng3   │ (nothing)                │ Editor (#18)   │ —        │ ◉ Idle   │
#   │  4       │ #v1d30   │ Movie.mkv                │ Player (#21)   │ Local    │ ♪ Playing│
#   └──────────┴──────────┴──────────────────────────┴────────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
#
#   Use: media <hash> pause | media <#> pause | media --window 12 pause

# Target by hash
media #m4u1c pause                     → pause YouTube in Firefox
media #p1a2y volume 50                 → set podcast volume

# Target by number
media 1 pause                          → pause #1

# Target by window
media --window 12 pause                → pause Firefox's media
media --window 21 seek +30             → seek movie forward

# Target by app
media --app Firefox pause              → pause Firefox media
media --app Player aspect-ratio 16:9   → set player aspect ratio

# Bare media (smart behavior)
media pause                            → if 1 playing: pause it
                                         if multiple playing: show disambiguation
media pause --all                      → pause everything
media resume                           → resume last paused

# Bare word state
media next                             → ambiguous if multiple
media #m4u1c next                      → target next track in specific session
media #v1d30 subtitle list             → subtitles for movie
media #v1d30 subtitle load ~/subs.srt  → load subtitle file
media #v1d30 chapter next              → next chapter

5. Node Context Switching
bashbash# Switch to remote node (changes context, all commands now run there)
@thinkpad                              → switched to thinkpad
#   ✓ Connected to thinkpad (Desktop, 62°C, battery 72%)

# Now everything is local to thinkpad
battery                                → thinkpad's battery
cpu                                    → thinkpad's CPU
services                               → thinkpad's services
audio                                  → thinkpad's audio
media                                  → thinkpad's media

# Copy to/from using context
copy ~/file.txt @server:/tmp/          → copy local → server
copy @server:/var/log/app.log ~/       → copy server → local

# Return to local
@local                                 → back to local machine
@                                      → shorthand for @local

# Node info
@server                                → switch to server
#   ✓ Connected to server (Server, uptime 47d, 4 containers running)

# Multi-node operations from any context
nodes                                  → all nodes
nodes online                           → online nodes
nodes --type server                    → by type

# Remote from any context without switching
@phone/battery/level                   → 0.72 (doesn't switch context)
node "server" run "services failed"    → explicit remote (doesn't switch)

# Node groups
@production                            → switch to production group
#   ✓ Connected to production (3 nodes: server-1, server-2, server-3)
#   Commands run on all nodes in group
services                               → services across all 3
packages outdated                      → outdated across all 3

# Trust
node "unknown-device" trust            → trust
node "unknown-device" deny             → deny
nodes trust                            → trusted
nodes pending                          → pending requests

Thought for 11.6 secondsGuide Mode + Naming Fix

Naming: Better, Not Different
which stays which. copy beats cp. Don't rename for the sake of renaming.
texttextKEEP (already good):     CHANGE (actually better):    DON'T (foolish):
  which                    cp → copy                    which → find-command
  ssh                      mv → move                    cat → read (actually fine)
  grep                     rm → delete
  kill                     ln → link
  ping                     chmod → access (capability model)
  curl                     mkdir → create
  git (→ vcs)              touch → create
  find
  awk
  sed
  tar
  gzip
Principle: If it's universally understood and descriptive, keep it. If we have a genuinely better model (capability vs bitmask), use it. Never rename to sound different.

<domain> --guide launches a full interactive TUI shell app. Not a wizard. Not a prompt. A real application.

Guide Mode Technical Design
bashbash# Every --guide launches a full TUI app
# Built on a shared TUI framework:

# Universal guide features:
# - All domains share: navigation, search, tabs, actions, help
# - Real-time updates (auto-refresh via event subscriptions)
# - Keyboard-first, mouse-optional
# - Responsive (adapts to terminal size)
# - Theme-aware (respects `theme` settings)
# - Accessible (screen reader compatible)

# Guide mode reads current system state on launch
# Subscribes to events for live updates
# Actions execute immediately (no confirmation unless destructive)
# Destructive actions show confirmation inline

# Example flow:
network --guide
# → Launches TUI
# → Shows current network state
# → WiFi tab active by default
# → Auto-refreshes signal strength, bandwidth
# → User navigates with keyboard
# → Enter on network → connects (prompts password if needed)
# → q → exits guide, returns to shell

What AI Integration Looks Like in Guide Mode
In every guide, pressing ? shows contextual AI help. Pressing / with natural language triggers AI search:
texttext# In any guide, press / and type naturally:

/services --guide → / "which services failed today"
#   → Filters to services that failed today

/network --guide → / "why is my connection slow"
#   → Runs inline diagnosis, shows results in the guide

/containers --guide → / "which container uses most memory"
#   → Sorts by memory, highlights the top one

/audio --guide → / "switch everything to headphones"
#   → Routes all audio streams to WH-1000XM5

/windows --guide → / "arrange dev workspace"
#   → Applies layout: Terminal left, Editor right, Browser bottom
Guide mode isn't a separate app. It's the shell, visual. Everything you can do with commands, you can do with keyboard in the guide. And the AI is always one keystroke away.

Thought for 38.6 secondsSmart Protocol Shell — Final Specification

Architecture
texttextL0  WIRE         Cap'n Proto. Zero-copy. Zero-cost. Timeless.
L1  RUNTIME      Nodes, capabilities, events, state, @path
L2  SHELL        Language, variables, types, pipelines, functions
L3  DOMAINS      30+ command surfaces. Bare word dashboards.
L4  INTELLIGENCE ask · suggest · explain · fix · auto · predict
L5  GUIDE        Interactive TUI per domain. --guide on anything.
L6  CROSS        health · security · privacy · debug · hardware
Each layer only knows layers below it. No circular dependencies. A node doesn't know about the shell. The shell doesn't know about domains. Domains don't know about AI. AI uses all layers below.

L0: Wire Protocol
Cap'n Proto schemas. Already defined across 40+ schema files. Every schema is:
Agnostic. No implementation names. VcsService, not GitService. PackageManager, not AptManager.Zero-copy. Readers never allocate. Messages are their own buffer.Zero-cost. Default values absent from wire. Unset fields cost nothing.Timeless. Works in 2025, 2138, on a phone or a spaceship.
No schema changes needed. All schemas from previous rounds stand.

L1: Runtime
Nodes
Every device is a node. A node declares its type and capabilities:
texttexttype NodeType = Desktop | Mobile | Server | Container | Vm
              | IoT | Vehicle | Ai | Gateway | Custom(Text)
A node has:Identity: name, type, address, public keyCapabilities: what it can do (display, audio, gpio, containers, ...)State: all state accessible via @pathEvents: subscribable streams of changes
Capability Model
No numeric modes. No rwx bitmasks. Capabilities are named permissions:
texttextaccess ~/script.sh
  → owner: lufuno (read, write, execute)
  → group: developers (read, execute)
  → others: (read)

access ~/script.sh grant execute         → grant execute to self
access ~/script.sh grant read everyone   → grant read to everyone
access ~/script.sh revoke write group    → revoke group write
access ~/script.sh set owner alice       → change owner
access ~/script.sh set group devops      → change group
@path State
All state accessible via paths:
texttext@battery/level                  → 0.72
@cpu/usage                      → 0.48
@network/wifi/signal            → 0.78
@audio/volume                   → 0.65
@server/cpu/usage               → remote node state
@phone/battery/level            → remote node state
Labels
Universal metadata. No "groups." A label is just a tag on anything:
texttextlabel window 3 "dev"             → apply label
label node "server-1" "prod"     → apply label
label service "nginx" "web"      → apply label

unlabel window 3 "dev"           → remove label

# Filter by label
windows --label "dev"            → windows with label
nodes --label "prod"             → nodes with label
services --label "web"           → services with label

# Act on label (batch operations)
windows --label "dev" minimize
windows --label "dev" tile horizontal
nodes --label "prod" run "health"

# @label is just context to a labeled set
@prod                            → switch context to labeled nodes
# Now all commands run across those nodes
services                         → services across all prod nodes
packages outdated                → outdated across all prod nodes
Labels are persistent. Cross-cutting. Apply to anything. No lifecycle management. They exist when applied, gone when removed.
Events
Every domain exposes subscribable events:
texttextwatch battery                      → stream battery events
watch services failed              → stream service failures
watch @server/containers           → stream remote container events
watch network where bandwidth > 10_000_000  → stream high bandwidth

L2: Shell Language
External commands just work. Smart keywords are reserved. Everything else executes:
texttextcargo build                        → runs cargo
npm install                        → runs npm
python script.py                   → runs python
ssh user@server                    → runs ssh
make test                          → runs make
vim ~/file.txt                     → runs vim
Variables
texttextlet $name = "smart"                     Text
let $count = 42                         Int
let $ratio = 0.72                       Float
let $active = true                      Bool
let $path = ~/Documents/file.txt        Path
let $point = { x: 100, y: 200 }        Record
let $names = ["Alice", "Bob"]           List<Text>
Type Definitions
texttexttype Severity = Info | Warning | Error | Critical

type Point = { x: Int, y: Int }
type Rect = { origin: Point, width: Int, height: Int }

type Option<T> = Some(T) | None
type Result<T, E> = Ok(T) | Err(E)
Pattern Matching
texttextmatch $state {
    "running"  => "healthy",
    "stopped"  => "down",
    "failed"   => "broken",
    _          => "unknown"
}

match $result {
    Ok($v)    => echo "Success: $v",
    Err($e)   => echo "Failed: $e",
}
Functions
texttextfn is_low_battery() -> Bool {
    return @battery/level < 0.20
}

fn restart_if_failed($name: Text) -> Void {
    let $state = service $name status
    if $state == "failed" {
        service $name restart
    }
}

let $double = |$n| $n * 2
Control Flow
texttextif @battery/level < 0.20 {
    power profile power-saver
}

for $svc in services failed {
    service $svc restart
}

while @cpu/usage > 0.90 {
    time timer 10s
}
Error Handling
texttexttry {
    container start "web"
} catch Container.ImageNotFound($e) {
    container image pull $e.image
    container start "web"
} catch $e {
    echo "Failed: $e"
}

# ? operator propagates errors
fn deploy() -> Result<Text, Error> {
    vcs push ?
    container image build . --tag myapp ?
    return Ok("Done")
}

L3: Domain Commands
Naming Rules
Three levels. Not everything needs where:
texttextLEVEL 1 — Named views (daily filters are verbs)
  packages outdated                   NOT  packages where outdated
  containers running                  NOT  containers where state == running
  services failed                     NOT  services where failed

LEVEL 2 — Category flags
  disks --type ssd                    NOT  disks where type == ssd
  apps --type gui                     NOT  apps where type == gui
  keys --type symmetric               NOT  keys where type == symmetric

LEVEL 3 — where (actual data queries)
  processes where cpu > 50
  windows where workspace == 2
  packages where size > 100MB

L4: Intelligence
ask — query your system in natural language
texttextask "why is my battery draining fast"
#   Battery drain rate: 18.2W (normal: 12W)
#   Top consumers: Firefox video (+4.1W), BT audio (+0.8W), brightness (+3.1W)
#   Suggestion: Close tabs, reduce brightness to 60%
#   Estimated improvement: 4h 30m → 6h 15m

ask "what changed since yesterday"
#   Packages: 3 upgraded. Services: cups stopped. DNS changed. 4 commits.

ask "is my system secure"
#   ✓ Firewall active. ✓ Device locked. ✓ Packages up to date.
#   ⚠ SSH root login enabled. ⚠ Bluetooth discoverable.

ask "why is the internet slow"
#   DNS: ✓ 2ms. Gateway: ✓ 1ms. WiFi: ✓ 78%. Speed: 12 Mbps (expected 100).
#   Diagnosis: ISP congestion at hop 4.
suggest — proactive recommendations
texttextsuggest
#   ⚠ 12 packages outdated (3 security) → packages upgrade --security
#   ⚠ Battery threshold not set → battery charge-threshold 80

Node System
texttext# Context switch
@server                                → switch to server (all commands run there)
@local                                 → back to local
@                                      → shorthand for @local
@prod                                  → switch to label (runs across labeled nodes)

# Remote state
@server/cpu/usage                      → without switching
@phone/battery/level                   → without switching

# Node management
nodes / nodes online / nodes --type server / --type phone / --type iot
node "thinkpad" / info / capabilities
node "thinkpad" run "cpu usage"        → explicit remote (no context switch)
node "server" run "service nginx restart"

# Remote files
copy ~/file.txt @server:/tmp/file.txt
copy @server:/var/log/app.log ~/
sync ~/Projects/ @server:/Projects/ / sync --dry-run

# Remote events
watch @server/services failed
watch @phone/battery where < 0.20

# Labels for node sets
label node "server-1" "prod"
label node "server-2" "prod"
nodes --label "prod"                   → prod nodes
@prod                                  → switch context to prod
node --label "prod" run "health"       → run on all prod nodes

# Trust
node "unknown" trust / deny
nodes trust / nodes pending

This is the specification. Six layers. Every domain. Every method. Labels instead of groups. Named views instead of where for common filters. AI that actually helps. Guide mode for every domain. Error handling with recovery. Node system for cross-device operation. External commands just work. A shell that beats bash day 1 and doesn't exist for any particular century.

Thought for 69 secondsInteractive Mode — For Everyone

Philosophy
The CLI is for people who know what they want. Interactive mode is for people who want to find out. Same power. Different door.
texttext$ network --interactive

  A non-technical user can:
    → See all WiFi networks visually
    → Click one, type password, done
    → See their connection strength as a visual bar
    → Understand everything without knowing any command

  A power user can:
    → Same screen, same actions
    → But also: keyboard shortcuts, batch operations, search
    → Navigate 10x faster with keys than mouse
    → Every CLI action available through menus
Not a wizard. Not a tutorial. Not dumbed down. It's the same shell, rendered visually.

Accessibility
texttextVISUAL IMPAIRMENT:
  - Every element has screen reader label
  - Tab navigation follows logical reading order
  - Color is never the only indicator (always paired with symbol/text)
  - High contrast mode: theme high-contrast on
  - Large text mode: theme font-size 18

MOTOR IMPAIRMENT:
  - All actions reachable by keyboard
  - No time-limited interactions (except optional "auto-dismiss toasts")
  - Large click targets (minimum 3 lines per interactive row)
  - Sticky keys supported

COGNITIVE ACCESSIBILITY:
  - Simple, consistent language across all domains
  - Same layout pattern in every domain (header/tabs/content/footer)
  - Icons always paired with text labels
  - Destructive actions always require confirmation
  - Undo available for most actions
  - Progress indicators for all waiting states

NON-ENGLISH:
  - All labels translatable (locale-aware)
  - Icons provide meaning independent of language
  - Number formats locale-aware

Design Standards
Every interactive mode must:
texttextVISUAL:
  ✓ Use consistent color system (green/yellow/red/blue semantics)
  ✓ Show progress bars for all numeric values
  ✓ Show sparklines for all time-series data
  ✓ Use icons paired with text (never icon-only)
  ✓ Show loading state for all async operations
  ✓ Animate transitions between views
  ✓ Responsive to terminal size (min 80x24, works up to any size)

INTERACTION:
  ✓ Mouse: click, hover, scroll, drag, right-click all work
  ✓ Keyboard: all actions reachable without mouse
  ✓ Both work simultaneously (no mode switch)
  ✓ Context menu on right-click or 'a' key
  ✓ Search with '/' from any view
  ✓ Help with '?' from any view

INFORMATION:
  ✓ Every screen teaches something (not just shows data)
  ✓ Units always shown (%, MB, °C, dBm, Mbps)
  ✓ Relative time shown ("3h ago", "just now")
  ✓ Status always clear (●/○/✗ with color)
  ✓ Destructive actions always confirm
  ✓ Success feedback (toast) for all actions
  ✓ Error messages include recovery suggestions

ACCESSIBILITY:
  ✓ Screen reader compatible
  ✓ Color never sole indicator (always paired with symbol)
  ✓ High contrast mode available
  ✓ Large text mode available
  ✓ All keyboard navigable
  ✓ No time-limited interactions

INTELLIGENCE:
  ✓ '/' with natural language triggers AI search
  ✓ '?' shows contextual help including AI suggestions
  ✓ Forms validate input in real-time
  ✓ Smart recommendations (best algorithm, optimal settings)
  ✓ Natural language input where possible ("Backup photos nightly at 2am")

This is interactive mode. Every domain. Every user. Same power as the CLI, presented so anyone can use it. Not a wizard. Not a tutorial. The shell itself, rendered for humans who don't think in commands.

Thought for 56.6 secondsSmart Interactive — Design System

Philosophy
texttextContent eats chrome.
Color is structure.
Whitespace is breathing.
Indentation is hierarchy.
If it doesn't inform, remove it.
A terminal screen is a canvas of 200×50 cells. Every cell costs attention. Borders cost attention without adding information. Boxes frame emptiness. Lines separate where color already divides.
The rule: Before rendering any character, ask: does this help the user do what they came to do? If not, delete it.

Layout
texttext┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                      │
│  HEADER          1 line. Domain name. Context. Section selector.     │
│                                                                      │
│  ────────────    thin separator (optional, only if content changes   │
│                   meaning between header and body)                    │
│                                                                      │
│  BODY            everything else. Flows freely. Uses indentation     │
│                   and color for structure. No boxes.                  │
│                                                                      │
│  FOOTER          1 line. Key hints. Minimal.                         │
│                                                                      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Three zones. That's it. No sidebar panel. No status bar. No toolbar. No breadcrumbs. The entire screen is content with a one-line header and one-line footer.
Header
Single line. Three parts:
texttext  ╶╴ Services  ·  1:Running  2:Failed  3:All  4:Enabled ╶╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴
  ─┬─────────     ─┬──────────────────────────────────     ─┬──────────
   Domain name      Section selector (numbered keys)         Fill line
Domain name in boldSections as numbered keys separated by middle dotsActive section in accent color (or underline)Fill characters (╴) extend to edge of terminalNo box. No border. Just a decorative line under the text.
If there's important context (like a selected item), append it:
texttext  ╶╴ Services  ·  1:Running  2:Failed  3:All  ·  nginx ● ╶╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴╴
Body
Flows top to bottom. Uses these structural tools:
Blank line — separates major sections (like paragraphs)
Indentation — 2 spaces per level, shows hierarchy
Color — separates meaning without lines
Thin line — only when two adjacent sections could be confused:
texttext  ─────────────────────────────────────────────
That's it. No vertical lines. No boxes. No panels.
Footer
Single line. Keys shown as terse hints:
texttext  ↑↓ s S r l e d · / ? q
With labels only for ambiguous keys:
texttext  ↑↓ Navigate  s Start  S Stop  r Restart  l Logs  / Search  ? Help  q Quit
Show full labels when space permits. Show terse when terminal is narrow.

Components
Status Indicator
Always inline. Always paired with text. Never alone.
texttext  ● Running           green dot + text
  ○ Stopped           dim/gray dot + text
  ✗ Failed            red dot + text
  ◉ Enabled           filled blue dot + text
  ○ Disabled          dim/gray dot + text
  ⚠ Warning           yellow + text
  ✓ OK                green check + text
  ● Connected         green dot + text
  ○ Disconnected      dim dot + text
Color-blind safe: symbol always differs (●/○/✗/◉) not just color.
Progress Bar
No box characters. Use block elements directly:
texttext  CPU    ████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░  48%
  Disk   ████████████████████████░  92%      ← red at >90%
  Batt   ████████████████░░░░░░░░  68%      ← yellow when discharging
  Signal ████████████████████░░░░  78%      ← green when strong
Rules:24 blocks wide (adjusts to terminal width)█ for filled, ░ for emptyColor changes at thresholds: green > 60%, yellow 20-60%, red < 20%Exception: disk red at > 90%, battery red at < 15%Label left-aligned, percentage right-alignedNo extra spacing or padding. Line is:   Label  █████░░░  XX%
Compact variant (inline in tables):
texttext  ████████░░ 65%
Sparkline
Inline mini-chart. 20 characters wide:
texttext  CPU  ▁▂▃▅▇█▇▅▃▂▁▁▂▃▅▇▅▃▂▁▁▂▃▅  48%
Rules:20 charactersUses ▁▂▃▄▅▆▇█ (8 levels)Color: dim for low, normal for mid, accent for high peaksLabel + sparkline + current value on one line
Key-Value List
Aligned label-value pairs. No separator character. Just alignment:
texttext  State       ● Running
  PID         1205
  Memory      48 MB
  CPU         2.1%
  Uptime      14d 3h 42m
  Started     Jan 1, 2025 08:15
Rules:Labels left-aligned, 12 chars wide (adjusts to longest label)Values left-aligned after labels2-space gap minimum between label and valueValues colored by meaning (state gets status color, numbers get thresholds)
Table
No vertical lines. No box characters. Column alignment with spaces:
texttext  NAME          STATE      CPU     MEMORY   DESCRIPTION
  nginx         ● Running  2.1%    48 MB    Web Server
  postgresql    ● Running  5.4%    256 MB   Database
  redis         ✗ Failed   0.0%    0 MB     Redis Cache
  cups          ○ Stopped  —       —        Print Service
Rules:Header row: UPPERCASE, dim colorHeader underlined with space (not a line character) or just boldRows separated by nothing (just line breaks)Selected row: highlighted background (subtle, not bright)Hovered row (mouse): slightly lighter backgroundColumn widths auto-calculated from contentRight-align numbers, left-align text— for null/empty valuesStatus columns use status indicator symbols inline
Compact table variant (for tight spaces):
texttext  nginx       ●  2.1%  48M   Web Server
  postgresql  ●  5.4%  256M  Database
  redis       ✗  0.0%  0M    Redis Cache
Tree / Hierarchy
Uses indentation and tree characters:

Rules:▸ collapsed, ▾ expandedIndent by 2 spaces per levelChildren directly below parent, indentedSelected item: highlighted background
Section Title
Not a header in a box. Just a line:
texttext  Available networks
Or with a decorative dash suffix:
texttext  Available networks ─────────────────────────
Or just bold text on its own line, preceded by a blank line.
Rules:Bold or slightly brighter than body textPreceded by blank lineNot followed by a line (content starts directly below, indented or not)
Input Field
No box. Just a highlighted line:
texttext  Password  ••••••••••••••
Or with cursor:
texttext  Password  my-pass█
Rules:Label left, value rightActive field: accent color underline or backgroundPlaceholder text: dimPassword: bullet charactersNo border. Just the text.
Toggle
Inline, compact:
texttext  Dark Mode        ON ████░░░░░░ OFF
  Night Light      ON ░░░░░░░░░░ OFF
  Auto-connect     ✓
Or simpler:
texttext  Dark Mode     ● on
  Night Light   ○ off
Rules:Active state: colored, boldInactive state: dimClickable/toggleable with Enter or Space
Slider
For values with range:
texttext  Brightness  ◀ ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░ ▶  65%
Or more compact:
texttext  Brightness  ████████████████░░░░░░░░  65%  ←→
Rules:Arrow keys or mouse drag to adjustColor matches value (dim for low, bright for high)Value shown inline
Search
Activates with /. Inline at top of body:
texttext  Search  fire█

  firefox          app
  firewalld        service
  firewall rules   command
Rules:Appears at top of body when activatedReplaces current view with filtered resultsEsc closes search, returns to previous viewResults update as you type (live filter)No box. Just the label, input, and results below.
Confirmation
Only for destructive/irreversible actions. Full screen overlay.
texttext

          Delete container "redis" (a1b2c3)?

          This will remove all data and cannot be undone.

              [ Yes, delete ]          [ Cancel ]

Rules:Centered vertically and horizontallyMinimal text. One question, one consequence.Two options: destructive (red/accent) and cancel (dim)Enter confirms, Esc cancelsBackground dimmed (if terminal supports it)Only for: delete, destroy, force stop, wipe, revoke, remove with dataNever for: start, stop, restart, connect, enable, disable
Toast
Auto-dismiss notification. Bottom-right corner:
texttext                                              ╶ ✓ Connected to HomeNetwork
Or:
texttext                                              ✓ Connected
Rules:Appears bottom-rightAuto-dismisses after 3 secondsSuccess: green check, Warning: yellow, Error: redNo box. Just text with status symbol.Stacks if multiple (up to 3 visible)Click or any key dismisses
Loading
Inline, not a box:
texttext  Scanning  ◜ ◝ ◞ ◟
Or:
texttext  Connecting  ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░░░░  50%
Rules:Spinner for indefinite waitsProgress bar for known-duration waitsInline where the result will appearNo modal overlay unless blocking
Dialog (non-critical)
For input forms. Inline in the body, not a modal:
texttext  Connect to "CoffeeShop"

  Password  ••••••••••••••
  Auto-connect  ✓
  Band  Auto ○  2.4 ○  5 ○

  Enter Connect  Esc Cancel
Rules:Appears inline where you are (not a floating box)Fields stacked verticallyLabel on left, input on rightTab moves between fieldsEnter submits, Esc cancelsNo border. No frame. Just indented form fields.
Empty State
When there's nothing to show:
texttext  No services found.
Or with action:
texttext  No containers running.
  Create one: c
Rules:One or two linesDim textOptional action hintNo decorative art or illustrations

Color
Semantic Colors
texttext  SUCCESS     #22c55e   green        Running, connected, healthy, enabled, passed
  ERROR       #ef4444   red          Failed, disconnected, denied, expired, critical
  WARNING     #eab308   yellow       Degraded, expiring soon, attention needed
  INFO        #06b6d4   cyan         Informational, help text, hints
  ACCENT      #3b82f6   blue         Selection, active tab, links, focused item
  MUTED       #6b7280   gray         Secondary text, disabled, inactive, placeholders
  PRIMARY     #f0f0f0   white        Main text
  SURFACE     #1a1a1a   dark gray    Background
Usage Rules
texttext  Text hierarchy:
    Brightest    → current value, selected item
    Normal       → regular content
    Dim          → labels, headers, inactive items, empty states

  Selection:
    Background   → subtle accent bg (not bright, ~20% opacity)
    Text         → normal color (not white-on-blue, that's ugly)

  Hover (mouse):
    Background   → slightly lighter than surface
    No border change. No underline. Just bg shift.
Color-blind Safety
Never rely on color alone:Green = ● or ✓ symbolRed = ✗ symbolYellow = ⚠ symbolAlways paired with text label

Typography
Weight
texttext  Bold         → domain name in header, section titles, selected items
  Normal       → body content, table data
  Dim          → headers, labels, hints, empty states, footer
Alignment
texttext  Left         → text, labels, names
  Right        → numbers, percentages, sizes, dates in tables
  Center       → confirmation dialog text
Width
texttext  Labels       → fixed width per table (longest label + 2)
  Values       → natural width, right-padded to column width
  Full-width   → sparklines, progress bars, search results

Spacing
texttext  Between major sections     → 1 blank line
  Between minor items        → 0 blank lines (just line break)
  Before section title       → 1 blank line
  After section title        → 0 blank lines (content follows directly)
  Header to body             → 0 blank lines (body starts immediately)
  Body to footer             → 0 blank lines (footer is last line)
  Indentation per level      → 2 spaces
  Table column gap           → 2 spaces minimum
  Progress bar gap           → 2 spaces before value

Interaction
Keyboard
texttext  ↑/↓  j/k       Navigate items
  ←/→  h/l       Adjust sliders, switch sections
  Enter           Activate, confirm, open
  Esc             Back, cancel, close search
  Tab             Next field (in forms), next section
  Space           Toggle (checkboxes, play/pause)
  /               Search
  ?               Help
  q               Quit interactive mode
  1-9             Section by number
  a               Action menu (context actions)
  s S             Start / Stop
  r               Restart / Refresh
  l               Logs
  e               Enable / Edit / Exec
  d               Delete / Disable
  n               New / Next
  c               Create / Connect
  f               Favorite / Filter
  Home/End        First / Last item
  Page Up/Down    Scroll page
Keys are mnemonic: s for start, S (shift) for stop. l for logs. e for exec/enable. The footer shows available keys for current context.
Mouse
texttext  Hover           → highlight row/item (subtle bg change)
  Left click      → select, activate, toggle
  Right click     → context action menu (same as 'a' key)
  Scroll wheel    → scroll list
  Drag            → adjust sliders
No hover tooltips. Information is inline. If you need to know more, press Enter.
Both Simultaneously
Keyboard focus and mouse hover are independent. Keyboard user sees focus ring (highlighted row). Mouse user sees hover highlight. They can switch freely.

Confirmation Rules
Confirm (full-screen overlay):Delete with data loss (container remove --force, VM remove --disks)Revoke credentials or keysWipe data (factory reset, format disk)Force operations (force push, force kill)Security-critical changes (disable firewall, disable MFA)
Don't confirm:Start / stop / restart services or containersConnect / disconnect networks or BluetoothEnable / disable featuresCreate new itemsInstall / remove packages (show progress instead)View logs, stats, info
Undo instead of confirm:
When possible, do the action and offer undo:texttext  ✓ cups stopped                     Undo: u

Error Rules
Not in a box. Inline. One line:
texttext  ✗ Port 8080 already in use by 'web'
With recovery hint on next line:
texttext  ✗ Port 8080 already in use by 'web'
    Use --port 8081 or stop 'web' first
In interactive mode, errors appear inline where the action happened:
texttext  redis    ✗ Failed to start — port 6379 in use

Responsive
texttext  ≥ 120 cols    Full layout. Tables show all columns.
  80-119 cols   Reduced columns. Shorter labels.
  < 80 cols     Minimal columns. Compact mode. Stack instead of table.
Tables adapt: hide less-important columns when narrow. Progress bars shrink. Sparklines shorten.

  40+ box-drawing characters         4 decorative characters (header)
  6 levels of nesting                2 levels (header/body)
  Tabs with borders                  Numbered keys

  Details in frames                  Details as key-value list
  Buttons in panels                  Actions in footer keys
  ~50 lines of chrome                ~3 lines of chrome
  Looks like a cheap terminal app    Looks like content
That's the design system. Every interactive screen follows these rules. Every component is reusable. Every layout is the same structure: one-line header, free-flowing body, one-line footer. No frames, no boxes, no tabs, no decoration that doesn't inform.

Revised Design Rules
texttext  1. TABS     for switching between conceptual areas
  2. PANELS   for list+detail on wide screens
  3. PAGES    for drilling into items (list → detail → sub)
  4. TABLES   for structured data (header + separator + rows)
  5. TREES    for hierarchical data (expand/collapse)
  6. RULES    for separating major sections
  7. COLOR    for meaning (not decoration)
  8. INDENT   for hierarchy
  9. BREADCRUMB for navigation path
  10. FOOTER  for available actions
Hierarchy of visual tools (strongest to weakest):
texttext  Page change    →  strongest separation (different view)
  Panel split    →  strong separation (side by side)
  Tab switch     →  category change (same page, different content)
  Rule           →  section break within a view
  Blank line     →  paragraph break
  Indent         →  parent-child relationship
  Color          →  semantic meaning
  Weight         →  emphasis (bold/normal/dim)
Use the weakest tool that provides enough separation. Don't use a page change where a rule suffices. Don't use a panel where indentation suffices.

Component Summary
texttext  COMPONENT         USE WHEN                         BORDER
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Tab bar           Switching conceptual areas        Underline

  Search            Filtering content                  Inline at top
  Breadcrumb        Navigation path                    In header text
Each component has clear rules for when to use it and when not to. The design system is consistent across all domains but flexible enough to present each domain in its natural way. Tabs for navigation, tables for data, trees for hierarchy, panels for split views, pages for drill-down. Structure where it informs, whitespace where it breathes.

## Assistant

Thought for 15.1 secondsModern Terminal Design System

Terminal as Engine
Modern terminals aren't dumb text pipes. They're rendering engines with:
texttext  CAPABILITY              PROTOCOL / FEATURE
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  True color (24-bit)     RGB escape sequences
  Inline images           Kitty graphics / Sixel / iTerm2
  Styled text             Undercurl, overline, strikethrough, italic, dim
  Hyperlinks              OSC 8 (clickable links)
  System notifications    OSC 9 (desktop notifications)
  Scroll regions          DECSTBM (partial screen scroll)
  Alternate screen        smcup/rmcup (full-screen app)
  Mouse tracking          Full X10/Normal/SGR mouse protocol
  Keyboard protocol       Kitty keyboard (disambiguated keys)
  Focus events            Terminal focus in/out
  Cursor shaping          Beam, block, underline
  Bracketed paste         Safe paste mode
  Unicode                 Box drawing, block elements, braille, symbols, geometric
  Dynamic content         In-place updates, minimal flicker
  Window size queries     CSI 14 t / CSI 16 t (pixel size)
  Color scheme detection  OSC 11 query (dark/light detection)
  Synchronized output     Batched rendering (no flicker)
  Sixel                   Inline raster images (DEC terminals, foot, mlterm)
  Kitty graphics          Inline images with alpha (kitty, wezterm)
  Kitty keyboard          Disambiguated key events
  Kitty images            Unicode placeholders for images
Smart detects what the terminal supports and renders at the highest level available. Fallback gracefully.

Detection
bashbash# Smart queries terminal capabilities on startup
terminal                               → detected capabilities
terminal info                          → full report

#   Hyperlinks  OSC 8

# Fallback tiers:
#   TIER 1 (full)    Kitty/WezTerm/Alacritty 0.13+
#                    Images, true color, kitty keyboard, all features
#   TIER 2 (rich)    iTerm2/Tmux 3.4+/Foot/Contour
#                    True color, Sixel or iTerm images, mouse, Unicode
#   TIER 3 (basic)   Any modern terminal
#                    256 color, mouse, Unicode box drawing
#   TIER 4 (minimal) Old terminals, SSH to legacy systems
#                    16 color, basic ASCII fallback

Layout System — Fixed Regions
The screen is divided into fixed and scrollable regions. Fixed regions stay in place. Only the content area scrolls.
texttext  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  HEADER (fixed)                                           │
  │  1 line. Domain + tabs. Stays on top.                     │
  ├──────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │              │                                            │
  │  SIDEBAR     │  CONTENT (scrollable)                      │
  │  (fixed)     │  Tables, lists, trees, forms, detail.     │
  │              │  Only this region scrolls.                 │
  │  Navigation  │                                            │
  │  20-25 chars │                                            │
  │  wide        │                                            │
  │              │                                            │
  ├──────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  FOOTER (fixed)                                           │
  │  1 line. Key hints. Stays on bottom.                      │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
When to use sidebar
texttext  USE sidebar:
    Navigation between major sections (not tabs)
    Multi-level drill-down (photos → album → photo)
    Persistent context (email folders, note tags)
    Settings pages with many categories

  DON'T use sidebar:
    Dashboard views (health, battery)
    Single-purpose screens (audio mixer)
    Simple lists (services, containers)
    Narrow terminals (< 120 cols)

Scroll regions
Header and footer are painted once and stay. Only the content region is redrawn on scroll:
texttext  DECSTBM (Set Top and Bottom Margins):
    Top margin:    after header line
    Bottom margin: before footer line
    Content scrolls within these margins only
Cursor never enters header or footer during scroll. They're stable anchors.

Color System — True Color
Semantic palette
csscss  :root {
    --bg:              #0c0c0c;
    --bg-surface:      #161616;
    --bg-elevated:     #1e1e1e;
    --bg-highlight:    #2a2a3a;    /* selection, hover */
    --bg-active:       #1a2a4a;    /* focused item */

    --text:            #e8e8e8;
    --text-secondary:  #8a8a8a;
    --text-dim:        #555555;

    --accent:          #5b9bf5;    /* blue — selection, active, links */
    --accent-subtle:   #1a2a4a;    /* accent bg (20% opacity feel) */

    --success:         #4eca6b;    /* running, connected, healthy */
    --error:           #e55353;    /* failed, disconnected, critical */
    --warning:         #e5b94e;    /* degraded, expiring, attention */
    --info:            #4ec9e5;    /* informational, hints */
  }
Background gradients (subtle)
Modern terminals with true color can render subtle gradients for depth:
texttext  Header:    slightly lighter than bg (#161616 → #0c0c0c gradient)
  Sidebar:   slightly lighter than content area
  Footer:    same as header
  Selection: accent-subtle bg (#1a2a4a)
  Hover:     bg-highlight (#2a2a3a)
Not visible gradients. Subtle enough to feel like depth without being flashy.
Color in content
texttext  SUCCESS (#4eca6b):
    ● Running, ✓ OK, ✓ Healthy, ● Connected, ◉ Enabled, ✓ Passed

  ERROR (#e55353):
    ✗ Failed, ✗ Disconnected, ✗ Denied, ✗ Expired, ✗ Critical

  WARNING (#e5b94e):
    ⚠ Degraded, ⚠ Expiring soon, ⚠ Attention needed

  INFO (#4ec9e5):
    ℹ Informational, hints, help text

  ACCENT (#5b9bf5):
    Active tab, selected item, links, focused field

  SECONDARY (#8a8a8a):
    Labels, headers, column titles, inactive items

  DIM (#555555):
    Placeholders, disabled items, decorative elements, separators

Smart sends notifications through both the internal system and the terminal's OSC escape, so you get them even if you're looking at a different window.

Responsive Tiers
Full (≥ 140 cols, ≥ 40 rows)
texttext  - Sidebar + content panels
  - Inline images
  - Rich charts
  - All columns in tables
  - Mini-map on logs
  - Split detail panel
Standard (100-139 cols, 30-39 rows)
texttext  - Tabs instead of sidebar
  - Tables with all columns
  - Sparklines (not images)
  - Single-panel view (list → detail → back)
  - Progress bars (not gauges)
Compact (80-99 cols, 24-29 rows)
texttext  - Tabs, fewer visible
  - Tables drop less-important columns
  - Sparklines shorten (10 chars)
  - No sidebars
  - Shorter labels
  - Footer shows terse key hints
Minimal (< 80 cols)
texttext  - No tabs, use `:` commands
  - Lists instead of tables
  - No sparklines
  - Abbreviated everything
  - Stack everything vertically

Design Rules — Complete
texttext  STRUCTURE
  ─────────
  1. Fixed header (1 line) + fixed footer (1 line) + scrollable body
  2. Optional sidebar (≥140 cols) for navigation-heavy domains
  3. Tabs for category switching within a domain
  4. Panels for list + detail (≥100 cols)
  5. Pages for drill-down (list → detail → sub-detail)
  6. Breadcrumb in header shows navigation path
  7. Scrollbar on right edge when content overflows

  VISUAL
  ──────
  8.  Tables: UPPERCASE header, thin separator ─, no vertical lines
  9.  Trees: ▸ ▾ with indentation, no box
  10. Rules: thin ─ between major sections
  11. Panels: thin │ separator, accent color
  12. Color: semantic (green/red/yellow/blue), never decorative
  13. Weight: bold = important, dim = secondary, italic = help
  14. True color for subtle depth (backgrounds, gradients)
  15. Undercurl for errors, double underline for security warnings
  16. Inline images where they inform (photos, diagrams)
  17. Sparklines for time-series, charts where images supported
  18. Progress bars with █░ characters
  19. Status indicators always paired with text: ● Running

  INTERACTION
  ───────────
  20. Keyboard + mouse work simultaneously
  21. Command palette: Ctrl+P or :
  22. Search: / (fuzzy, highlighted results)
  23. Context actions: a or right-click
  24. Drill-down: Enter or right arrow
  25. Back: Esc or left arrow
  26. Sections: number keys
  27. Hyperlinks: any URL/path/email/command clickable
  28. Desktop notifications via OSC 9 when terminal unfocused

  RESPONSIVE
  ──────────
  29. ≥140 cols: sidebar + panels + images + charts
  30. 100-139: tabs + panels + sparklines
  31. 80-99: tabs + single view + compact tables
  32. <80: commands only, stacked layout

  ANIMATION
  ─────────
  33. Spinners for indefinite waits (braille ⠋⠙⠹⠸⠼⠴⠦⠧⠇⠏)
  34. Value flash (bold 200ms) when live data changes
  35. Dim-bright transition (100ms) on page change
  36. No animation for animation's sake

  CONFIRMATION
  ────────────
  37. Only for: delete+data loss, force operations, security-critical
  38. Dialog: centered, rounded corners, dim background
  39. Otherwise: do the action, offer undo (toast with undo key)

  CAPABILITY DETECTION
  ────────────────────
  40. Detect terminal on startup (kitty/iterm/sixel/basic)
  41. Render at highest tier available
  42. Graceful fallback for every feature
  43. Never break on unknown terminal

Icon Rules
texttext  PLACEMENT
  ─────────
  1. Header:     1 icon before domain name
  2. Sidebar:    1 icon before item name
  3. Tables:     1 icon before item name (first column) or status icons
  4. Status:     Icon replaces or precedes ●/○/✗ symbol
  5. Actions:    Icon in action menus, not in footer key hints
  6. Dashboard:  1 icon before domain summary line
  7. Checklist:  2 icons (check + domain) per line
  8. Breadcrumb: Icon before each segment

  SIZING
  ──────
  9.  Each icon = 1 character width + 1 space
  10. Icons never replace text (always paired)
  11. Icons align vertically in columns

  COLOR
  ─────
  12. Domain icon: accent color
  13. Status icon: status color (green/red/yellow)
  14. File type icon: file-type color or secondary
  15. Action icon: secondary color
  16. Navigation icon: dim color

  FALLBACK
  ────────
  17. If Nerd Font detected: use Nerd Font glyphs
  18. If not detected: fall back to Unicode symbols
  19. If Unicode fails: fall back to ASCII text
  20. Never display broken glyphs (▯ □)
  21. Detection happens once at startup
  22. Fallback set is consistent (all icons switch together)text  PLACEMENT
